name: End-to-End Goal-Driven Web Navigation
summary: Introduces WebNav for converting websites into goal-directed hyperlink navigation tasks and WikiNav for evaluating language-conditioned navigation and question answering on Wikipedia.
authors: Rodrigo Nogueira; Kyunghyun Cho

name: Reinforcement Learning on Web Interfaces Using Workflow-Guided Exploration
summary: Uses workflows extracted from demonstrations to constrain reinforcement-learning exploration for interactive web tasks.
authors: Evan Zheran Liu; Kelvin Guu; Panupong Pasupat; Tianlin Shi; Percy Liang

name: Mapping Natural Language Commands to Web Elements
summary: Defines language grounding on webpages as choosing the UI element targeted by a natural-language command. A collection of more than 50,000 commands and three baseline models study functional references, relationships between elements, and visual position cues.
authors: Panupong Pasupat; Tian-Shun Jiang; Evan Zheran Liu; Kelvin Guu; Percy Liang

name: Learning to Navigate the Web
summary: Introduces guided RL for QWeb, using a curriculum of smaller instructions and generated tasks to train an agent that follows instructions and fills forms on web pages.
authors: Izzeddin Gur; Ulrich Rueckert; Aleksandra Faust; Dilek Hakkani-Tur

name: A Systematic Literature Review of Automated Techniques for Functional GUI Testing of Mobile Applications
summary: Surveys automated functional GUI testing techniques for mobile apps, comparing the effectiveness, efficiency and practicality of approaches reported in 25 studies.
authors: Yauhen Leanidavich Arnatovich; Lipo Wang

name: DOM-Q-NET: Grounded RL on Structured Language
summary: Introduces DOM-Q-NET, an RL architecture for web navigation that represents HTML as a tree and uses separate Q-function networks for clicking elements and typing text.
authors: Sheng Jia; Jamie Kiros; Jimmy Ba

name: Interactive Task and Concept Learning from Natural Language Instructions and GUI Demonstrations
summary: Introduces PUMICE, an agent that learns mobile-app procedures and conditional concepts through natural-language conversation and GUI demonstrations, recursively resolving ambiguous instructions with users.
authors: Toby Jia-Jun Li; Marissa Radensky; Justin Jia; Kirielle Singarajah; Tom M. Mitchell; Brad A. Myers

name: Mapping Natural Language Instructions to Mobile UI Action Sequences
summary: Introduces PIXELHELP for predicting mobile UI action sequences from instructions, together with action-phrase annotations and synthetic UI action descriptions for training. Separate Transformers extract instruction steps and ground object descriptions using interface content and screen position.
authors: Yang Li; Jiacong He; Xin Zhou; Yuan Zhang; Jason Baldridge
venue: Proceedings of the 58th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

name: From Robotic Process Automation to Intelligent Process Automation: Emerging Trends
summary: A survey of robotic and intelligent process automation traces the use of machine learning and AI in business workflows and identifies open research challenges.
authors: Tathagata Chakraborti; Vatche Isahagian; Rania Khalaf; Yasaman Khazaeni; Vinod Muthusamy; Yara Rizk; Merve Unuvar
venue: Lecture Notes in Business Information Processing

name: Object Detection for Graphical User Interface: Old Fashioned or Deep Learning or a Combination?
summary: Compares seven traditional and learned GUI element detectors on more than 50,000 interface images. The analysis motivates a coarse-to-fine non-text detector combined with a learned text detector to address GUI-specific localization requirements.
authors: Jieshan Chen; Mulong Xie; Zhenchang Xing; Chunyang Chen; Xiwei Xu; Liming Zhu; Guoqiang Li

name: Widget Captioning: Generating Natural Language Description for Mobile User Interface Elements
summary: Introduces crowdsourced descriptions of mobile UI elements and studies multimodal models that generate useful widget captions.
authors: Yang Li; Gang Li; Luheng He; Jingjie Zheng; Hong Li; Zhiwei Guan
venue: Proceedings of the 2020 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing (EMNLP)

name: ActionBert: Leveraging User Actions for Semantic Understanding of User Interfaces
summary: Pretrains ActionBert on user interaction traces to combine visual, linguistic, and UI-structure features. It evaluates the resulting UI representations on tasks including icon classification and description-based component retrieval.
authors: Zecheng He; Srinivas Sunkara; Xiaoxue Zang; Ying Xu; Lijuan Liu; Nevan Wichers; Gabriel Schubiner; Ruby Lee; Jindong Chen; Blaise Agüera y Arcas

name: Screen Recognition: Creating Accessibility Metadata for Mobile Applications from Pixels
summary: Infers UI elements and accessibility metadata from mobile screenshots to support screen-reader interaction with iOS applications.
authors: Xiaoyi Zhang; Lilian de Greef; Amanda Swearngin; Samuel White; Kyle Murray; Lisa Yu; Qi Shan; Jeffrey Nichols; Jason Wu; Chris Fleizach; Aaron Everitt; Jeffrey P. Bigham

name: WebSRC: A Dataset for Web-Based Structural Reading Comprehension
summary: Introduces question answering over webpage text and structure, with aligned HTML, screenshots, and metadata for structural reading comprehension.
authors: Xingyu Chen; Zihan Zhao; Lu Chen; Danyang Zhang; Jiabao Ji; Ao Luo; Yuxuan Xiong; Kai Yu

name: Grounding Open-Domain Instructions to Automate Web Support Tasks
summary: Introduces RUSS, which translates support instructions into a domain-specific language and grounds them in actionable web elements.
authors: Nancy Xu; Sam Masling; Michael Du; Giovanni Campagna; Larry Heck; James Landay; Monica S Lam

name: Mobile App Tasks with Iterative Feedback (MoTIF): Addressing Task Feasibility in Interactive Visual Environments
summary: Introduces MoTIF, a dataset of natural-language requests for interactive mobile apps, including infeasible requests and follow-up questions for studying task feasibility.
authors: Andrea Burns; Deniz Arsan; Sanjna Agrawal; Ranjitha Kumar; Kate Saenko; Bryan A. Plummer

name: Understanding Mobile GUI: from Pixel-Words to Screen-Sentences
summary: Models mobile screens as atomic text and graphic components whose relationships are learned by a Screen Transformer. The work introduces RICO-PW annotations and evaluates metadata-free screen understanding on relation, clickability, retrieval, and app-classification tasks.
authors: Jingwen Fu; Xiaoyi Zhang; Yuwang Wang; Wenjun Zeng; Sam Yang; Grayson Hilliard

name: AndroidEnv: A Reinforcement Learning Platform for Android
summary: Presents an Android environment for training and evaluating reinforcement-learning agents through touchscreen interaction.
authors: Daniel Toyama; Philippe Hamel; Anita Gergely; Gheorghe Comanici; Amelia Glaese; Zafarali Ahmed; Tyler Jackson; Shibl Mourad; Doina Precup

name: AppBuddy: Learning to Accomplish Tasks in Mobile Apps via Reinforcement Learning
summary: Introduces AppBuddy, an RL training platform and task suite for mobile apps where agents use on-screen element states and tap or type to complete multi-step tasks.
authors: Maayan Shvo; Zhiming Hu; Rodrigo Toro Icarte; Iqbal Mohomed; Allan Jepson; Sheila A. McIlraith

name: UIBert: Learning Generic Multimodal Representations for UI Understanding
summary: Learns shared image, text, and structural UI representations through self-supervised tasks based on relationships among interface components.
authors: Chongyang Bai; Xiaoxue Zang; Ying Xu; Srinivas Sunkara; Abhinav Rastogi; Jindong Chen; Blaise Aguera y Arcas

name: Screen2Words: Automatic Mobile UI Summarization with Multimodal Learning
summary: Studies mobile-screen summarization using visual, textual, and structural UI information, with a dataset of human-written descriptions.
authors: Bryan Wang; Gang Li; Xin Zhou; Zhourong Chen; Tovi Grossman; Yang Li

name: VUT: Versatile UI Transformer for Multi-Modal Multi-Task User Interface Modeling
summary: The Versatile UI Transformer jointly models interface screenshots, structure, and language for five UI tasks. Its encoder supports element detection when structural metadata is absent, while an autoregressive component handles UI question answering and command grounding.
authors: Yang Li; Gang Li; Xin Zhou; Mostafa Dehghani; Alexey Gritsenko

name: WebGPT: Browser-assisted question-answering with human feedback
summary: Trains a question-answering model to search and navigate a text-based web browser, collect references and improve long-form answers using demonstrations and human feedback.
authors: Reiichiro Nakano; Jacob Hilton; Suchir Balaji; Jeff Wu; Long Ouyang; Christina Kim; Christopher Hesse; Shantanu Jain; Vineet Kosaraju; William Saunders; Xu Jiang; Karl Cobbe; Tyna Eloundou; Gretchen Krueger; Kevin Button; Matthew Knight; Benjamin Chess; John Schulman

name: Learning to Denoise Raw Mobile UI Layouts for Improving Datasets at Scale
summary: Introduces CLAY, a pipeline that repairs noisy mobile UI layouts by removing nodes without valid visual counterparts and assigning semantic element types, supported by human-annotated layouts for evaluation.
authors: Gang Li; Gilles Baechler; Manuel Tragut; Yang Li

name: A Dataset for Interactive Vision-Language Navigation with Unknown Command Feasibility
summary: Introduces MoTIF mobile-app interactions with feasible and infeasible commands, feasibility explanations, and follow-up questions for ambiguous requests.
authors: Andrea Burns; Deniz Arsan; Sanjna Agrawal; Ranjitha Kumar; Kate Saenko; Bryan A. Plummer

name: A data-driven approach for learning to control computers
summary: Combines reinforcement learning with behavioral priors from human interactions to learn computer control through keyboard and mouse actions.
authors: Peter C Humphreys; David Raposo; Toby Pohlen; Gregory Thornton; Rachita Chhaparia; Alistair Muldal; Josh Abramson; Petko Georgiev; Alex Goldin; Adam Santoro; Timothy Lillicrap
venue: Proceedings of the 39th International Conference on Machine Learning

name: META-GUI: Towards Multi-modal Conversational Agents on Mobile GUI
summary: Introduces GUI-based task-oriented dialogue and a dataset pairing mobile-interface operations with conversational responses.
authors: Liangtai Sun; Xingyu Chen; Lu Chen; Tianle Dai; Zichen Zhu; Kai Yu

name: WebShop: Towards Scalable Real-World Web Interaction with Grounded Language Agents
summary: Provides a simulated shopping environment where language agents search, configure, and select products from natural-language requirements.
authors: Shunyu Yao; Howard Chen; John Yang; Karthik Narasimhan

name: CORNET: Learning Table Formatting Rules By Example
summary: Introduces CORNET, a system that learns spreadsheet conditional-formatting rules from cells formatted by users, using symbolic rule enumeration and a neural ranker.
authors: Mukul Singh; José Cambronero; Sumit Gulwani; Vu Le; Carina Negreanu; Mohammad Raza; Gust Verbruggen

name: ScreenQA: Large-Scale Question-Answer Pairs over Mobile App Screenshots
summary: Introduces screenshot question answering over mobile interfaces, linking answers to screen content and bounding boxes.
authors: Yu-Chung Hsiao; Fedir Zubach; Gilles Baechler; Srinivas Sunkara; Victor Carbune; Jason Lin; Maria Wang; Yun Zhu; Jindong Chen

name: Enabling Conversational Interaction with Mobile UI using Large Language Models
summary: Studies few-shot prompting of a single language model for four mobile-UI interaction tasks, aiming to support conversational interface use without a separate trained model for each task.
authors: Bryan Wang; Gang Li; Yang Li

name: Spotlight: Mobile UI Understanding using Vision-Language Models with a Focus
summary: Introduces Spotlight, a vision-language model conditioned on a UI screenshot and a selected region of interest. It evaluates screenshot-based mobile UI understanding and explores multitask learning and few-shot prompting.
authors: Gang Li; Yang Li

name: MUG: Interactive Multimodal Grounding on User Interfaces
summary: Studies iterative UI grounding in which users refine or correct an agent's interpretation over multiple conversational turns.
authors: Tao Li; Gang Li; Jingjie Zheng; Purple Wang; Yang Li

name: Towards Better Semantic Understanding of Mobile Interfaces
summary: Augments RICO screens and view hierarchies with human labels for icon shape and meaning and for links between UI elements and text labels. It compares image-only and multimodal models on semantic understanding of previously unseen apps.
authors: Srinivas Sunkara; Maria Wang; Lijuan Liu; Gilles Baechler; Yu-Chung Hsiao; Jindong; Chen; Abhanshu Sharma; James Stout

name: Pix2Struct: Screenshot Parsing as Pretraining for Visual Language Understanding
summary: Pix2Struct pretrains an image-to-text model by reconstructing simplified HTML from masked webpage screenshots. Its variable-resolution visual representation is evaluated across several domains, including user-interface understanding.
authors: Kenton Lee; Mandar Joshi; Iulia Turc; Hexiang Hu; Fangyu Liu; Julian Eisenschlos; Urvashi Khandelwal; Peter Shaw; Ming-Wei Chang; Kristina Toutanova

name: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
summary: Introduces ReAct, a method that interleaves reasoning traces and actions for language-model agents; WebShop is one of its interactive decision-making evaluations.
authors: Shunyu Yao; Jeffrey Zhao; Dian Yu; Nan Du; Izhak Shafran; Karthik Narasimhan; Yuan Cao

name: Understanding HTML with Large Language Models
summary: Studies language models for HTML element classification, page description and autonomous web navigation. Fine-tuned models are evaluated on MiniWoB, and a distilled, automatically labeled CommonCrawl HTML corpus supports the training approach.
authors: Izzeddin Gur; Ofir Nachum; Yingjie Miao; Mustafa Safdari; Austin Huang; Aakanksha Chowdhery; Sharan Narang; Noah Fiedel; Aleksandra Faust

name: UGIF: UI Grounded Instruction Following
summary: Introduces multilingual smartphone instruction-following data and a pipeline that retrieves help instructions and maps them to UI actions.
authors: Sagar Gubbi Venkatesh; Partha Talukdar; Srini Narayanan
venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: NAACL 2024

name: Fill in the Blank: Context-aware Automated Text Input Generation for Mobile GUI Testing
summary: Introduces QTypist, an LLM-based method that generates text inputs from mobile GUI context and integrates with automated testing tools to help them reach further app pages.
authors: Zhe Liu; Chunyang Chen; Junjie Wang; Xing Che; Yuekai Huang; Jun Hu; Qing Wang

name: Lexi: Self-Supervised Learning of the UI Language
summary: Introduces Lexi and UICaption to learn UI image-text representations from descriptions of interface functionality. Evaluation covers UI action entailment, instruction-based retrieval, referring-expression grounding, and UI entity recognition.
authors: Pratyay Banerjee; Shweti Mahajan; Kushal Arora; Chitta Baral; Oriana Riva

name: WebUI: A Dataset for Enhancing Visual UI Understanding with Web Semantics
summary: Collects rendered webpages and structural metadata for visual UI modeling, studying how web semantics transfer to interface-understanding tasks.
authors: Jason Wu; Siyan Wang; Siman Shen; Yi-Hao Peng; Jeffrey Nichols; Jeffrey P. Bigham

name: FLAME: A small language model for spreadsheet formulas
summary: Introduces FLAME, a model trained on Excel formulas for spreadsheet formula repair, completion and retrieval, supporting formula authoring in spreadsheet software.
authors: Harshit Joshi; Abishai Ebenezer; José Cambronero; Sumit Gulwani; Aditya Kanade; Vu Le; Ivan Radiček; Gust Verbruggen

name: Language Models can Solve Computer Tasks
summary: Introduces recursive criticism and improvement prompting for language-model agents performing computer tasks, evaluated on MiniWoB++ with a small number of demonstrations per task.
authors: Geunwoo Kim; Pierre Baldi; Stephen McAleer

name: DroidBot-GPT: GPT-powered UI Automation for Android
summary: Transforms Android UI states and available actions into language prompts for an LLM to choose and execute task steps.
authors: Hao Wen; Hongming Wang; Jiaxuan Liu; Yuanchun Li

name: Mobile-Env: Building Qualified Evaluation Benchmarks for LLM-GUI Interaction
summary: Provides an Android benchmark toolkit with controlled environments, intermediate feedback, and task sets for reproducible GUI-agent evaluation.
authors: Danyang Zhang; Zhennan Shen; Rui Xie; Situo Zhang; Tianbao Xie; Zihan Zhao; Siyuan Chen; Lu Chen; Hongshen Xu; Ruisheng Cao; Kai Yu

name: Mobile User Interface Element Detection Via Adaptively Prompt Tuning
summary: Introduces MUI-zh and APT for detecting mobile UI elements, combining visual features with OCR descriptions to adjust category prompts in CLIP-based detectors.
authors: Zhangxuan Gu; Zhuoer Xu; Haoxing Chen; Jun Lan; Changhua Meng; Weiqiang Wang

name: Multimodal Web Navigation with Instruction-Finetuned Foundation Models
summary: Trains WebGUM offline from demonstrations by jointly tuning an instruction-following language model and a vision encoder over webpage screenshots and HTML. The agent predicts browser actions and is evaluated on MiniWoB, WebShop, and Mind2Web.
authors: Hiroki Furuta; Kuang-Huei Lee; Ofir Nachum; Yutaka Matsuo; Aleksandra Faust; Shixiang Shane Gu; Izzeddin Gur
venue: International Conference on Learning Representations

name: Hierarchical Prompting Assists Large Language Model on Web Navigation
summary: Separates web navigation prompting into a SUMMARIZER that extracts action-relevant observations and an ACTOR that chooses the next action from the condensed context.
authors: Abishek Sridhar; Robert Lo; Frank F. Xu; Hao Zhu; Shuyan Zhou

name: AdaPlanner: Adaptive Planning from Feedback with Language Models
summary: Introduces AdaPlanner, which revises code-structured plans in response to environmental feedback and reuses successful plans as exemplars. Experiments include MiniWoB++ web tasks alongside ALFWorld.
authors: Haotian Sun; Yuchen Zhuang; Lingkai Kong; Bo Dai; Chao Zhang

name: SheetCopilot: Bringing Software Productivity to the Next Level through Large Language Models
summary: Introduces SheetCopilot, an agent that steers spreadsheet software via atomic virtual APIs, along with a 221-task spreadsheet manipulation benchmark.
authors: Hongxin Li; Jingran Su; Yuntao Chen; Qing Li; Zhaoxiang Zhang

name: From Pixels to UI Actions: Learning to Follow Instructions via Graphical User Interfaces
summary: Studies instruction-following agents that observe screenshots and act through a generic mouse-and-keyboard action space, evaluating pixel-based pretraining for GUI tasks on MiniWoB++.
authors: Peter Shaw; Mandar Joshi; James Cohan; Jonathan Berant; Panupong Pasupat; Hexiang Hu; Urvashi Khandelwal; Kenton Lee; Kristina Toutanova
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems

name: Responsible Task Automation: Empowering Large Language Models as Responsible Task Automators
summary: Presents ResponsibleTA, a coordinator-executor framework that checks command feasibility and task completion while using local memory for privacy-related controls. The paper compares prompted and learned implementations and evaluates them on UI task automation.
authors: Zhizheng Zhang; Xiaoyi Zhang; Wenxuan Xie; Yan Lu

name: Prompting Is All You Need: Automated Android Bug Replay with Large Language Models
summary: Introduces AdbGPT, a prompting-based approach that uses LLMs to replay app bugs from written reports, applying few-shot examples and reasoning without model training.
authors: Sidong Feng; Chunyang Chen

name: Mind2Web: Towards a Generalist Agent for the Web
summary: Introduces a web-task dataset spanning diverse websites and evaluates generalization to unseen sites and domains.
authors: Xiang Deng; Yu Gu; Boyuan Zheng; Shijie Chen; Samuel Stevens; Boshi Wang; Huan Sun; Yu Su

name: Synapse: Trajectory-as-Exemplar Prompting with Memory for Computer Control
summary: Synapse filters task-irrelevant page state and places complete abstracted state-action trajectories into the prompt. An embedding-based exemplar memory retrieves relevant demonstrations for new tasks, evaluated on MiniWoB++ and Mind2Web.
authors: Longtao Zheng; Rundong Wang; Xinrun Wang; Bo An

name: Android in the Wild: A Large-Scale Dataset for Android Device Control
summary: Collects Android interaction demonstrations with screens, actions, and instructions across device and platform variations for robustness evaluation.
authors: Christopher Rawles; Alice Li; Daniel Rodriguez; Oriana Riva; Timothy Lillicrap
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems

name: A Real-World WebAgent with Planning, Long Context Understanding, and Program Synthesis
summary: Combines task decomposition, HTML summarization, and generated Python programs to carry out instructions on websites.
authors: Izzeddin Gur; Hiroki Furuta; Austin Huang; Mustafa Safdari; Yutaka Matsuo; Douglas Eck; Aleksandra Faust

name: WebArena: A Realistic Web Environment for Building Autonomous Agents
summary: Introduces reproducible web environments with task-completion checks for evaluating autonomous web agents.
authors: Shuyan Zhou; Frank F. Xu; Hao Zhu; Xuhui Zhou; Robert Lo; Abishek Sridhar; Xianyi Cheng; Tianyue Ou; Yonatan Bisk; Daniel Fried; Uri Alon; Graham Neubig

name: AgentBench: Evaluating LLMs as Agents
summary: Evaluates language agents across eight interactive environments and analyzes failures in reasoning, decisions, and instruction following.
authors: Xiao Liu; Hao Yu; Hanchen Zhang; Yifan Xu; Xuanyu Lei; Hanyu Lai; Yu Gu; Hangliang Ding; Kaiwen Men; Kejuan Yang; Shudan Zhang; Xiang Deng; Aohan Zeng; Zhengxiao Du; Chenhui Zhang; Sheng Shen; Tianjun Zhang; Yu Su; Huan Sun; Minlie Huang; Yuxiao Dong; Jie Tang

name: Unveiling the Tricks: Automated Detection of Dark Patterns in Mobile Applications
summary: Introduces UIGuard, a system that examines mobile UI visuals and text to detect dark patterns, together with a labeled dataset of benign and malicious interfaces.
authors: Jieshan Chen; Jiamou Sun; Sidong Feng; Zhenchang Xing; Qinghua Lu; Xiwei Xu; Chunyang Chen

name: AutoDroid: LLM-powered Task Automation in Android
summary: Combines language-model reasoning with app analysis, UI representations, and exploration-derived memory for Android task automation.
authors: Hao Wen; Yuanchun Li; Guohong Liu; Shanhui Zhao; Tao Yu; Toby Jia-Jun Li; Shiqi Jiang; Yunhao Liu; Yaqin Zhang; Yunxin Liu

name: LASER: LLM Agent with State-Space Exploration for Web Navigation
summary: LASER represents web navigation as exploration over a defined set of states, allowing an agent to revisit earlier states after mistakes. The study evaluates this backtracking approach on WebShop and Amazon tasks.
authors: Kaixin Ma; Hongming Zhang; Hongwei Wang; Xiaoman Pan; Wenhao Yu; Dong Yu

name: You Only Look at Screens: Multimodal Chain-of-Action Agents
summary: Introduces Auto-GUI, a screenshot-based agent using previous actions and future action plans to guide device interaction.
authors: Zhuosheng Zhang; Aston Zhang
venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: ACL 2024

name: AXNav: Replaying Accessibility Tests from Natural Language
summary: Introduces an LLM and pixel-based UI system that executes natural-language accessibility tests, records navigable videos and flags potential interface issues.
authors: Maryam Taeb; Amanda Swearngin; Eldon Schoop; Ruijia Cheng; Yue Jiang; Jeffrey Nichols

name: SteP: Stacked LLM Policies for Web Actions
summary: SteP dynamically composes specialized web-action policies through a stack that records the active chain of policy calls. It studies this control structure across WebArena, MiniWoB++, and CRM workflows.
authors: Paloma Sodhi; S. R. K. Branavan; Yoav Artzi; Ryan McDonald

name: Reinforced UI Instruction Grounding: Towards a Generic UI Task Automation API
summary: Trains a screenshot-based instruction-grounding model to predict target coordinates, using reinforcement learning to improve spatial decoding.
authors: Zhizheng Zhang; Wenxuan Xie; Xiaoyi Zhang; Yan Lu

name: ILuvUI: Instruction-tuned LangUage-Vision modeling of UIs from Machine Conversations
summary: ILuvUI generates 335,000 conversational training examples paired with UI screenshots, covering questions, descriptions, and plans. The resulting vision-language model is assessed on element detection, response quality, and examples of multi-step UI navigation.
authors: Yue Jiang; Eldon Schoop; Amanda Swearngin; Jeffrey Nichols

name: UReader: Universal OCR-free Visually-situated Language Understanding with Multimodal Large Language Model
summary: Introduces UReader, which combines unified instruction tuning, auxiliary text-reading tasks and shape-adaptive image crops for OCR-free visual language understanding. Its evaluation includes webpage screenshots alongside documents, tables, charts and natural images.
authors: Jiabo Ye; Anwen Hu; Haiyang Xu; Qinghao Ye; Ming Yan; Guohai Xu; Chenliang Li; Junfeng Tian; Qi Qian; Ji Zhang; Qin Jin; Liang He; Xin Alex Lin; Fei Huang

name: CrashTranslator: Automatically Reproducing Mobile Application Crashes Directly from Stack Trace
summary: Introduces CrashTranslator, which predicts GUI exploration steps from stack traces with an LLM and uses RL-guided search to reproduce crashes in Android apps.
authors: Yuchao Huang; Junjie Wang; Zhe Liu; Yawen Wang; Song Wang; Chunyang Chen; Yuanzhe Hu; Qing Wang

name: A Zero-Shot Language Agent for Computer Control with Structured Reflection
summary: Studies a zero-shot computer-control agent that plans executable actions and organizes its own reflections after mistakes. MiniWoB++ experiments examine learning to complete tasks without supplied expert trajectories.
authors: Tao Li; Gang Li; Zhiwei Deng; Bryan Wang; Yang Li

name: OpenAgents: An Open Platform for Language Agents in the Wild
summary: OpenAgents hosts three language agents, for data analysis, API plugins and autonomous web browsing, behind a web interface for non-expert users, with local deployment for developers.
authors: Tianbao Xie; Fan Zhou; Zhoujun Cheng; Peng Shi; Luoxuan Weng; Yitao Liu; Toh Jing Hua; Junning Zhao; Qian Liu; Che Liu; Leo Z. Liu; Yiheng Xu; Hongjin Su; Dongchan Shin; Caiming Xiong; Tao Yu

name: Set-of-Mark Prompting Unleashes Extraordinary Visual Grounding in GPT-4V
summary: Overlays labeled image regions to help multimodal models refer to and reason about visual targets; a general visual-prompting method relevant to GUI grounding.
authors: Jianwei Yang; Hao Zhang; Feng Li; Xueyan Zou; Chunyuan Li; Jianfeng Gao

name: Vision-Based Mobile App GUI Testing: A Survey
summary: Surveys vision-based mobile app GUI testing across test generation, record-and-replay and testing frameworks, drawing on 271 papers including 92 vision-based studies.
authors: Shengcheng Yu; Chunrong Fang; Ziyuan Tuo; Quanjun Zhang; Chunyang Chen; Zhenyu Chen; Zhendong Su

name: InstructExcel: A Benchmark for Natural Language Instruction in Excel
summary: Introduces InstructExcel, a benchmark for generating Excel OfficeScripts from natural-language requests, built using scripts recorded from user actions and a collection of existing spreadsheets.
authors: Justin Payan; Swaroop Mishra; Mukul Singh; Carina Negreanu; Christian Poelitz; Chitta Baral; Subhro Roy; Rasika Chakravarthy; Benjamin Van Durme; Elnaz Nouri

name: Make LLM a Testing Expert: Bringing Human-like Interaction to Mobile GUI Testing via Functionality-aware Decisions
summary: Introduces GPTDroid for mobile GUI testing: it feeds app page information to an LLM, runs generated test scripts and uses feedback and memory to guide further exploration.
authors: Zhe Liu; Chunyang Chen; Junjie Wang; Mengzhuo Chen; Boyu Wu; Xing Che; Dandan Wang; Qing Wang

name: WebWISE: Web Interface Control and Sequential Exploration with Large Language Models
summary: WebWISE filters DOM elements into observations and generates short programs for click, scroll, and text-entry steps. It evaluates in-context learning from either one supplied example or an example collected during a successful zero-shot MiniWoB++ trial.
authors: Heyi Tao; Sethuraman T; Michal Shlapentokh-Rothman; Derek Hoiem

name: AllTogether: Investigating the Efficacy of Spliced Prompt for Web Navigation using Large Language Models
summary: AllTogether standardizes prompts for HTML-based web navigation and compares prompting with instruction fine-tuning. Its analysis examines how HTML context, interaction history, and current environmental feedback affect task execution.
authors: Jiarun Liu; Wentao Hu; Chunhong Zhang

name: PPTC Benchmark: Evaluating Large Language Models for PowerPoint Task Completion
summary: Evaluates multi-turn PowerPoint creation and editing by scoring the resulting presentation files.
authors: Yiduo Guo; Zekai Zhang; Yaobo Liang; Dongyan Zhao; Nan Duan

name: GPT-4V in Wonderland: Large Multimodal Models for Zero-Shot Smartphone GUI Navigation
summary: Studies MM-Navigator, a multimodal agent that interprets smartphone screenshots and predicts localized actions without task-specific training.
authors: An Yan; Zhengyuan Yang; Wanrong Zhu; Kevin Lin; Linjie Li; Jianfeng Wang; Jianwei Yang; Yiwu Zhong; Julian McAuley; Jianfeng Gao; Zicheng Liu; Lijuan Wang

name: Autonomous Large Language Model Agents Enabling Intent-Driven Mobile GUI Testing
summary: DroidAgent uses language models and memory to set and execute GUI test goals in Android apps; an evaluation covers 15 apps from the Themis benchmark.
authors: Juyeon Yoon; Robert Feldt; Shin Yoo
venue: 2024 IEEE Conference on Software Testing, Verification and Validation (ICST)

name: ProAgent: From Robotic Process Automation to Agentic Process Automation
summary: Introduces ProAgent, an LLM-based agent that builds automation workflows from human instructions and coordinates specialized agents during workflow execution.
authors: Yining Ye; Xin Cong; Shizuo Tian; Jiannan Cao; Hao Wang; Yujia Qin; Yaxi Lu; Heyang Yu; Huadong Wang; Yankai Lin; Zhiyuan Liu; Maosong Sun

name: GAIA: a benchmark for General AI Assistants
summary: Introduces questions that test assistant reasoning, multimodal understanding, browsing, and tool use beyond screen-action execution alone.
authors: Grégoire Mialon; Clémentine Fourrier; Craig Swift; Thomas Wolf; Yann LeCun; Thomas Scialom

name: Exposing Limitations of Language Model Agents in Sequential-Task Compositions on the Web
summary: CompWoB adds 50 composed web-automation tasks to study generalization from simpler interactions. The paper compares prompted and fine-tuned agents, balances task training data, and probes sensitivity to changes in instruction order.
authors: Hiroki Furuta; Yutaka Matsuo; Aleksandra Faust; Izzeddin Gur

name: Explore, Select, Derive, and Recall: Augmenting LLM with Human-like Memory for Mobile Task Automation
summary: Introduces MobileGPT, which organizes mobile-app experience into reusable subtasks using an explore, select, derive, and recall cycle. Its memory supports learning task procedures and adapting them to new contexts.
authors: Sunjae Lee; Junyoung Choi; Jungjae Lee; Munim Hasan Wasi; Hojun Choi; Steven Y. Ko; Sangeun Oh; Insik Shin

name: Intelligent Virtual Assistants with LLM-based Process Automation
summary: Presents LLMPA, a mobile process-automation architecture that decomposes requests, identifies interface elements, predicts actions and checks errors. Demonstrations evaluate multistep operations in Alipay.
authors: Yanchu Guan; Dong Wang; Zhixuan Chu; Shiyu Wang; Feiyue Ni; Ruihua Song; Longfei Li; Jinjie Gu; Chenyi Zhuang

name: CogAgent: A Visual Language Model for GUI Agents
summary: Introduces a visual-language model with low- and high-resolution image encoders for screenshot understanding and GUI navigation.
venue: Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition

name: UINav: A Practical Approach to Train On-Device Automation Agents
summary: Introduces UINav, a demonstration-based method for training mobile UI automation agents, with a referee model for failure feedback and automatic augmentation of examples.
authors: Wei Li; Fu-Lin Hsu; Will Bishop; Folawiyo Campbell-Ajala; Max Lin; Oriana Riva

name: VisionTasker: Mobile Task Automation Using Vision Based UI Understanding and LLM Task Planning
summary: VisionTasker converts screenshots into textual UI interpretations and presents one interface at a time to an LLM planner for action selection. It evaluates visual representations and execution of 147 tasks on an Android smartphone, including integration with programming by demonstration.
authors: Yunpeng Song; Yiheng Bian; Yongtao Tang; Guiyu Ma; Zhongmin Cai

name: ASSISTGUI: Task-Oriented Desktop Graphical User Interface Automation
summary: Introduces Windows application tasks and an actor-critic agent framework for mouse-and-keyboard automation of desktop workflows.
authors: Difei Gao; Lei Ji; Zechen Bai; Mingyu Ouyang; Peiran Li; Dongxing Mao; Qinchen Wu; Weichen Zhang; Peiyi Wang; Xiangwu Guo; Hengxu Wang; Luowei Zhou; Mike Zheng Shou

authors: Chi Zhang; Zhao Yang; Jiaxuan Liu; Yanda Li; Yucheng Han; Xin Chen; Zebiao Huang; Bin Fu; Gang Yu

name: WebVLN: Vision-and-Language Navigation on Websites
summary: WebVLN trains website navigation from question-based instructions using both rendered visual information and underlying HTML. It introduces WebVLN-v1 and a website-aware navigation network to study this digital variant of vision-and-language navigation.
authors: Qi Chen; Dileepa Pitawela; Chongyang Zhao; Gengze Zhou; Hsiang-Ting Chen; Qi Wu

name: AutoTask: Executing Arbitrary Voice Commands by Exploring and Learning from Mobile GUI

authors: Lihang Pan; Bowen Wang; Chun Yu; Yuxuan Chen; Xiangyu Zhang; Yuanchun Shi

name: GPT-4V(ision) is a Generalist Web Agent, if Grounded
summary: Introduces SeeAct and live-website evaluation, examining how visual planning and element grounding affect web-agent task completion.
authors: Boyuan Zheng; Boyu Gou; Jihyung Kil; Huan Sun; Yu Su
venue: Proceedings of the 41st International Conference on Machine Learning

name: MobileAgent: enhancing mobile control via human-machine interaction and SOP integration
summary: Combines operating-procedure context with user interaction to guide mobile task automation and handle personalized or sensitive requests.
authors: Tinghe Ding

name: SeeClick: Harnessing GUI Grounding for Advanced Visual GUI Agents
summary: Trains a screenshot-driven GUI agent with grounding pretraining and introduces ScreenSpot for evaluating interface target localization.
authors: Kanzhi Cheng; Qiushi Sun; Yougang Chu; Fangzhi Xu; Yantao Li; Jianbing Zhang; Zhiyong Wu
venue: Proceedings of the 62nd Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers)

name: AgentBoard: An Analytical Evaluation Board of Multi-turn LLM Agents
summary: Introduces AgentBoard, a multiturn agent evaluation framework with intermediate progress metrics and analysis tools. Its broader task suite includes WebShop and WebArena interactions with stepwise progress measurements.
authors: Chang Ma; Junlei Zhang; Zhihao Zhu; Cheng Yang; Yujiu Yang; Yaohui Jin; Zhenzhong Lan; Lingpeng Kong; Junxian He

name: VisualWebArena: Evaluating Multimodal Agents on Realistic Visual Web Tasks
summary: Introduces visually grounded website tasks for evaluating multimodal agents that must interpret both images and text.

venue: Proceedings of the 62nd Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers)

name: WebVoyager: Building an End-to-End Web Agent with Large Multimodal Models
summary: Combines multimodal web interaction with a real-website task collection and an automated evaluation protocol.
authors: Hongliang He; Wenlin Yao; Kaixin Ma; Wenhao Yu; Yong Dai; Hongming Zhang; Zhenzhong Lan; Dong Yu
venue: Proceedings of the 62nd Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers)

name: GPTVoiceTasker: Advancing Multi-step Mobile Task Efficiency Through Dynamic Interface Exploration and Learning
summary: Introduces GPTVoiceTasker, a mobile assistant that interprets user commands, executes device interactions, and learns from prior commands to streamline later task execution. The work includes a user study of task efficiency.
authors: Minh Duc Vu; Han Wang; Zhuang Li; Jieshan Chen; Shengdong Zhao; Zhenchang Xing; Chunyang Chen

name: Mobile-Agent: Autonomous Multi-Modal Mobile Device Agent with Visual Perception
summary: Uses visual perception tools and task decomposition to operate mobile applications without relying on app interface metadata.
authors: Junyang Wang; Haiyang Xu; Jiabo Ye; Ming Yan; Weizhou Shen; Ji Zhang; Fei Huang; Jitao Sang

name: Dual-View Visual Contextualization for Web Navigation
summary: Uses screenshot geometry and visual content to enrich HTML element representations for web navigation. Nearby elements contribute textual and visual context, with evaluation on cross-task, cross-website, and cross-domain Mind2Web splits.
authors: Jihyung Kil; Chan Hee Song; Boyuan Zheng; Xiang Deng; Yu Su; Wei-Lun Chao

name: ScreenAI: A Vision-Language Model for UI and Infographics Understanding
summary: Introduces ScreenAI and screen-annotation training that supports UI question answering, navigation, and summarization data generation.
authors: Gilles Baechler; Srinivas Sunkara; Maria Wang; Fedir Zubach; Hassan Mansoor; Vincent Etter; Victor Cărbune; Jason Lin; Jindong Chen; Abhanshu Sharma

name: UEyes: An Eye-Tracking Dataset across User Interface Types
summary: Introduces UEyes, an eye-tracking dataset of webpage, desktop, mobile, and poster interfaces, and analyzes how people view these different UI types.
authors: Yue Jiang; Luis A. Leiva; Paul R. B. Houssel; Hamed R. Tavakoli; Julia Kylmälä; Antti Oulasvirta

name: WebLINX: Real-World Website Navigation with Multi-Turn Dialogue
summary: Collects expert demonstrations of conversational web navigation and studies retrieval-based element selection for processing large pages.
authors: Xing Han Lù; Zdeněk Kasner; Siva Reddy
venue: Proceedings of the 41st International Conference on Machine Learning

name: Understanding the Weakness of Large Language Model Agents within a Complex Android Environment
summary: Introduces AndroidArena and analyzes agent limitations in cross-application tasks, user constraints, exploration, and reflection.
authors: Mingzhe Xing; Rongkai Zhang; Hui Xue; Qi Chen; Fan Yang; Zhen Xiao

name: OS-Copilot: Towards Generalist Computer Agents with Self-Improvement
summary: Provides an operating-system agent framework connecting applications, files, terminals, and web tools, with accumulated skills for subsequent tasks.
authors: Zhiyong Wu; Chengcheng Han; Zichen Ding; Zhenmin Weng; Zhoumianze Liu; Shunyu Yao; Tao Yu; Lingpeng Kong

name: UFO: A UI-Focused Agent for Windows OS Interaction
summary: UFO uses two agents to inspect Windows application interfaces and their control metadata, then grounds and executes user requests within and across applications. The study evaluates this UI-focused architecture on nine Windows applications.
authors: Chaoyun Zhang; Liqun Li; Shilin He; Xu Zhang; Bo Qiao; Si Qin; Minghua Ma; Yu Kang; Qingwei Lin; Saravan Rajmohan; Dongmei Zhang; Qi Zhang
venue: Proceedings of the 2025 Conference of the Nations of the Americas Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics: Human Language Technologies (Volume 1: Long Papers)

name: ScreenAgent: A Vision Language Model-driven Computer Control Agent
summary: Combines a screenshot-and-action dataset with a planning, acting, and reflecting loop for computer control through mouse and keyboard actions.
authors: Runliang Niu; Jindong Li; Shiqi Wang; Yali Fu; Xiyu Hu; Xueyuan Leng; He Kong; Yi Chang; Qi Wang

name: A Trembling House of Cards? Mapping Adversarial Attacks against Language Agents
summary: Presents a conceptual perception–reasoning–action framework and 12 potential attack scenarios for language agents, including hypothetical web-navigation attacks.
authors: Lingbo Mo; Zeyi Liao; Boyuan Zheng; Yu Su; Chaowei Xiao; Huan Sun

name: Watch Out for Your Agents! Investigating Backdoor Threats to LLM-Based Agents
summary: Studies backdoor attacks on LLM agents, including triggers in user queries or intermediate observations, with web shopping among the evaluated agent tasks.
authors: Wenkai Yang; Xiaohan Bi; Yankai Lin; Sishuo Chen; Jie Zhou; Xu Sun

name: CoCo-Agent: A Comprehensive Cognitive MLLM Agent for Smartphone GUI Automation
summary: Combines screenshots, layout information, and action history with a factored action predictor for smartphone automation.
authors: Xinbei Ma; Zhuosheng Zhang; Hai Zhao
venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: ACL 2024

name: Improving Language Understanding from Screenshots
summary: Studies language understanding from text-rendered screenshots using joint image-patch and text prediction; a perception foundation relevant to screen-reading models.
authors: Tianyu Gao; Zirui Wang; Adithya Bhaskar; Danqi Chen

name: On the Multi-turn Instruction Following for Conversational Web Agents
summary: MT-Mind2Web evaluates web navigation through sequences of conversational user instructions. Self-MAP combines memory-augmented planning with reflection to preserve context and dependencies across those interaction turns.
authors: Yang Deng; Xuan Zhang; Wenxuan Zhang; Yifei Yuan; See-Kiong Ng; Tat-Seng Chua
venue: Proceedings of the 62nd Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers)

name: WIPI: A New Web Threat for LLM-Driven Web Agents
summary: Studies WIPI, a black-box indirect-instruction threat in which webpage content redirects LLM-driven web agents. Evaluation spans plugin-based agents, Web GPTs, and open-source web-agent implementations.
authors: Fangzhou Wu; Shutong Wu; Yulong Cao; Chaowei Xiao

name: OmniACT: A Dataset and Benchmark for Enabling Multimodal Generalist Autonomous Agents for Desktop and Web
summary: Introduces a dataset and benchmark for generating executable task scripts from screenshots and visually grounded desktop or web instructions.
authors: Raghav Kapoor; Yash Parag Butala; Melisa Russak; Jing Yu Koh; Kiran Kamble; Waseem Alshikh; Ruslan Salakhutdinov

name: Android in the Zoo: Chain-of-Action-Thought for GUI Agents
summary: Introduces Chain-of-Action-Thought and Android-In-The-Zoo annotations that connect prior actions, screen observations, intended actions, and expected outcomes.
authors: Jiwen Zhang; Jihao Wu; Yihua Teng; Minghui Liao; Nuo Xu; Xiao Xiao; Zhongyu Wei; Duyu Tang
venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2024

name: Cradle: Empowering Foundation Agents Towards General Computer Control
summary: Uses screenshot observations, planning modules, and generated low-level keyboard and mouse control for general computer interaction.
authors: Weihao Tan; Wentao Zhang; Xinrun Xu; Haochong Xia; Ziluo Ding; Boyu Li; Bohan Zhou; Junpeng Yue; Jiechuan Jiang; Yewen Li; Ruyi An; Molei Qin; Chuqiao Zong; Longtao Zheng; Yujie Wu; Xiaoqiang Chai; Yifei Bi; Tianbao Xie; Pengjie Gu; Xiyun Li; Ceyao Zhang; Long Tian; Chaojie Wang; Xinrun Wang; Börje F. Karlsson; Bo An; Shuicheng Yan; Zongqing Lu
venue: Proceedings of the 42nd International Conference on Machine Learning

name: SheetAgent: Towards A Generalist Agent for Spreadsheet Reasoning and Manipulation via Large Language Models
summary: Introduces SheetRM, a benchmark of long-horizon spreadsheet tasks, and SheetAgent, an LLM agent that plans, retrieves information and reflects while manipulating spreadsheets.
authors: Yibin Chen; Yifu Yuan; Zeyu Zhang; Yan Zheng; Jinyi Liu; Fei Ni; Jianye Hao; Hangyu Mao; Fuzheng Zhang

name: PPTC-R benchmark: Towards Evaluating the Robustness of Large Language Models for PowerPoint Task Completion
summary: Benchmarks robustness of API-based PowerPoint completion under sentence-level, semantic, and multilingual instruction perturbations and changes to the available API set.
authors: Zekai Zhang; Yiduo Guo; Yaobo Liang; Dongyan Zhao; Nan Duan

name: UI Semantic Group Detection: Grouping UI Elements with Similar Semantics in Mobile Graphical User Interface
summary: UISCGD detects semantic groups of adjacent text and non-text UI elements. It learns from Android and iOS screenshots to support interface retrieval, UI-to-code structure and screen-reader accessibility.
authors: Shuhong Xiao; Yunnong Chen; Yaxuan Song; Liuqing Chen; Lingyun Sun; Yankun Zhen; Yanfang Chang

name: WorkArena: How Capable Are Web Agents at Solving Common Knowledge Work Tasks?

authors: Alexandre Drouin; Maxime Gasse; Massimo Caccia; Issam H. Laradji; Manuel Del Verme; Tom Marty; Léo Boisvert; Megh Thakkar; Quentin Cappart; David Vazquez; Nicolas Chapados; Alexandre Lacoste

name: AutoGuide: Automated Generation and Selection of Context-Aware Guidelines for Large Language Model Agents
summary: Introduces AutoGuide, which generates conditional, context-aware guidelines from past agent experience to support decisions in sequential tasks, including web navigation.

name: Computer User Interface Understanding. A New Dataset and a Learning Framework
summary: Introduces desktop interaction videos and a framework combining synthetic examples with hierarchical contrastive learning for interface classification.

name: Tur[k]ingBench: A Challenge Benchmark for Web Agents
summary: Evaluates web agents on multimodal annotation tasks adapted from HTML interfaces originally built for crowdsourcing workers.

venue: Proceedings of the 2025 Conference of the Nations of the Americas Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics: Human Language Technologies (Volume 1: Long Papers)

name: MineDreamer: Learning to Follow Instructions via Chain-of-Imagination for Simulated-World Control
summary: Introduces MineDreamer, a Minecraft agent that imagines stages of an instruction and turns them into keyboard-and-mouse actions in a simulated world.
authors: Enshen Zhou; Yiran Qin; Zhenfei Yin; Yuzhou Huang; Ruimao Zhang; Lu Sheng; Yu Qiao; Jing Shao

name: AgentStudio: A Toolkit for Building General Virtual Agents
summary: AgentStudio combines an interactive GUI/API environment with tools for creating tasks, annotating interface elements, and labeling actions in videos. Its online suite and GroundUI, IDMBench, and CriticBench datasets examine interaction, grounding, learning from video, and success detection.
authors: Longtao Zheng; Zhiyuan Huang; Zhenghai Xue; Xinrun Wang; Bo An; Shuicheng Yan

name: Draw-and-Understand: Leveraging Visual Prompts to Enable MLLMs to Comprehend What You Want
summary: Introduces Draw-and-Understand and MDVP-Bench for understanding visual prompts such as points and boxes; its multi-domain data includes mobile and web screenshots.
authors: Weifeng Lin; Xinyu Wei; Ruichuan An; Peng Gao; Bocheng Zou; Yulin Luo; Siyuan Huang; Shanghang Zhang; Hongsheng Li

name: ReALM: Reference Resolution As Language Modeling
summary: Frames conversational and on-screen reference resolution as language modeling, allowing textual representations of screen entities to support user-reference interpretation. Evaluation separately examines on-screen references against an existing resolver and language-model baselines.
authors: Joel Ruben Antony Moniz; Soundarya Krishnan; Melis Ozyildirim; Prathamesh Saraf; Halim Cagri Ates; Yuan Zhang; Hong Yu

name: Prompt2Task: Automating UI Tasks on Smartphones from Textual Prompts
summary: Prompt2Task converts textual goals or procedures into smartphone UI automation using agents for intent interpretation, external-information handling, and execution. User feedback and accumulated task knowledge support subsequent task generation and operation.
authors: Tian Huang; Chun Yu; Weinan Shi; Zijian Peng; David Yang; Weiqi Sun; Yuanchun Shi

name: AutoWebGLM: A Large Language Model-based Web Navigating Agent
summary: Builds a web agent through simplified HTML observations, human-and-AI browsing data, curriculum training, and reinforcement-learning refinement.

authors: Keen You; Haotian Zhang; Eldon Schoop; Floris Weers; Amanda Swearngin; Jeffrey Nichols; Yinfei Yang; Zhe Gan

name: WILBUR: Adaptive In-Context Learning for Robust and Accurate Web Agents
summary: WILBUR learns to rank prior task demonstrations for a web agent’s prompt and synthesizes instructions from past runs. A generated task curriculum and a backtracking mechanism support adaptation and recovery, evaluated on WebVoyager.
authors: Michael Lutz; Arth Bohra; Manvel Saroyan; Artem Harutyunyan; Giovanni Campagna

name: VisualWebBench: How Far Have Multimodal LLMs Evolved in Web Page Understanding and Grounding?
summary: Separately evaluates web-page reading, understanding, and element grounding across tasks drawn from real websites.
authors: Junpeng Liu; Yifan Song; Bill Yuchen Lin; Wai Lam; Graham Neubig; Yuanzhi Li; Xiang Yue

name: Autonomous Evaluation and Refinement of Digital Agents
summary: Compares automatic trajectory evaluators for web navigation and device control against oracle judgments. The resulting feedback is used for agent fine-tuning and inference-time guidance, including experiments on WebArena.
authors: Jiayi Pan; Yichi Zhang; Nicholas Tomlin; Yifei Zhou; Sergey Levine; Alane Suhr

name: OSWorld: Benchmarking Multimodal Agents for Open-Ended Tasks in Real Computer Environments

summary: Introduces AutoScraper, a two-stage framework that uses HTML structure and similarities across pages to generate scrapers for data collection from websites.

summary: FlowMind generates API-based workflows from user requests for process automation and presents workflow descriptions that users can inspect and comment on.

authors: Rajat Chawla; Adarsh Jha; Muskaan Kumar; Mukunda NS; Ishaan Bhola

name: LlamaTouch: A Faithful and Scalable Testbed for Mobile UI Task Automation
summary: LlamaTouch executes mobile tasks on devices and evaluates whether an agent visits manually annotated essential application or system states. Screenshot and hierarchy annotations, combined with exact and fuzzy state matching, support evaluation of 496 tasks across multiple agents.
authors: Li Zhang; Shihe Wang; Xianqing Jia; Zhihan Zheng; Yunhe Yan; Longxi Gao; Yuanchun Li; Mengwei Xu

name: Benchmarking Mobile Device Control Agents across Diverse Configurations
summary: Introduces B-MoCA, an interactive mobile-control benchmark that varies device settings, layouts, and languages to test generalization.

name: MMAC-Copilot: Multi-modal Agent Collaboration Operating Copilot

name: Automating the Enterprise with Foundation Models

name: Unveiling Disparities in Web Task Handling Between Human and Web Agent
summary: Compares human think-aloud web-task behavior with web-agent planning, action, and reflection. The analysis highlights differences in updating plans, handling ambiguity, and investigating failures.

name: MUD: Towards a Large-Scale and Noise-Filtered UI Dataset for Modern Style UI Modeling
summary: MUD combines LLM-guided Android app exploration, noise filtering and human annotation to collect modern UI screenshots. The study evaluates the resulting data for element detection and UI retrieval.
authors: Sidong Feng; Suyu Ma; Han Wang; David Kong; Chunyang Chen

name: Latent State Estimation Helps UI Agents to Reason
summary: Studies explicit textual estimates of latent UI state, including whether commanded actions occurred and how far a task has progressed. The experiments compare agents that reason with these estimates against agents that omit them across public and internal task benchmarks.
authors: William E Bishop; Alice Li; Christopher Rawles; Oriana Riva

name: SmartFlow: Robotic Process Automation using LLMs
summary: Presents SmartFlow, which converts visible GUI elements into text for language-model action planning and executes the plan through a scripting engine. A collection of enterprise applications evaluates adaptation to different layouts and tasks.
authors: Arushi Jain; Shubham Paliwal; Monika Sharma; Lovekesh Vig; Gautam Shroff

name: AndroidWorld: A Dynamic Benchmarking Environment for Autonomous Agents
summary: Introduces parameterized Android tasks with initialization, success checks, and cleanup for reproducible interactive evaluation.
authors: Christopher Rawles; Sarah Clinckemaillie; Yifan Chang; Jonathan Waltz; Gabrielle Lau; Marybeth Fair; Alice Li; William Bishop; Wei Li; Folawiyo Campbell-Ajala; Daniel Toyama; Robert Berry; Divya Tyamagundlu; Timothy Lillicrap; Oriana Riva

name: V-Zen: Efficient GUI Understanding and Precise Grounding With A Novel Multimodal LLM
summary: Describes V-Zen, a multimodal GUI model with dual-resolution image encoders for grounding and next-action prediction, fine-tuned using GUIDE interface elements and task sequences.

authors: Junyang Wang; Haiyang Xu; Haitao Jia; Xi Zhang; Ming Yan; Weizhou Shen; Ji Zhang; Fei Huang; Jitao Sang

name: WebSuite: Systematically Evaluating Why Web Agents Fail
summary: WebSuite organizes browser operations into an action taxonomy and tests both isolated controls and complete workflows. Its diagnostic tasks attribute failures to specific actions, enabling comparison of text-based and multimodal web agents.
authors: Eric Li; Jim Waldo

name: On the Effects of Data Scale on UI Control Agents
summary: Studies how Android task performance changes with demonstration scale and releases AndroidControl with high- and low-level instructions.
authors: Wei Li; William Bishop; Alice Li; Chris Rawles; Folawiyo Campbell-Ajala; Divya Tyamagundlu; Oriana Riva
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems

name: CAAP: Context-Aware Action Planning Prompting to Solve Computer Tasks with Front-End UI Only
summary: CAAP converts screenshots into textual observations and plans keyboard-and-mouse actions using a prompt that examines task context from multiple perspectives. The agent is evaluated on MiniWoB++ and WebShop using only front-end visual observations.
authors: Junhee Cho; Jihoon Kim; Daseul Bae; Jinho Choo; Youngjune Gwon; Yeong-Dae Kwon

name: Tell Me What's Next: Textual Foresight for Generic UI Representations
summary: Textual Foresight learns UI representations by describing the future screen expected after an action on the current interface. The OpenApp dataset supports pretraining and downstream evaluation of representations that connect individual elements with whole-screen changes.
authors: Andrea Burns; Kate Saenko; Bryan A. Plummer

name: MobileAgentBench: An Efficient and User-Friendly Benchmark for Mobile LLM Agents
summary: Introduces a mobile-agent benchmark with tasks across open-source applications, organized by difficulty to reduce manual evaluation effort.
authors: Luyuan Wang; Yongyu Deng; Yiwei Zha; Guodong Mao; Qinmin Wang; Tianchen Min; Wei Chen; Shoufa Chen

name: Practical, Automated Scenario-based Mobile App Testing
summary: ScenTest builds scenario-specific event knowledge graphs from crowdsourced test reports containing GUI and action information. It uses the current app state and testing context to generate scenario tests across applications.
authors: Shengcheng Yu; Chunrong Fang; Mingzhe Du; Zimin Ding; Zhenyu Chen; Zhendong Su

summary: TongUI converts multimodal online tutorials, including videos and articles, into GUI-agent trajectories. Its GUI-Net dataset contains 143,000 trajectories spanning five operating systems and more than 200 applications, and supports fine-tuning for grounding and navigation.
authors: Bofei Zhang; Zirui Shang; Zhi Gao; Wang Zhang; Rui Xie; Xiaojian Ma; Tao Yuan; Xinxiao Wu; Song-Chun Zhu; Qing Li

name: WebLists: Extracting Structured Information From Complex Interactive Websites Using Executable LLM Agents
summary: Introduces WebLists, a benchmark for structured extraction from interactive websites, and BardeenAgent, which turns web-agent runs into replayable CSS-selector programs.
authors: Arth Bohra; Manvel Saroyan; Danil Melkozerov; Vahe Karufanyan; Gabriel Maher; Pascal Weinberger; Artem Harutyunyan; Giovanni Campagna

name: LearnAct: Few-Shot Mobile GUI Agent with a Unified Demonstration Benchmark
summary: LearnAct parses human demonstrations into reusable knowledge, retrieves relevant examples, and uses them during mobile GUI task execution. The accompanying LearnGUI benchmark includes 2,252 offline tasks and 101 online tasks for studying adaptation from demonstrations.
authors: Guangyi Liu; Pengxiang Zhao; Liang Liu; Zhiming Chen; Yuxiang Chai; Shuai Ren; Hao Wang; Shibo He; Wenchao Meng

name: A Survey on (M)LLM-Based GUI Agents
summary: Analyzes LLM-based GUI agents through four components (perception, exploration, planning, and interaction) and the methods used to evaluate them.
authors: Fei Tang; Haolei Xu; Hang Zhang; Siqi Chen; Xingyu Wu; Yongliang Shen; Wenqi Zhang; Guiyang Hou; Zeqi Tan; Yuchen Yan; Kaitao Song; Jian Shao; Weiming Lu; Jun Xiao; Yueting Zhuang

name: ViMo: A Generative Visual GUI World Model for App Agents
summary: ViMo predicts the next mobile-app screenshot after a candidate action by separately modeling graphics and text. A symbolic placeholder representation preserves layout while a second predictor supplies readable text, enabling visual lookahead for GUI-agent planning.
authors: Dezhao Luo; Bohan Tang; Kang Li; Georgios Papoudakis; Jifei Song; Shaogang Gong; Jianye Hao; Jun Wang; Kun Shao

name: DoomArena: A framework for Testing AI Agents Against Evolving Security Threats
summary: Presents a modular security testing framework that plugs into BrowserGym and tool-use benchmarks to evaluate agents under configurable threat models.
authors: Leo Boisvert; Mihir Bansal; Chandra Kiran Reddy Evuru; Gabriel Huang; Abhay Puri; Avinandan Bose; Maryam Fazel; Quentin Cappart; Jason Stanley; Alexandre Lacoste; Alexandre Drouin; Krishnamurthy Dvijotham

name: InfiGUI-R1: Advancing Multimodal GUI Agents from Reactive Actors to Deliberative Reasoners
summary: Uses a staged reasoning-focused training framework to move GUI agents from reactive actions toward deliberative planning and recovery.
authors: Yuhang Liu; Pengxiang Li; Congkai Xie; Xavier Hu; Xiaotian Han; Shengyu Zhang; Hongxia Yang; Fei Wu

name: UFO2: The Desktop AgentOS
summary: Introduces UFO2, a Windows desktop agent architecture combining a coordinating HostAgent, application-specialized agents, and a shared GUI/API action layer. It integrates UI Automation, visual parsing, speculative planning, and an isolated picture-in-picture desktop.
authors: Chaoyun Zhang; He Huang; Chiming Ni; Jian Mu; Si Qin; Shilin He; Lu Wang; Fangkai Yang; Pu Zhao; Chao Du; Liqun Li; Yu Kang; Zhao Jiang; Suzhen Zheng; Rujia Wang; Jiaxu Qian; Minghua Ma; Jian-Guang Lou; Qingwei Lin; Saravan Rajmohan; Dongmei Zhang

name: Guiding VLM Agents with Process Rewards at Inference Time for GUI Navigation
summary: Guides visual GUI agents at inference time with a process-reward model that evaluates intermediate actions. It combines stepwise guidance with trajectory reflection and retry mechanisms in static and interactive navigation tasks.
authors: Zhiyuan Hu; Shiyun Xiong; Yifan Zhang; See-Kiong Ng; Anh Tuan Luu; Bo An; Shuicheng Yan; Bryan Hooi

name: PixelWeb: The First Web GUI Dataset with Pixel-Wise Labels
summary: Introduces PixelWeb, a webpage GUI dataset with element images, contours, and pixel masks. Its annotation pipeline combines bitmap channel information with DOM-based visibility and stacking analysis to address occlusion and overlapping elements.
authors: Qi Yang; Weichen Bi; Haiyang Shen; Yaoqi Guo; Yun Ma

name: Toward a Human-Centered Evaluation Framework for Trustworthy LLM-Powered GUI Agents
summary: Presents a position paper on privacy and security evaluation for GUI agents, identifying risk categories and challenges in involving human evaluators. It proposes risk-aware assessment and in-context consent as design directions.
authors: Chaoran Chen; Zhiping Zhang; Ibrahim Khalilov; Bingcan Guo; Simret A Gebreegziabher; Yanfang Ye; Ziang Xiao; Yaxing Yao; Tianshi Li; Toby Jia-Jun Li

name: WASP: Benchmarking Web Agent Security Against Prompt Injection Attacks
summary: Introduces WASP, an end-to-end benchmark for prompt-injection security in web agents. Its evaluation separates partial attack progress from completion of the attacker’s full objective.
authors: Ivan Evtimov; Arman Zharmagambetov; Aaron Grattafiori; Chuan Guo; Kamalika Chaudhuri

name: LLM-Powered GUI Agents in Phone Automation: Surveying Progress and Prospects
summary: Reviews LLM-driven phone GUI agents with a taxonomy of agent frameworks, prompt- and training-based modeling, datasets, and benchmarks.
authors: Guangyi Liu; Pengxiang Zhao; Yaozhen Liang; Liang Liu; Yaxuan Guo; Han Xiao; Weifeng Lin; Yuxiang Chai; Yue Han; Shuai Ren; Hao Wang; Xiaoyu Liang; WenHao Wang; Tianze Wu; Zhengxi Lu; Siheng Chen; LiLinghao; Hao Wang; Guanjing Xiong; Yong Liu; Hongsheng Li

name: A Survey on GUI Agents with Foundation Models Enhanced by Reinforcement Learning
summary: Formalizes GUI tasks as Markov decision processes and traces agent training from prompting through supervised fine-tuning to reinforcement learning.
authors: Jiahao Li; Kaer Huang

name: WebEvolver: Enhancing Web Agent Self-Improvement with Coevolving World Model
summary: WebEvolver trains a co-evolving world model to predict web observations and generate additional agent-training trajectories. The same model supports look-ahead action selection at inference, with evaluation on live web-task benchmarks.
authors: Tianqing Fang; Hongming Zhang; Zhisong Zhang; Kaixin Ma; Wenhao Yu; Haitao Mi; Dong Yu

name: WebThinker: Empowering Large Reasoning Models with Deep Research Capability
summary: Combines iterative web search and link-following with interleaved reasoning and report drafting for deep research. Its reported web explorer retrieves page content through a crawler.
authors: Xiaoxi Li; Jiajie Jin; Guanting Dong; Hongjin Qian; Yongkang Wu; Ji-Rong Wen; Yutao Zhu; Zhicheng Dou

name: ScaleTrack: Scaling and back-tracking Automated GUI Agents
summary: ScaleTrack combines a unified collection of GUI grounding samples with a planning objective that predicts the next action while reconstructing prior actions. This backward prediction links the current screenshot to interaction history during agent training.
authors: Jing Huang; Zhixiong Zeng; Wenkang Han; Yufeng Zhong; Liming Zheng; Shuai Fu; Jingyuan Chen; Lin Ma

name: Visual Test-time Scaling for GUI Agent Grounding
summary: RegionFocus adds visual test-time scaling by zooming into selected screenshot regions and maintaining an image-based map of landmarks and actions. It evaluates this grounding procedure with UI-TARS and Qwen2.5-VL on ScreenSpot-Pro and WebVoyager.
authors: Tiange Luo; Lajanugen Logeswaran; Justin Johnson; Honglak Lee

name: OSUniverse: Benchmark for Multimodal GUI-navigation AI Agents
summary: Introduces OSUniverse, a desktop GUI benchmark spanning precise clicks through multistep and multiapplication tasks. It provides both manual scoring and an automated validation mechanism.
authors: Mariya Davydova; Daniel Jeffries; Patrick Barker; Arturo Márquez Flores; Sinéad Ryan

name: WebGen-Bench: Evaluating LLMs on Generating Interactive and Functional Websites from Scratch
summary: Introduces WebGen-Bench for evaluating agents that generate multi-file websites, using a web-navigation agent to check whether the resulting pages pass interaction tests.
authors: Zimu Lu; Yunqiao Yang; Houxing Ren; Haotian Hou; Han Xiao; Ke Wang; Weikang Shi; Aojun Zhou; Mingjie Zhan; Hongsheng Li

name: Do MLLMs Capture How Interfaces Guide User Behavior? A Benchmark for Multimodal UI/UX Design Understanding
summary: Introduces WiserUI-Bench, pairing real UI variants from industry A/B tests with observed behavioral winners and expert explanations. It evaluates models’ ability to predict the more effective interface and explain its effect on user behavior.
authors: Jaehyun Jeon; Min Soo Kim; Jang Han Yoon; Sumin Shim; Yejin Choi; Hanbin Kim; Dae Hyun Kim; Youngjae Yu

name: EcoAgent: An Efficient Device-Cloud Collaborative Multi-Agent Framework for Mobile Automation
summary: EcoAgent splits mobile automation between cloud planning and on-device observation and verification. Compact screen descriptions and feedback reduce communication costs, with evaluation on AndroidWorld.
authors: Biao Yi; Xavier Hu; Yurun Chen; Shengyu Zhang; Hongxia Yang; Fan Wu

name: AgentVigil: Generic Black-Box Red-teaming for Indirect Prompt Injection against LLM Agents
summary: Introduces AgentVigil, a black-box fuzzing framework for finding indirect prompt injections against LLM agents, including attacks that redirect web navigation.
authors: Zhun Wang; Vincent Siu; Zhe Ye; Tianneng Shi; Yuzhou Nie; Xuandong Zhao; Chenguang Wang; Wenbo Guo; Dawn Song

name: Leveraging Vision-Language Models for Visual Grounding and Analysis of Automotive UI
summary: Introduces AutomotiveUI-Bench-4K and a fine-tuned vision-language model for locating elements and evaluating automotive infotainment interfaces.
authors: Benjamin Raphael Ernhofer; Daniil Prokhorov; Jannica Langner; Dominik Bollmann

name: Seed1.5-VL Technical Report
summary: Reports Seed1.5-VL, a general vision-language model evaluated on GUI control and gameplay alongside visual understanding and reasoning tasks.
