summary: GUI-ReWalk begins with stochastic interface exploration and then infers goals to generate coherent action trajectories. It supports long-horizon workflows across applications and studies training on the resulting data using grounding and navigation benchmarks.
authors: Musen Lin; Minghao Liu; Taoran Lu; Lichen Yuan; Yiwei Liu; Haonan Xu; Yu Miao; Yuhao Chao; Zhaojian Li

name: UIPro: Unleashing Superior Interaction Capability For GUI Agents
summary: UIPro pretrains GUI understanding on 20.6 million tasks and then harmonizes interaction datasets through a unified action space. Continued fine-tuning uses the merged multi-platform data to train action prediction for generalist GUI operation.
authors: Hongxin Li; Jingran Su; Jingfan Chen; Zheng Ju; Yuntao Chen; Qing Li; Zhaoxiang Zhang

name: Mano Technical Report
summary: Introduces Mano, a GUI agent trained with simulated data, supervised fine-tuning, and offline and online RL, with a verification module for error recovery.
authors: Tianyu Fu; Anyang Su; Chenxu Zhao; Hanning Wang; Minghui Wu; Zhe Yu; Fei Hu; Mingjia Shi; Wei Dong; Jiayao Wang; Yuyang Chen; Ruiyang Yu; Siran Peng; Menglin Li; Nan Huang; Haitian Wei; Jiawei Yu; Yi Xin; Xilin Zhao; Kai Gu; Ping Jiang; Sifan Zhou; Shuo Wang

name: Orcust: Stepwise-Feedback Reinforcement Learning for GUI Agent
summary: Orcust combines principle-constrained reward modeling with GUI trajectory collection in instrumented virtual machines. Environment-checkable and model-derived principles guide stepwise feedback for grounding, basic operations, and complete task execution.
authors: Junyu Lu; Songxin Zhang; Zejian Xie; Zhuoyang Song; Jiaxing Zhang

name: MobileRL: Online Agentic Reinforcement Learning for Mobile GUI Agents
summary: MobileRL adapts GRPO to mobile GUI training with difficulty-dependent replay of successes and filtering of failure curricula. A shortest-path reward adjustment accounts for task length, with evaluations on AndroidWorld and AndroidLab.
authors: Yifan Xu; Xiao Liu; Xinghan Liu; Jiaqi Fu; Hanchen Zhang; Bohao Jing; Shudan Zhang; Yuting Wang; Wenyi Zhao; Yuxiao Dong

name: Agentic Reinforcement Learning with Implicit Step Rewards
summary: Introduces iStar, a general agentic RL method that learns implicit step rewards; WebShop is one of several interactive benchmarks used to evaluate it.
authors: Xiaoqian Liu; Ke Wang; Yuchuan Wu; Fei Huang; Yongbin Li; Junge Zhang; Jianbin Jiao

name: Robust, Observable, and Evolvable Agentic Systems Engineering: A Principled Framework Validated via the Fairy GUI Agent
summary: Presents an agent-engineering framework combining runtime goal clarification, an observable component architecture and evolving execution memory. The Fairy mobile GUI agent evaluates these mechanisms on ambiguous tasks and through controlled and user studies.
authors: Jiazheng Sun; Ruimeng Yang; Xu Han; Jiayang Niu; Mingxuan Li; Te Yang; Yongyong Lu; Xin Peng

name: Recon-Act: A Self-Evolving Multi-Agent Browser-Use System via Web Reconnaissance, Tool Generation, and Task Execution
summary: Introduces Recon-Act, a browser-use framework that compares failed and successful web trajectories to create reusable tools for planning and executing long-horizon website tasks.
authors: Kaiwen He; Zhiwei Wang; Chenyi Zhuang; Jinjie Gu

name: Learning GUI Grounding with Spatial Reasoning from Visual Feedback
summary: GUI-Cursor treats GUI grounding as a sequence of cursor movements guided by visible feedback and movement history. Online reinforcement learning with trajectory rewards trains the model to refine the target location across multiple steps.
authors: Yu Zhao; Wei-Ning Chen; Huseyin Atahan Inan; Samuel Kessler; Lu Wang; Lukas Wutschitz; Fangkai Yang; Chaoyun Zhang; Pasquale Minervini; Saravan Rajmohan; Robert Sim

name: UISim: An Interactive Image-Based UI Simulator for Dynamic Mobile Environments
summary: Introduces UISim, an image-based mobile UI simulator that predicts the next screen layout after an action and renders the resulting screen for testing and data generation.
authors: Jiannan Xiang; Yun Zhu; Lei Shu; Maria Wang; Lijun Yu; Gabriel Barcik; James Lyon; Srinivas Sunkara; Jindong Chen

name: Benchmarking MLLM-based Web Understanding: Reasoning, Robustness and Safety
summary: Evaluates multimodal LLMs on web interface reasoning, visual perturbation robustness, and safety-critical web understanding tasks.
authors: Junliang Liu; Jingyu Xiao; Wenxin Tang; Zhixian Wang; Zipeng Xie; Wenxuan Wang; Minrui Zhang; Shuanghe Yu

name: D-Artemis: A Deliberative Cognitive Framework for Mobile GUI Multi-Agents
summary: Introduces D-Artemis, a mobile GUI agent framework that retrieves app-specific tips, checks actions before execution, and reflects on their outcomes without trajectory training.
authors: Hongze Mi; Yibo Feng; Wenjie Lu; Yuqi Wang; Jinyuan Li; Song Cao; He Cui; Tengfei Tian; Xuelin Zhang; Haotian Luo; Di Sun; Jun Fang; Hua Chai; Naiqiang Tan; Gang Pan

name: ProRe: A Proactive Reward System for GUI Agents via Reasoner-Actor Collaboration
summary: ProRe evaluates GUI task outcomes by having a reasoner assign targeted environment-probing tasks to specialist actors. The additional observations support reward judgments, with separate evaluation of judge accuracy and downstream agent task success.
authors: Gaole Dai; Shiqi Jiang; Ting Cao; Yuqing Yang; Yuanchun Li; Rui Tan; Mo Li; Lili Qiu

name: RISK: A Framework for GUI Agents in E-commerce Risk Management
summary: RISK combines browser-interaction training data, a benchmark, and reinforcement fine-tuning for e-commerce risk-management workflows. Its trajectories and rewards distinguish individual actions from multi-step stateful tasks involving deeply embedded web content.
authors: Renqi Chen; Zeyin Tao; Jianming Guo; Jingzhe Zhu; Yiheng Peng; Qingqing Sun; Tianyi Zhang; Shuai Chen

name: Secure and Efficient Access Control for Computer-Use Agents via Context Space
summary: Introduces CSAgent, which combines static access policies with user intent and context and enforces them through an operating-system service. A supporting toolchain constructs and refines policies for agents using API, CLI and GUI interfaces.
authors: Haochen Gong; Chenxiao Li; Rui Chang; Wenbo Shen

name: WebGen-Agent: Enhancing Interactive Website Generation with Multi-Level Feedback and Step-Level Reinforcement Learning
summary: Introduces WebGen-Agent for website code generation, using screenshot critiques and GUI-agent tests to refine code and provide step-level training rewards.
authors: Zimu Lu; Houxing Ren; Yunqiao Yang; Ke Wang; Zhuofan Zong; Junting Pan; Mingjie Zhan; Hongsheng Li

name: GUI-PRA: Process Reward Agent for GUI Tasks
summary: GUI-PRA evaluates GUI progress by generating task-specific criteria and actively inspecting visual evidence with tools. It tests offline judgment on OS-Critic Bench and the effects of this feedback on online mobile policies in AndroidWorld.
authors: Tao Xiong; Xavier Hu; Yurun Chen; Yuhang Liu; Changqiao Wu; Pengzhi Gao; Wei Liu; Jian Luan; Shengyu Zhang

name: GUI-Shepherd: Reliable Process Reward and Verification for Long-Sequence GUI Tasks
summary: Introduces GUI-Shepherd, a process reward model trained on annotated GUI interactions to give step-level feedback for agent training and verification on AndroidWorld and AndroidControl.
authors: Cong Chen; Kaixiang Ji; Hao Zhong; Muzhi Zhu; Anzhou Li; Guo Gan; Ziyuan Huang; Cheng Zou; Jiajia Liu; Jingdong Chen; Hao Chen; Chunhua Shen

name: Efficient Multi-turn RL for GUI Agents via Decoupled Training and Adaptive Data Curation
summary: DART separates GUI reinforcement learning into asynchronous environment, rollout, data-management, and training services. It curates experience by task difficulty, successful trajectories, and step uncertainty while correcting rollout-policy mismatch, with evaluation on OSWorld.
authors: Pengxiang Li; Zechen Hu; Zirui Shang; Jingrong Wu; Yang Liu; Hui Liu; Zhi Gao; Chenrui Shi; Bofei Zhang; Zihao Zhang; Xiaochuan Shi; Zedong YU; Yuwei Wu; Xinxiao Wu; Yunde Jia; Liuyu Xiang; Zhaofeng He; Qing Li

name: Generalist Scanner Meets Specialist Locator: A Synergistic Coarse-to-Fine Framework for Robust GUI Grounding
summary: GMS pairs a general vision-language scanner that proposes interface regions with a specialist locator that predicts coordinates within them. Hierarchical coarse-to-fine search coordinates the two components for GUI grounding on ScreenSpot-Pro.
authors: Zhecheng Li; Guoxian Song; Yiwei Wang; Zhen Xiong; Junsong Yuan; Yujun Cai

name: Retrieval-augmented GUI Agents with Generative Guidelines
summary: RAG-GUI trains a small guidance adapter to filter and summarize retrieved web tutorials while keeping the acting agent fixed. Supervised and rejection-sampling stages prepare the adapter for inference-time assistance, tested on offline web/mobile tasks and interactive Android tasks.
authors: Ran Xu; Kaixin Ma; Wenhao Yu; Hongming Zhang; Joyce C. Ho; Carl Yang; Dong Yu

name: Scaling Synthetic Task Generation for Agents via Exploration
summary: AutoPlay explores application states and functions to generate tasks, then uses a model executor and verifier to construct demonstrations. It produces 20,000 tasks across 20 Android apps and 10,000 tasks across 13 Ubuntu apps for supervised and reinforcement learning of UI agents.
authors: Ram Ramrakhya; Andrew Szot; Omar Attia; Yuhao Yang; Anh Nguyen; Bogdan Mazoure; Zhe Gan; Harsh Agrawal; Alexander Toshev

name: ReasoningBank: Scaling Agent Self-Evolving with Reasoning Memory
summary: Distills generalizable reasoning strategies from both successful and failed agent trajectories into a persistent memory bank for test-time retrieval.
authors: Siru Ouyang; Jun Yan; I-Hung Hsu; Yanfei Chen; Ke Jiang; Zifeng Wang; Rujun Han; Long T. Le; Samira Daruki; Xiangru Tang; Vishy Tirumalashetty; George Lee; Mahsan Rofouei; Hangfei Lin; Jiawei Han; Chen-Yu Lee; Tomas Pfister

name: Flash-Searcher: Fast and Effective Web Agents via DAG-Based Parallel Execution
summary: Introduces Flash-Searcher, a parallel agent framework that organizes dependent subtasks as a graph and runs independent paths concurrently; it is evaluated on deep-search benchmarks.
authors: Tianrui Qin; Qianben Chen; Sinuo Wang; He Xing; King Zhu; He Zhu; Dingfeng Shi; Xinxin Liu; Ge Zhang; Jiaheng Liu; Yuchen Eleanor Jiang; Xitong Gao; Wangchunshu Zhou

name: SCUBA: Salesforce Computer Use Benchmark
summary: SCUBA evaluates enterprise UI navigation and CRM workflows with 300 task instances derived from Salesforce user interviews. Salesforce sandbox execution and milestone-based assessment support comparisons between zero-shot agents and agents given demonstrations.
authors: Yutong Dai; Krithika Ramakrishnan; Jing Gu; Matthew Fernandez; Yanqi Luo; Viraj Prabhu; Zhenyu Hu; Silvio Savarese; Caiming Xiong; Zeyuan Chen; Ran Xu

name: Ferret-UI Lite: Lessons from Building Small On-Device GUI Agents
summary: Ferret-UI Lite develops a 3B GUI agent using mixed real and synthetic data, reasoning with visual tools at inference, and reinforcement learning. It evaluates grounding and navigation across mobile, web, and desktop settings, including AndroidWorld and OSWorld.
authors: Zhen Yang; Zi-Yi Dou; Di Feng; Forrest Huang; Anh Nguyen; Keen You; Omar Attia; Yuhao Yang; Michael Feng; Haotian Zhang; Ram Ramrakhya; Chao Jia; Jeffrey Nichols; Alexander Toshev; Yinfei Yang; Zhe Gan

name: PAL-UI: Planning with Active Look-back for Vision-Based GUI Agents
summary: PAL-UI combines observation/action summaries with selective retrieval of historical screenshots during planning. It trains mobile navigation models from step-level supervision and evaluates transfer to web navigation without additional training.
authors: Zikang Liu; Junyi Li; Wayne Xin Zhao; Dawei Gao; Yaliang Li; Ji-rong Wen

name: Graph2Eval: Automatic Multimodal Task Generation for Agents via Knowledge Graphs
summary: Introduces Graph2Eval, which generates multimodal agent evaluation tasks from knowledge graphs, including multi-step web interactions in Graph2Eval-Bench.
authors: Yurun Chen; Xavier Hu; Yuhan Liu; Ziqi Wang; Zeyi Liao; Lin Chen; Feng Wei; Yuxi Qian; Bo Zheng; Keting Yin; Shengyu Zhang

name: GUI-KV: Efficient GUI Agents via KV Cache with Spatio-Temporal Awareness
summary: GUI-KV compresses vision-language agents’ attention caches using visual-token saliency and redundancy between screenshot frames. The method requires no retraining and evaluates how cache budgets affect GUI action accuracy and computational cost.
authors: Kung-Hsiang Huang; Haoyi Qiu; Yutong Dai; Caiming Xiong; Chien-Sheng Wu

name: WAInjectBench: Benchmarking Prompt Injection Detections for Web Agents
summary: Introduces WAInjectBench with a threat-model taxonomy and malicious and benign text-image datasets for web-agent prompt-injection detection. It compares detector families across explicit and less visible forms of injected content.
authors: Yinuo Liu; Xilong Wang; Ruohan Xu; Yuqi Jia; Neil Zhenqiang Gong

name: WALT: Web Agents that Learn Tools
summary: WALT explores website functionality and converts demonstrated interactions into validated, reusable tools combining DOM actions, URL navigation, and agentic fallbacks. It evaluates this expanded browser action space on WebArena and VisualWebArena.
authors: Viraj Prabhu; Yutong Dai; Matthew Fernandez; Jing Gu; Krithika Ramakrishnan; Yanqi Luo; Silvio Savarese; Caiming Xiong; Junnan Li; Zeyuan Chen; Ran Xu

name: Just Do It!? Computer-Use Agents Exhibit Blind Goal-Directedness
summary: BLIND-ACT tests whether computer-use agents persist with ambiguous, contradictory, or infeasible goals without adequate contextual reasoning. Its OSWorld-based tasks and judged trajectories examine these behaviors and the effect of mitigation prompts.
authors: Erfan Shayegani; Keegan Hines; Yue Dong; Nael Abu-Ghazaleh; Roman Lutz; Spencer Whitehead; Vidhisha Balachandran; Besmira Nushi; Vibhav Vineet

name: Say One Thing, Do Another? Diagnosing Reasoning-Execution Gaps in VLM-Powered Mobile-Use Agents
summary: Introduces an evaluation framework for mobile GUI agents that compares actions implied by their reasoning with intended and executed actions to diagnose mismatches.
authors: Lingzhong Dong; Ziqi Zhou; Shuaibo Yang; Haiyue Sheng; Pengzhou Cheng; Zongru Wu; Zheng Wu; Gongshen Liu; Zhuosheng Zhang

name: Scaling Agents for Computer Use
summary: Introduces Behavior Judge, which converts execution trajectories into behavior narratives and compares multiple candidate rollouts. Experiments examine this selection approach on OSWorld, WindowsAgentArena and AndroidWorld.
authors: Gonzalo Gonzalez-Pumariega; Vincent Tu; Chih-Lun Lee; Jiachen Yang; Ang Li; Xin Eric Wang

name: BrowserArena: Evaluating LLM Agents on Real-World Web Navigation Tasks
summary: Introduces BrowserArena, a live-web platform for head-to-head agent comparisons on user-submitted tasks. Step-level human annotations support targeted analysis of navigation, pop-up handling and CAPTCHA-related failures.
authors: Sagnik Anupam; Davis Brown; Shuo Li; Eric Wong; Hamed Hassani; Osbert Bastani

name: FocusAgent: Simple Yet Effective Ways of Trimming the Large Context of Web Agents
summary: Introduces FocusAgent, which uses a lightweight LLM to select task-relevant lines from web agents' accessibility-tree observations, reducing context size and exposure to prompt injection.
authors: Imene Kerboua; Sahar Omidi Shayegan; Megh Thakkar; Xing Han Lù; Léo Boisvert; Massimo Caccia; Jérémy Espinas; Alexandre Aussem; Véronique Eglin; Alexandre Lacoste

name: Improving GUI Grounding with Explicit Position-to-Coordinate Mapping
summary: This work addresses GUI localization errors caused by mismatches between visual patch positions and output pixel coordinates. RULER tokens provide explicit coordinate references, while Interleaved MRoPE balances width and height encoding; evaluation uses the ScreenSpot benchmark family.
authors: Suyuchen Wang; Tianyu Zhang; Ahmed Masry; Christopher Pal; Spandana Gella; Bang Liu; Perouz Taslakian

name: WAREX: Web Agent Reliability Evaluation on Existing Benchmarks
summary: WAREX augments existing web-agent benchmarks with reliability challenges arising from unstable systems and changing or disruptive website behavior. Evaluation on WebArena, WebVoyager and REAL examines how these disturbances affect task completion.
authors: Su Kara; Fazle Faisal; Suman Nath

name: Learning Efficient Guardrails for Compliance
summary: Introduces PolicyGuardBench for detecting policy violations in full web-agent trajectories and their prefixes, and trains PolicyGuard as an efficient guardrail model.
authors: Xiaofei Wen; Wenjie Jacky Mo; Yanan Xie; Peng Qi; Muhao Chen

name: Cross-Modal Content Optimization for Steering Web Agent Preferences
summary: Introduces Cross-Modal Preference Steering (CPS), a black-box attack that edits a listing's images and text to steer VLM-based web agents' selections.
authors: Tanqiu Jiang; Min Bai; Nikolaos Pappas; Yanjun Qi; Sandesh Swamy

name: \textsc{GUI-Spotlight}: Adaptive Iterative Focus Refinement for Enhanced GUI Visual Grounding
summary: GUI-Spotlight trains a grounding model to reason over images and call tools that iteratively narrow its visual focus. The paper evaluates this refinement method on ScreenSpot-Pro after training on 18,500 samples.
authors: Bin Lei; Nuo Xu; Ali Payani; Mingyi Hong; Chunhua Liao; Yu Cao; Caiwen Ding

name: JEF-Hinter: Leveraging Offline Knowledge for Improving Web Agents Adaptation
summary: Introduces JEF-Hinter, which distills successful and failed trajectories into compact episodic hints and retrieves them for the current agent state. Web benchmark experiments examine guidance from decisive steps.
authors: Hadi Nekoei; Aman Jaiswal; Patrice Bechard; Oleh Shliazhko; Orlando Marquez Ayala; Mathieu Reymond; Massimo Caccia; Alexandre Drouin; Sarath Chandar; Alexandre Lacoste

name: Understanding User Experiences of Computer Use Agents: Design Space and Opportunities for Building Agent UX Prototypes
summary: Maps design considerations for computer-use agent experiences and introduces AgentUXlab, a browser-based probe for prototyping and evaluating agent UX on a website.
authors: Jenny T. Liang; Titus Barik; Jeffrey Nichols; Eldon Schoop; Ruijia Cheng

name: 3Dify: a Framework for Procedural 3D-CG Generation Assisted by LLMs Using MCP and RAG
summary: Introduces 3Dify, a natural-language 3D graphics framework that operates creation tools through MCP and uses a computer-using agent for GUI operations when MCP is unavailable.
authors: Shun-ichiro Hayashi; Daichi Mukunoki; Tetsuya Hoshino; Satoshi Ohshima; Takahiro Katagiri

name: From Imperative to Declarative: Towards LLM-friendly OS Interfaces for Boosted Computer-Use Agents
summary: Introduces a Declarative Model Interface that maps existing GUIs to access, state and observation primitives while handling low-level interactions. Evaluation uses Word, PowerPoint and Excel on Windows with a GUI-agent baseline.
authors: Yuan Wang; Mingyu Li; Haibo Chen

name: Watch and Learn: Learning to Use Computers from Online Videos
summary: Introduces Watch & Learn (W&L), which converts human computer-use videos into UI action trajectories by predicting actions between consecutive screen states.
authors: Chan Hee Song; Yiwen Song; Palash Goyal; Yu Su; Oriana Riva; Hamid Palangi; Tomas Pfister

name: GUISpector: An MLLM Agent Framework for Automated Verification of Natural Language Requirements in GUI Prototypes
summary: Introduces GUISpector, an MLLM agent framework that operates GUI prototypes to check natural-language requirements and produces feedback for developers.
authors: Kristian Kolthoff; Felix Kretzer; Simone Paolo Ponzetto; Alexander Maedche; Christian Bartelt

name: Demystifying deep search: a holistic evaluation with hint-free multi-hop questions and factorised metrics
summary: Introduces WebDetective, a deep-search benchmark with a traceable Wikipedia sandbox, and EvidenceLoop, an evidence-tracking workflow for web-agent search and synthesis.
authors: Maojia Song; Renhang Liu; Xinyu Wang; Yong Jiang; Pengjun Xie; Fei Huang; Jingren Zhou; Dorien Herremans; Soujanya Poria

name: Agent+P: Guiding UI Agents via Symbolic Planning
summary: Guides UI agents with symbolic planning over a UI transition graph initialized from app-code analysis and updated through online exploration, with evaluation on AndroidWorld.
authors: Shang Ma; Xusheng Xiao; Yanfang Ye

name: A Multimodal GUI Architecture for Interfacing with LLM-Based Conversational Assistants
summary: Presents an MCP architecture that exposes an application's GUI navigation graph and view-specific tools to speech-enabled LLM assistants for voice interaction.
authors: Hans G. W. van Dam

name: Your Harness is Not Secure: Benchmarking Real-world Threat of Command Line Interface Agent
summary: Introduces AdvCLI, a sandbox benchmark for evaluating whether command-line agents carry out security-relevant operating-system tasks across multiple hosts.
authors: Weidi Luo; Qiming Zhang; Tianyu Lu; Xiaogeng Liu; Bin Hu; Hung-Chun Chiu; Siyuan Ma; Yizhe Zhang; Xusheng Xiao; Yinzhi Cao; Zhen Xiang; Chaowei Xiao

name: Invisible to Humans, Triggered by Agents: Stealthy Jailbreak Attacks on Mobile Vision-Language Agents
summary: Uses the near-zero contact-touch signals of automated mobile agents to expose malicious visual content selectively during agent interactions. The paper combines this agent-only perceptual injection with HG-IDA* prompt optimization to study unauthorized cross-app actions.
authors: Renhua Ding; Xiao Yang; Zhengwei Fang; Jun Luo; Kun He; Jun Zhu

name: ReInAgent: A Context-Aware GUI Agent Enabling Human-in-the-Loop Mobile Task Navigation
summary: Introduces ReInAgent, coordinating information management, planning, and reflection around a shared memory for mobile tasks. It proactively asks users for information and checks consistency when instructions are ambiguous or change during execution.
authors: Haitao Jia; Ming He; Zimo Yin; Likang Wu; Jianping Fan; Jitao Sang

name: Auto-scaling Continuous Memory for GUI Agent
summary: Encodes GUI trajectories into compact continuous embeddings that can be retrieved directly into an agent’s input. An automated environment-discovery and rollout pipeline expands this memory for long tasks and unfamiliar interfaces.
authors: Wenyi Wu; Kun Zhou; Ruoxin Yuan; Vivian Yu; Stephen Wang; Zhiting Hu; Biwei Huang

name: WARC-Bench: Web Archive Based Benchmark for GUI Subtask Executions
summary: WARC-Bench packages dynamic web pages as replayable archives and evaluates short navigation subtasks involving components such as date pickers and scrollable containers. It also studies supervised training followed by reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards on these browser interactions.
authors: Sanjari Srivastava; Gang Li; Cheng Chang; Rishu Garg; Manpreet Kaur; Charlene Y. Lee; Yuezhang Li; Yining Mao; Ignacio Cases; Yanan Xie; Peng Qi

name: ALLOY: Generating Reusable Agent Workflows from User Demonstration
summary: Introduces ALLOY, which turns user demonstrations into editable, reusable workflows for LLM-based web agents carrying out preference-dependent tasks.
authors: Jiawen Li; Zheng Ning; Yuan Tian; Toby Jia-jun Li

name: SecureWebArena: A Holistic Security Evaluation Benchmark for LVLM-based Web Agents
summary: Introduces SecureWebArena with simulated interactive websites, an attack-vector taxonomy and labeled agent trajectories. Its evaluation separates failures in reasoning, behavioral traces and task outcomes across vision-language agent families.
authors: Zonghao Ying; Yangguang Shao; Jianle Gan; Gan Xu; Wenxin Zhang; Quanchen Zou; Junzheng Shi; Zhenfei Yin; Mingchuan Zhang; Aishan Liu; Xianglong Liu

name: BrowserAgent: Building Web Agents with Human-Inspired Web Browsing Actions
summary: Trains BrowserAgent to use Playwright-based scrolling, clicking and typing directly on webpages for information-seeking tasks. Supervised and rejection fine-tuning are paired with explicit memory for conclusions carried across steps.
authors: Tao Yu; Zhengbo Zhang; Zhiheng Lyu; Junhao Gong; Hongzhu Yi; Xinming Wang; Yuxuan Zhou; Jiabing Yang; Ping Nie; Yan Huang; Wenhu Chen

name: SusBench: An Online Benchmark for Evaluating Dark Pattern Susceptibility of Computer-Use Agents
summary: Introduces SusBench, an online benchmark that inserts dark-pattern designs into consumer websites for agent evaluation. A human study checks the realism of the interventions, and agent trials compare susceptibility across pattern types.
authors: Longjie Guo; Chenjie Yuan; Mingyuan Zhong; Robert Wolfe; Ruican Zhong; Yue Xu; Bingbing Wen; Hua Shen; Lucy Lu Wang; Alexis Hiniker

name: WebRouter: Query-specific Router via Variational Information Bottleneck for Cost-sensitive Web Agent
summary: Introduces WebRouter, a cost-aware router that compresses web-agent prompts to choose among LLMs, with cost and accuracy measured on WebVoyager websites.
authors: Tao Li; Jinlong Hu; Yang Wang; Junfeng Liu; Xuejun Liu

name: R-WoM: Retrieval-augmented World Model For Computer-use Agents
summary: R-WoM evaluates how well world models predict nearby GUI states, align complete procedures, and recognize milestone transitions. It retrieves external tutorials to guide simulated future interactions, with experiments on subsets of OSWorld and WebArena.
authors: Kai Mei; Jiang Guo; Shuaichen Chang; Mingwen Dong; Dongkyu Lee; Xing Niu; Jiarong Jiang

name: HackWorld: Evaluating Computer-Use Agents on Exploiting Web Application Vulnerabilities
summary: Introduces HackWorld for evaluating visual computer-use agents in a capture-the-flag collection of web applications. The benchmark examines interface navigation and multistep planning during vulnerability discovery and exploitation tasks.
authors: Xiaoxue Ren; Penghao Jiang; Kaixin Li; Zhiyong Huang; Xiaoning Du; Jiaojiao Jiang; Zhenchang Xing; Jiamou Sun; Terry Yue Zhuo

name: Detect Anything via Next Point Prediction
summary: Introduces Rex-Omni, a general visual perception model trained for coordinate prediction; GUI grounding is one capability evaluated alongside detection and OCR.
authors: Qing Jiang; Junan Huo; Xingyu Chen; Yuda Xiong; Zhaoyang Zeng; Yihao Chen; Tianhe Ren; Junzhi Yu; Lei Zhang

name: In-Browser LLM-Guided Fuzzing for Real-Time Prompt Injection Testing in Agentic AI Browsers
summary: Proposes an in-browser fuzzing framework that uses language-model guidance to test indirect prompt-injection vulnerabilities in agentic browsers. The work focuses on unwanted actions triggered by webpage instructions under the browser agent's user privileges.
authors: Avihay Cohen

name: ReUseIt: Synthesizing Reusable AI Agent Workflows for Web Automation
summary: Introduces ReUseIt, which synthesizes reusable web-agent workflows from successful and failed attempts and adds guards to detect and fix execution errors.
authors: Yimeng Liu; Misha Sra; Jeevana Priya Inala; Chenglong Wang

name: Hi-Agent: Hierarchical Vision-Language Agents for Mobile Device Control
summary: Introduces Hi-Agent, jointly training a high-level reasoning model and a low-level mobile action model. Execution feedback supplies a foresight advantage for optimizing subgoal decisions, with evaluations on Android control benchmarks.

name: WebAggregator: Enhancing Compositional Reasoning Capabilities of Deep Research Agent Foundation Models
summary: Introduces WebAggregator, a pipeline for synthesizing compositional questions from websites to train deep-research agents, plus the WebAggregatorQA testbed.
authors: Rui Wang; Ce Zhang; Jun-Yu Ma; Jianshu Zhang; Hongru Wang; Yi Chen; Boyang Xue; Tianqing Fang; Zhisong Zhang; Hongming Zhang; Haitao Mi; Dong Yu; Kam-Fai Wong

name: State Your Intention to Steer Your Attention: An AI Assistant for Intentional Digital Living
summary: Introduces an assistant that reads screenshots, application titles, and URLs to compare computer activity with a user's stated intention and send notifications when it diverges.
authors: Juheon Choi; Juyong Lee; Jian Kim; Chanyoung Kim; Taywon Min; W. Bradley Knox; Min Kyung Lee; Kimin Lee

name: Agentic Entropy-Balanced Policy Optimization
summary: Introduces Agentic Entropy-Balanced Policy Optimization (AEPO), an RL method that adjusts rollout sampling and policy updates for tool-using web agents.
authors: Guanting Dong; Licheng Bao; Zhongyuan Wang; Kangzhi Zhao; Xiaoxi Li; Jiajie Jin; Jinghan Yang; Hangyu Mao; Fuzheng Zhang; Kun Gai; Guorui Zhou; Yutao Zhu; Ji-Rong Wen; Zhicheng Dou

name: ColorBench: Benchmarking Mobile Agents with Graph-Structured Framework for Complex Long-Horizon Tasks
summary: ColorBench represents mobile tasks as graphs of states collected from real devices, providing a quasi-dynamic environment with multiple valid paths and error paths. It evaluates single-app and cross-app tasks using completion, subtask progress, and atomic diagnostics.
authors: Yuanyi Song; Heyuan Huang; Qiqiang Lin; Yin Zhao; Xiangmou Qu; Jun Wang; Xingyu Lou; Weiwen Liu; Zhuosheng Zhang; Jun Wang; Yong Yu; Weinan Zhang; Zhaoxiang Wang

name: LLMs as Scalable, General-Purpose Simulators For Evolving Digital Agent Training
summary: Introduces UI-Simulator, which generates UI states and transitions for agent-training trajectories, and UI-Simulator-Grow, which prioritizes tasks and trajectory variants.
authors: Yiming Wang; Da Yin; Yuedong Cui; Ruichen Zheng; Zhiqian Li; Zongyu Lin; Di Wu; Xueqing Wu; Chenchen Ye; Yu Zhou; Kai-Wei Chang

name: CORE: Reducing UI Exposure in Mobile Agents via Collaboration Between Cloud and Local LLMs
summary: Introduces CORE, which divides mobile UI hierarchies into semantic blocks and shares planning between local and cloud language models. Local ranking limits the screen information sent for cloud-side element selection, with a multi-round mechanism for correcting inadequate context.
authors: Gucongcong Fan; Chaoyue Niu; Chengfei Lyu; Fan Wu; Guihai Chen

name: PolySkill: Learning Generalizable Skills Through Polymorphic Abstraction
summary: Introduces PolySkill, which separates a web-agent skill's goal from its execution so agents can learn and reuse skills across websites.
authors: Simon Yu; Gang Li; Weiyan Shi; Peng Qi

name: GUIrilla: A Scalable Framework for Automated Desktop UI Exploration
summary: GUIrilla systematically explores macOS interfaces to collect interaction traces and accessibility metadata for downstream GUI research. It organizes these observations into hierarchical MacApp Trees and describes an accessibility-driven collection library.
authors: Sofiya Garkot; Maksym Shamrai; Ivan Synytsia; Mariya Hirna

name: WEBSERV: A Full-Stack and RL-Ready Web Environment for Training Web Agents at Scale
summary: WebServ combines copy-on-write container environments with a compact DOM-derived browser interface for training web agents. Network-aware waiting supports action execution in single-page applications, with evaluations and reinforcement-learning experiments on WebArena-Lite.
authors: Yuxuan Lu; Ziyi Wang; Jing Huang; Hui Liu; Jiri Gesi; Yan Han; Shihan Fu; Tianqi Zheng; Xianfeng Tang; Chen Luo; Yisi Sang; Jin Lai; Dakuo Wang

name: Beyond Pipelines: A Survey of the Paradigm Shift toward Model-Native Agentic AI
summary: Surveys model-native agentic AI and the role of RL in learned planning, tool use and memory, covering GUI agents as one application alongside deep-research agents.
authors: Jitao Sang; Jinlin Xiao; Jiarun Han; Jilin Chen; Xiaoyi Chen; Shuyu Wei; Yongjie Sun; Yuhang Wang

name: UltraCUA: A Foundation Model for Computer Use Agents with Hybrid Action
summary: UltraCUA trains a shared policy for primitive GUI actions and high-level tool calls using synthesized tasks and hybrid trajectories. Supervised fine-tuning followed by online reinforcement learning is evaluated on OSWorld and WindowsAgentArena.
authors: Yuhao Yang; Zhen Yang; Zi-Yi Dou; Anh Nguyen; Keen You; Omar Attia; Andrew Szot; Michael Feng; Ram Ramrakhya; Alexander Toshev; Chao Huang; Yinfei Yang; Zhe Gan

name: Investigating the Impact of Dark Patterns on LLM-Based Web Agents
summary: Presents LiteAgent for recording web-agent interactions and TrickyArena for enabling or disabling dark patterns in controlled websites. Experiments compare how individual patterns, combined patterns and visual or HTML changes affect agent decisions.
authors: Devin Ersoy; Brandon Lee; Ananth Shreekumar; Arjun Arunasalam; Muhammad Ibrahim; Antonio Bianchi; Z. Berkay Celik

name: Genesis: Evolving Attack Strategies for LLM Web Agent Red-Teaming
summary: Introduces Genesis, a red-teaming framework that generates adversarial injections for web agents and revises attack strategies using responses and interaction logs.
authors: Zheng Zhang; Jiarui He; Yuchen Cai; Deheng Ye; Peilin Zhao; Ruili Feng; Hao Wang

name: AndroidControl-Curated: Revealing the True Potential of GUI Agents through Benchmark Purification
summary: AndroidControl-Curated audits ambiguities and factual errors in AndroidControl and produces a refined evaluation dataset. The paper also studies post-training a small Magma-R1 model on a curated subset to examine the effect of data quality on GUI action assessment.
authors: Ho Fai Leung; Xiaoyan Xi; Fei Zuo

name: CUARewardBench: A Benchmark for Evaluating Reward Models on Computer-using Agent
summary: Introduces CUARewardBench for evaluating outcome and process reward models on annotated computer-use trajectories, plus Unanimous Prompt Ensemble (UPE) for reward judgments.
authors: Haojia Lin; Xiaoyu Tan; Yulei Qin; Zihan Xu; Yuchen Shi; Zongyi Li; Gang Li; Shaofei Cai; Siqi Cai; Chaoyou Fu; Ke Li; Xing Sun

name: WebGraphEval: Multi-Turn Trajectory Evaluation for Web Agents using Graph Representation
summary: Introduces WebGraphEval, which merges multiple agents' trajectories into a weighted graph of canonical actions. Structural analyses examine recurring behavior, inefficient paths and important decision points beyond a final success score.
authors: Yaoyao Qian; Yuanli Wang; Jinda Zhang; Yun Zong; Meixu Chen; Hanhan Zhou; Jindan Huang; Yifan Zeng; Xinyu Hu; Chan Hee Song; Danqing Zhang

name: See, Think, Act: Online Shopper Behavior Simulation with VLM Agents
summary: Studies online shopper action prediction with VLM agents using webpage screenshots, HTML, and action history from OPeRA, trained with SFT and hierarchical RL rewards.
authors: Yimeng Zhang; Jiri Gesi; Ran Xue; Tian Wang; Ziyi Wang; Yuxuan Lu; Sinong Zhan; Huimin Zeng; Qingjun Cui; Yufan Guo; Jing Huang; Mubarak Shah; Dakuo Wang

name: SheetBrain: A Neuro-Symbolic Agent for Accurate Reasoning over Complex and Large Spreadsheets
summary: Introduces SheetBrain, a spreadsheet question-answering and manipulation agent that uses a Python sandbox and Excel tools, plus the SheetBench benchmark.
authors: Ziwei Wang; Jiayuan Su; Mengyu Zhou; Huaxing Zeng; Mengni Jia; Xiao Lv; Haoyu Dong; Xiaojun Ma; Shi Han; Dongmei Zhang

name: ColorAgent: Building A Robust, Personalized, and Interactive OS Agent
summary: Presents ColorAgent, an operating system agent for long-horizon user instructions, trained with step-wise RL and self-evolving training and evaluated on AndroidWorld and AndroidLab.
authors: Ning Li; Qiqiang Lin; Zheng Wu; Xiaoyun Mo; Weiming Zhang; Yin Zhao; Xiangmou Qu; Jiamu Zhou; Jun Wang; Congmin Zheng; Yuanyi Song; Hongjiang Chen; Heyuan Huang; Jihong Wang; Jiaxin Yin; Jingwei Yu; Junwei Liao; Qiuying Peng; Xingyu Lou; Jun Wang; Weiwen Liu; Zhuosheng Zhang; Weinan Zhang

name: VideoAgentTrek: Computer Use Pretraining from Unlabeled Videos
summary: Extracts structured GUI actions from screen-recorded tutorials using inverse dynamics, then uses the inferred trajectories for computer-use training.
authors: Dunjie Lu; Yiheng Xu; Junli Wang; Haoyuan Wu; Xinyuan Wang; Zekun Wang; Junlin Yang; Hongjin Su; Jixuan Chen; Junda Chen; Yuchen Mao; Jingren Zhou; Junyang Lin; Binyuan Hui; Tao Yu

name: Branch-and-Browse: Efficient and Controllable Web Exploration with Tree-Structured Reasoning and Action Memory
summary: Branch-and-Browse is a web agent framework that uses tree-structured subtasks, web state replay, and page action memory to explore and complete tasks.
authors: Shiqi He; Yue Cui; Xinyu Ma; Yaliang Li; Bolin Ding; Mosharaf Chowdhury

name: Surfer 2: The Next Generation of Cross-Platform Computer Use Agents
summary: Surfer2 combines hierarchical context management with separate planning and execution, self-verification, and recovery for visual computer use. It evaluates the framework across web, desktop, and Android tasks without task-specific fine-tuning.
authors: Mathieu Andreux; Märt Bakler; Yanael Barbier; Hamza Benchekroun; Emilien Biré; Antoine Bonnet; Riaz Bordie; Nathan Bout; Matthias Brunel; Aleix Cambray; Pierre-Louis Cedoz; Antoine Chassang; Gautier Cloix; Ethan Connelly; Alexandra Constantinou; Ramzi De Coster; Hubert de la Jonquiere; Aurélien Delfosse; Maxime Delpit; Alexis Deprez; Augustin Derupti; Mathieu Diaz; Shannon D'Souza; Julie Dujardin; Abai Edmund; Michael Eickenberg; Armand Fatalot; Wissem Felissi; Isaac Herring; Xavier Koegler; Erwan Le Jumeau de Kergaradec; Aurélien Lac; Maxime Langevin; Corentin Lauverjat; Antonio Loison; Avshalom Manevich; Axel Moyal; Axel Nguyen Kerbel; Marinela Parovic; Julien Revelle; Guillaume Richard; Mats Richter; Ronan Riochet; María Santos; Romain Savidan; Laurent Sifre; Maxime Theillard; Marc Thibault; Ivan Valentini; Tony Wu; Laura Yie; Kai Yuan; Jevgenij Zubovskij

name: UI-Ins: Enhancing GUI Grounding with Multi-Perspective Instruction-as-Reasoning
summary: Treats alternative instruction formulations as reasoning paths and trains GUI-grounding models to select and combine useful perspectives.
authors: Liangyu Chen; Hanzhang Zhou; Chenglin Cai; Jianan Zhang; Panrong Tong; Quyu Kong; Xu Zhang; Chen Liu; Yuqi Liu; Wenxuan Wang; Yue Wang; Qin Jin; Steven Hoi

name: GhostEI-Bench: Do Mobile Agents Resilience to Environmental Injection in Dynamic On-Device Environments?
summary: Introduces GhostEI-Bench, a benchmark that injects deceptive UI events into Android emulator workflows to assess mobile agents and analyze failures from actions and screenshots.
authors: Chiyu Chen; Xinhao Song; Yunkai Chai; Yang Yao; Haodong Zhao; Lijun Li; Jie Li; Yan Teng; Gongshen Liu; Yingchun Wang

name: Mixing Importance with Diversity: Joint Optimization for KV Cache Compression in Large Vision-Language Models
summary: MixKV compresses vision-language model KV caches by balancing importance and diversity; its evaluations include GUI grounding alongside broader multimodal tasks.
authors: Xuyang Liu; Xiyan Gui; Yuchao Zhang; Linfeng Zhang

name: OpenPhone: Mobile Agentic Foundation Models
summary: OpenPhone trains a compact mobile policy with supervised learning followed by GRPO on synthetic GUI data, incorporating reasoning and memory management. Its device-cloud design handles routine work locally and delegates complex subtasks, with online evaluation on AndroidLab.
authors: Yangqin Jiang; Chao Huang

name: Mitigating Coordinate Prediction Bias from Positional Encoding Failures
summary: Introduces Vision-PE Shuffle Guidance (VPSG), a training-free correction for coordinate drift in visual models, evaluated for localization on ScreenSpot-Pro.
authors: Xingjian Tao; Yiwei Wang; Yujun Cai; Yihong Luo; Kai Han; Jing Tang

name: WebATLAS: An LLM Agent with Experience-Driven Memory and Action Simulation
summary: WebATLAS is a web agent that stores interaction outcomes and simulates candidate actions before acting, using past experience to plan navigation on unseen websites.
authors: Jiali Cheng; Anjishnu Kumar; Roshan Lal; Rishi Rajasekaran; Hani Ramezani; Omar Zia Khan; Oleg Rokhlenko; Sunny Chiu-Webster; Gang Hua; Hadi Amiri

name: MGA: Memory-Driven GUI Agent for Observation-Centric Interaction
summary: Introduces MGA, which separates task-agnostic screen-state reading from decision making and connects steps through structured state memory. Validated state deltas replace full trajectory replay, evaluated on OSWorld and application tasks.
authors: Weihua Cheng; Junming Liu; Yifei Sun; Botian Shi; Yirong Chen; Ding Wang

name: OS-Sentinel: Towards Safety-Enhanced Mobile GUI Agents via Hybrid Validation in Realistic Workflows
summary: Introduces MobileRisk-Live and OS-Sentinel, combining a formal verifier for system-level violations with a multimodal judge for contextual risks in mobile GUI workflows.
authors: Qiushi Sun; Mukai Li; Zhoumianze Liu; Zhihui Xie; Fangzhi Xu; Zhangyue Yin; Kanzhi Cheng; Zehao Li; Zichen Ding; Qi Liu; Zhiyong Wu; Zhuosheng Zhang; Ben Kao; Lingpeng Kong

name: OSWorld-MCP: Benchmarking MCP Tool Invocation In Computer-Use Agents
summary: OSWorld-MCP evaluates how agents choose between GUI operations and MCP tool calls in computer tasks. It combines generated and curated tools, with 158 manually validated tools across seven applications, to examine tool use alongside task completion.
authors: Hongrui Jia; Jitong Liao; Xi Zhang; Haiyang Xu; Tianbao Xie; Chaoya Jiang; Ming Yan; Si Liu; Wei Ye; Fei Huang

name: Agent Data Protocol: Unifying Datasets for Diverse, Effective Fine-tuning of LLM Agents
summary: The agent data protocol (ADP) provides a shared format for agent training data across browsing, tool use, coding, and other tasks, including web agent workflows.
authors: Yueqi Song; Ketan Ramaneti; Zaid Sheikh; Ziru Chen; Boyu Gou; Tianbao Xie; Yiheng Xu; Danyang Zhang; Apurva Gandhi; Fan Yang; Joseph Liu; Tianyue Ou; Zhihao Yuan; Frank Xu; Shuyan Zhou; Xingyao Wang; Xiang Yue; Tao Yu; Huan Sun; Yu Su; Graham Neubig

name: GUI Knowledge Bench: Revealing the Knowledge Gap of VLMs in GUI Tasks
summary: GUI Knowledge Bench tests knowledge of widgets, interactions, and procedures across six named platforms and 292 applications to assess VLMs used for GUI tasks.
authors: Chenrui Shi; Zedong Yu; Zhi Gao; Ruining Feng; Enqi Liu; Yuwei Wu; Yunde Jia; Liuyu Xiang; Zhaofeng He; Qing Li
environments: web; desktop; windows; macos; linux; android; ios; cross-platform

name: Measuring the Security of Mobile LLM Agents under Adversarial Prompts from Untrusted Third-Party Channels
summary: Measures how untrusted third-party notifications, messages, and app content can hijack mobile LLM agents into executing unauthorized cross-app actions.
authors: Chenghao Du; Quanfeng Huang; Tingxuan Tang; Zihao Wang; Adwait Nadkarni; Yue Xiao

name: GUI-Rise: Structured Reasoning and History Summarization for GUI Navigation
summary: Combines structured progress-and-decision reasoning with history summarization to improve cross-domain generalization in GUI navigation agents.
authors: Tao Liu; Chongyu Wang; Rongjie Li; Yingchen Yu; Xuming He; Bai Song

name: Enhancing Trustworthy GUI Grounding via Self-Critiqued Reinforcement Learning
summary: HyperClick trains GUI grounders to produce a click and an accompanying confidence estimate using rewards for correctness and confidence alignment. Its evaluation examines localization, calibration, and abstention behavior.
authors: Shaojie Zhang; Pei Fu; Ruoceng Zhang; Jiahui Yang; Anan Du; Xiuwen Xi; Shaokang Wang; Ying Huang; Bin Qin; Zhenbo Luo; Jian Luan

name: GUI-AIMA: Aligning Intrinsic Multimodal Attention with a Context Anchor for GUI Grounding
summary: Introduces GUI-AIMA, which supervises instruction-relevant attention over visual patches. Patch-level grounding can be combined with an optional zoom stage and is evaluated across GUI localization benchmarks.
authors: Shijie Zhou; Viet Dac Lai; Hao Tan; Jihyung Kil; Wanrong Zhu; Changyou Chen; Ruiyi Zhang

name: Scaling Agent Learning via Experience Synthesis
summary: DreamGym synthesizes agent experiences with a reasoning-based environment model for online RL; its evaluations include the web task setting WebArena.
authors: Zhaorun Chen; Zhuokai Zhao; Kai Zhang; Bo Liu; Qi Qi; Yifan Wu; Tarun Kalluri; Sara Cao; Yuanhao Xiong; Haibo Tong; Huaxiu Yao; Hengduo Li; Jiacheng Zhu; Xian Li; Dawn Song; Bo Li; Jason Weston; Dat Huynh

name: Learning from Online Videos at Inference Time for Computer-Use Agents
summary: This work retrieves online video tutorials and converts them into structured GUI action demonstrations with short objectives. A two-stage selection process supplies a relevant local trajectory as in-context guidance at each execution step.
authors: Yujian Liu; Ze Wang; Hao Chen; Ximeng Sun; Xiaodong Yu; Jialian Wu; Jiang Liu; Emad Barsoum; Zicheng Liu; Shiyu Chang

name: GUI-360$^\circ$: A Comprehensive Dataset and Benchmark for Computer-Using Agents
summary: Collects Windows application trajectories with screenshots and action traces for grounding, screen parsing, and action prediction.
authors: Jian Mu; Chaoyun Zhang; Chiming Ni; Lu Wang; Bo Qiao; Kartik Mathur; Qianhui Wu; Yuhang Xie; Xiaojun Ma; Mengyu Zhou; Si Qin; Liqun Li; Yu Kang; Minghua Ma; Qingwei Lin; Saravan Rajmohan; Dongmei Zhang

name: SynthAgent: Adapting Web Agents with Synthetic Supervision
summary: Introduces SynthAgent, which generates tasks by exploring website elements and refines them when observations reveal conflicts. A later trajectory-refinement stage removes misaligned behavior before fine-tuning agents for the target websites.
authors: Zhaoyang Wang; Yiming Liang; Xuchao Zhang; Qianhui Wu; Siwei Han; Anson Bastos; Rujia Wang; Chetan Bansal; Baolin Peng; Jianfeng Gao; Saravan Rajmohan; Huaxiu Yao

name: WebVIA: A Web-based Vision-Language Agentic Framework for Interactive and Verifiable UI-to-Code Generation
summary: WebVIA combines a web UI exploration agent, interactive UI-to-Code generation, and validation of generated code's interactivity.
authors: Mingde Xu; Zhen Yang; Wenyi Hong; Lihang Pan; Xinyue Fan; Yan Wang; Xiaotao Gu; Bin Xu; Jie Tang

name: AUTO-Explorer: Automated Data Collection for GUI Agent
summary: Introduces Auto-Explorer, an automated GUI exploration method that records software states for training-data collection. UIXplore evaluates exploration coverage, and collected data is used to fine-tune and test GUI element grounding.
authors: Xiangwu Guo; Difei Gao; Mike Zheng Shou

name: Grounding Computer Use Agents on Human Demonstrations
summary: GroundCUA turns expert desktop demonstrations into densely annotated screenshots and grounding instructions. The GroundNext model family uses this supervision and subsequent reinforcement learning, with both grounding benchmarks and an OSWorld agent configuration used for evaluation.
authors: Aarash Feizi; Shravan Nayak; Xiangru Jian; Kevin Qinghong Lin; Kaixin Li; Rabiul Awal; Xing Han Lù; Johan Obando-Ceron; Juan A. Rodriguez; Nicolas Chapados; David Vazquez; Adriana Romero-Soriano; Reihaneh Rabbany; Perouz Taslakian; Christopher Pal; Spandana Gella; Sai Rajeswar

name: An Efficient Training Pipeline for Reasoning Graphical User Interface Agents
summary: A GUI grounding pipeline filters 4.8M synthetic examples to 12K training instances and adapts a 3B vision-language model, evaluated on ScreenSpot, Multimodal-Mind2Web, and AndroidControl.
authors: Georgios Pantazopoulos; Eda B. Özyiğit

name: AgentPRM: Process Reward Models for LLM Agents via Step-Wise Promise and Progress
summary: AgentPRM scores sequential agent decisions by their promise and progress toward a goal, with web shopping and browser navigation among the motivating tasks.
authors: Zhiheng Xi; Chenyang Liao; Guanyu Li; Yajie Yang; Wenxiang Chen; Zhihao Zhang; Binghai Wang; Senjie Jin; Yuhao Zhou; Jian Guan; Wei Wu; Tao Ji; Tao Gui; Qi Zhang; Xuanjing Huang

name: History-Aware Reasoning for GUI Agents
summary: HAR-GUI combines episodic reasoning and short-term memory to use earlier interactions when selecting GUI actions. Its training constructs reflective scenarios and correction guidance and applies a hybrid reinforcement-learning reward to the 3B policy.
authors: Ziwei Wang; Leyang Yang; Xiaoxuan Tang; Sheng Zhou; Dajun Chen; Wei Jiang; Yong Li

name: ProBench: Benchmarking GUI Agents with Accurate Process Information
summary: ProBench extends mobile GUI evaluation with tasks whose correctness depends on the interaction process as well as the final state. Its ProcessProvider supplies process information for assessing agent behavior and analyzing failure modes.
authors: Leyang Yang; Ziwei Wang; Xiaoxuan Tang; Sheng Zhou; Dajun Chen; Wei Jiang; Yong Li

name: TaskSense: Cognitive Chain Modeling and Difficulty Estimation for GUI Tasks
summary: Cognitive Chain estimates GUI task difficulty by extracting sequences of cognitive steps from execution traces, then uses those estimates to assess GUI agents.
authors: Yiwen Yin; Zhian Hu; Xiaoxi Xu; Chun Yu; Xintong Wu; Wenyu Fan; Yuanchun Shi

name: Co-EPG: A Framework for Co-Evolution of Planning and Grounding in Autonomous GUI Agents
summary: Co-EPG alternates reinforcement learning for a planner with updates to a grounding model using generated training examples. The evolving grounder provides feedback to the planner, and evaluation uses Multimodal Mind2Web and AndroidControl.
authors: Yuan Zhao; Hualei Zhu; Tingyu Jiang; Shen Li; Xiaohang Xu; Hao Henry Wang

name: OSGym: Scalable OS Infra for Computer Use Agents
summary: OSGym supplies full operating-system sandboxes with GUIs for parallel computer-use data collection and training. It combines per-replica state management, hardware-aware orchestration, copy-on-write virtual-machine disks, and layered failure recovery.
authors: Zengyi Qin; Jinyuan Chen; Yunze Man; Shengcao Cao; Ziqi Pang; Zhuoyuan Wang; Han Fang; Ling Zhu; Zixin Xie; Zibu Wei; Tianshu Ran; Haoran Geng; Ray Pan; Qizhen Sun; Zachary Bright; Yuyang Cai; Chongye Yang; Jiace Zhao; Tianrui Liu; Han Cao; Yeyang Zhou; Rui Wang; Song Wang; Xiang Ren; Bo Zhang; Yutong Ban; Pieter Abbeel; Brian Anthony

name: Mobile-Agent-RAG: Driving Smart Multi-Agent Coordination with Contextual Knowledge Empowerment for Long-Horizon Mobile Automation
summary: Uses separate retrieval systems for high-level mobile-task planning and precise interface operations, with a benchmark for extended cross-app tasks.
authors: Yuxiang Zhou; Jichang Li; Yanhao Zhang; Haonan Lu; Guanbin Li

name: WebCoach: Self-Evolving Web Agents with Cross-Session Memory Guidance
summary: Introduces WebCoach, which condenses navigation logs into persistent episodic memory and retrieves experiences by similarity and recency. Runtime hooks selectively supply advice to browser agents, evaluated on WebVoyager without retraining the underlying models.
authors: Genglin Liu; Shijie Geng; Sha Li; Hejie Cui; Sarah Zhang; Xin Liu; Tianyi Liu

name: MEGA-GUI: Multi-stage Enhanced Grounding Agents for GUI Elements
summary: Introduces MEGA-GUI, which separates coarse region selection from fine-grained interface-element grounding. Bidirectional zooming and context-aware instruction rewriting coordinate specialized vision-language agents across visual scales.
authors: SeokJoo Kwak; Jihoon Kim; Boyoun Kim; Jung Jae Yoon; Wooseok Jang; Jeonghoon Hong; Jaeho Yang; Yeong-Dae Kwon

name: STEP: Success-Rate-Aware Trajectory-Efficient Policy Optimization
summary: STEP allocates RL sampling by task success rate and trains on individual steps from interaction trajectories, with evaluations on OSWorld and AndroidWorld.
authors: Yuhan Chen; Yuxuan Liu; Long Zhang; Pengzhi Gao; Jian Luan; Wei Liu

name: DualTAP: A Dual-Task Adversarial Protector for Mobile MLLM Agents
summary: Applies dual-task adversarial perturbations to mobile screenshots to conceal personally identifiable information from untrusted MLLM routers while preserving agent task utility.
authors: Fuyao Zhang; Jiaming Zhang; Che Wang; Xiongtao Sun; Yurong Hao; Guowei Guan; Wenjie Li; Longtao Huang; Wei Yang Bryan Lim

name: Can We Stop Malicious AI? KILLBENCH: A Benchmark for External AI Kill Switch Feasibility
summary: KillBench evaluates external prompt-style signals intended to halt maliciously operating web agents, across harmful scenarios and agent configurations.
authors: Sechan Lee; Hyounghun Kim; Sangdon Park

name: Computer-Use Agents as Judges for Generative User Interface
summary: AUI-Gym evaluates generated websites by having computer-use agents attempt tasks whose executability is checked programmatically. A feedback dashboard condenses navigation histories into visual summaries that a coding agent can use to revise an interface.
authors: Kevin Qinghong Lin; Siyuan Hu; Linjie Li; Zhengyuan Yang; Lijuan Wang; Philip Torr; Mike Zheng Shou

name: D-GARA: A Dynamic Benchmarking Framework for GUI Agent Robustness in Real-World Anomalies
summary: D-GARA evaluates Android GUI agents under runtime anomalies such as permission dialogs, battery warnings, and update prompts. Its modular environment embeds these interruptions in Android applications to study recovery and robustness.
authors: Sen Chen; Tong Zhao; Yi Bin; Fei Ma; Wenqi Shao; Zheng Wang

name: UI-CUBE: Enterprise-Grade Computer Use Agent Benchmarking Beyond Task Accuracy to Operational Reliability
summary: UI-CUBE evaluates 226 tasks ranging from individual controls to copy-paste and enterprise workflows. Interface variations, multiple resolutions, and application-state validation support diagnosis of operational reliability beyond task accuracy alone.
authors: Horia Cristescu; Charles Park; Trong Canh Nguyen; Sergiu Talmacel; Alexandru-Gabriel Ilie; Stefan Adam

name: Building Browser Agents: Architecture, Security, and Practical Solutions
summary: Reports architectural and security lessons from building a browser agent, including hybrid accessibility-tree and visual context, browser tooling and programmatic constraints. A WebGames evaluation accompanies the discussion of reliability and specialization.
authors: Aram Vardanyan

name: Fara-7B: An Efficient Agentic Model for Computer Use
summary: Introduces FaraGen synthetic web trajectories, a compact screenshot-based action model, and WebTailBench for underrepresented browser tasks.
authors: Ahmed Awadallah; Yash Lara; Raghav Magazine; Hussein Mozannar; Akshay Nambi; Yash Pandya; Aravind Rajeswaran; Corby Rosset; Alexey Taymanov; Vibhav Vineet; Spencer Whitehead; Andrew Zhao

name: AppSelectBench: Application-Level Tool Selection Benchmark
summary: AppSelectBench evaluates whether computer-using agents choose the right desktop application for a task, using generated user intents and multiple evaluation protocols.
authors: Tianyi Chen; Michael Solodko; Sen Wang; Jongwoo Ko; Junheng Hao; Colby Banbury; Sara Abdali; Saeed Amizadeh; Qing Xiao; Yinheng Li; Tianyu Ding; Kamran Ghasedi Dizaji; Suzhen Zheng; Hao Fan; Justin Wagle; Pashmina Cameron; Kazuhito Koishida

name: "Are We Done Yet?": A Vision-Based Judge for Autonomous Task Completion of Computer Use Agents
summary: This study tests vision-language models as task-completion judges using screenshots and instructions from 42 built-in macOS applications. It evaluates judgment accuracy on human-labeled tasks and separately studies how judge feedback affects agent task success.
authors: Marta Sumyk; Oleksandr Kosovan

name: BrowseSafe: Understanding and Preventing Prompt Injection Within AI Browser Agents
summary: BrowseSafe builds a benchmark of prompt injections in realistic HTML for browser agents and evaluates defenses against attacks that can affect agent actions.
authors: Kaiyuan Zhang; Mark Tenenholtz; Kyle Polley; Jerry Ma; Denis Yarats; Ninghui Li

name: OpenApps: Simulating Environment Variations to Measure UI-Agent Reliability
summary: Introduces OpenApps, a configurable app ecosystem for measuring UI-agent reliability under changes in appearance and content. Its evaluation compares task success and failure behavior across many versions of the same apps.
authors: Karen Ullrich; Jingtong Su; Claudia Shi; Arjun Subramonian; Amir Bar; Ivan Evtimov; Nikolaos Tsilivis; Randall Balestriero; Julia Kempe; Mark Ibrahim

name: Prune4Web: DOM Tree Pruning Programming for Web Agent
summary: Introduces Prune4Web, where generated scoring programs filter DOM elements according to decomposed subtasks before grounding. An annotation pipeline and two-turn training procedure coordinate the planner, programmatic filter and grounder.
authors: Jiayuan Zhang; Kaiquan Chen; Zhihao Lu; Enshen Zhou; Qian Yu; Jing Zhang

name: Qwen3-VL Technical Report
summary: Describes the Qwen3-VL dense and MoE vision-language models, with 256K-token interleaved context, interleaved-MRoPE, DeepStack and textual video timestamps; a general foundation model aimed partly at agentic use.
authors: Shuai Bai; Yuxuan Cai; Ruizhe Chen; Keqin Chen; Xionghui Chen; Zesen Cheng; Lianghao Deng; Wei Ding; Chang Gao; Chunjiang Ge; Wenbin Ge; Zhifang Guo; Qidong Huang; Jie Huang; Fei Huang; Binyuan Hui; Shutong Jiang; Zhaohai Li; Mingsheng Li; Mei Li; Kaixin Li; Zicheng Lin; Junyang Lin; Xuejing Liu; Jiawei Liu; Chenglong Liu; Yang Liu; Dayiheng Liu; Shixuan Liu; Dunjie Lu; Ruilin Luo; Chenxu Lv; Rui Men; Lingchen Meng; Xuancheng Ren; Xingzhang Ren; Sibo Song; Yuchong Sun; Jun Tang; Jianhong Tu; Jianqiang Wan; Peng Wang; Pengfei Wang; Qiuyue Wang; Yuxuan Wang; Tianbao Xie; Yiheng Xu; Haiyang Xu; Jin Xu; Zhibo Yang; Mingkun Yang; Jianxin Yang; An Yang; Bowen Yu; Fei Zhang; Hang Zhang; Xi Zhang; Bo Zheng; Humen Zhong; Jingren Zhou; Fan Zhou; Jing Zhou; Yuanzhi Zhu; Ke Zhu

name: Real-Time Procedural Learning From Experience for AI Agents
summary: PRAXIS stores action outcomes and retrieves past state-action-result examples to guide agent decisions, with evaluation on the REAL web browsing benchmark.
authors: Dasheng Bi; Yubin Hu; Mohammed N. Nasir

name: Training High-Level Schedulers with Execution-Feedback Reinforcement Learning for Long-Horizon GUI Automation
summary: This work trains high-level schedulers with staged reinforcement learning driven by execution feedback. Its CES framework separates a Coordinator for planning and decomposition, a StateTracker for compressed context, and a low-level Executor.
authors: Zehao Deng; Tianjie Ju; Zheng Wu; Zhuosheng Zhang; Gongshen Liu

name: MCP vs RAG vs NLWeb vs HTML: A Comparison of the Effectiveness and Efficiency of Different Agent Interfaces to the Web (Technical Report)
summary: Compares HTML browsing, RAG, MCP, and NLWeb interfaces for web agents performing product search, comparison, and checkout tasks in four simulated e-shops.
authors: Aaron Steiner; Ralph Peeters; Christian Bizer

name: MPR-GUI: Benchmarking and Enhancing Multilingual Perception and Reasoning in GUI Agents
summary: MPR-GUI evaluates GUI perception and reasoning through strictly aligned tasks in six languages. GUI-XLI adjusts non-English hidden representations toward English representations at language-sensitive layers during inference to address the measured cross-language gaps.
authors: Ruihan Chen; Qiming Li; Xiaocheng Feng; Weihong Zhong; Xiaoliang Yang; Yuxuan Gu; Zekun Zhou; Yunfei Lu; Haoyu Ren; Kun Chen; Dandan Tu; Bing Qin

name: AFRAgent : An Adaptive Feature Renormalization Based High Resolution Aware GUI agent
summary: Introduces AFRAgent, which uses adaptive feature renormalization to combine low-resolution visual embeddings with high-resolution details. The architecture is evaluated for smartphone GUI automation on Meta-GUI and AITW.
authors: Neeraj Anand; Rishabh Jain; Sohan Patnaik; Balaji Krishnamurthy; Mausoom Sarkar

name: DrawingBench: Evaluating Spatial Reasoning and UI Interaction Capabilities of Large Language Models through Mouse-Based Drawing Tasks
summary: DrawingBench evaluates sequences of low-level mouse-based GUI actions through 250 drawing prompts and rule-based criteria. Action inspection and multi-turn external feedback support analysis of spatial reasoning, tool-state management, and refinement.
authors: Hyunjun Kim; Sooyoung Ryu

name: HiconAgent: History Context-aware Policy Optimization for GUI Agents
summary: HiconAgent trains GUI policies to use history through variable-length context sampling and paired policy updates with compressed and complete histories. Its compression retains past actions while removing historical observations, and an alignment loss couples the two branches.
authors: Xurui Zhou; Gongwei Chen; Yuquan Xie; Zaijing Li; Kaiwen Zhou; Shuai Wang; Shuo Yang; Zhuotao Tian; Rui Shao

name: Chain-of-Ground: Improving GUI Grounding via Iterative Reasoning and Reference Feedback
summary: Chain-of-Ground uses iterative visual reasoning and reference feedback to refine GUI localization without additional training. It evaluates on ScreenSpot-Pro and introduces TPanel-UI to probe grounding on industrial control panels with visual distortions.
authors: Aiden Yiliu Li; Bizhi Yu; Daoan Lei; Tianhe Ren; Shilong Liu

name: GUI Exploration Lab: Enhancing Screen Navigation in Agents via Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning
summary: Introduces GUI Exploration Lab, a simulation engine for composing screens, interface elements, and navigation graphs. It studies how supervised learning, single-turn RL, and multiturn RL affect GUI navigation and exploration.
authors: Haolong Yan; Yeqing Shen; Xin Huang; Jia Wang; Kaijun Tan; Zhixuan Liang; Hongxin Li; Zheng Ge; Osamu Yoshie; Si Li; Xiangyu Zhang; Daxin Jiang

name: LegalWebAgent: Empowering Access to Justice via LLM-Based Web Agents
summary: LegalWebAgent separates user-needs clarification, webpage browsing, and actions such as form completion or scheduling. A 15-task evaluation studies legal-service workflows relevant to Québec civil-law users, using HTML and screenshot observations.
authors: Jinzhe Tan; Karim Benyekhlef

name: Zoom in, Click out: Unlocking and Evaluating the Potential of Zooming for GUI Grounding
summary: ZoomClick uses repeated zooming and context adjustment to improve GUI grounding without training. The paper studies zoom depth, crop sizes, and related choices and introduces GUIZoom-Bench to evaluate how grounding models respond to zoomed views.
authors: Zhiyuan Jiang; Shenghao Xie; Wenyi Li; Wenqiang Zu; Peihang Li; Jiahao Qiu; Siqi Pei; Lei Ma; Tiejun Huang; Mengdi Wang; Shilong Liu

name: Privacy Practices of Browser Agents
summary: Presents a privacy evaluation framework for browser agents covering component weaknesses, website defenses, tracking, privacy-related prompts and personal-data leakage. The framework is applied to deployed browser-agent tools.
authors: Alisha Ukani; Hamed Haddadi; Ali Shahin Shamsabadi; Peter Snyder

name: MVP: Multiple View Prediction Improves GUI Grounding
summary: MVP addresses unstable GUI coordinates by predicting across several attention-guided cropped views. It clusters the resulting coordinates and selects the densest cluster centroid, evaluating this training-free inference method across grounding models.
authors: Yunzhu Zhang; Zeyu Pan; Zhengwen Zeng; Shuheng Shen; Changhua Meng; Linchao Zhu

name: GAIR: GUI Automation via Information-Joint Reasoning and Group Reflection
summary: Introduces GAIR, which combines information from specialized GUI models through a general-purpose coordinating model. When the available information is insufficient, group reflection sends targeted requests back to the specialists before selecting an operation.
authors: Zishu Wei; Qixiang Ma; Xavier Hu; Yuhang Liu; Hui Zang; Yudong Zhao; Tao Wang; Shengyu Zhang; Fei Wu

name: AgentProg: Empowering Long-Horizon GUI Agents with Program-Guided Context Management
summary: Introduces AgentProg, organizing mobile-agent interaction history as a program with variables and control flow to decide what context to retain. A global belief state handles partial observability, with evaluation on AndroidWorld and extended long-horizon tasks.
authors: Shizuo Tian; Hao Wen; Yuxuan Chen; Jiacheng Liu; Shanhui Zhao; Guohong Liu; Ju Ren; Yunxin Liu; Yuanchun Li

name: WebSTAR: Scalable Data Synthesis for Computer Use Agents with Step-Level Filtering
summary: Introduces a pipeline that filters individual steps from noisy computer-agent rollouts and augments them with reasoning for training. WebSTAR and WebSCORE support GUI-policy supervision and a distilled process reward model, StepRM.
authors: Yifei He; Pranit Chawla; Yaser Souri; Subhojit Som; Xia Song

name: Using GUI Agent for Electronic Design Automation
summary: GUI-EDA collects more than 2,000 screenshot-answer-action pairs from engineers working across five CAD tools and five physical domains. The accompanying benchmark evaluates more than 30 GUI agents on specialized electronic-design workflows.
authors: Chunyi Li; Longfei Li; Zicheng Zhang; Xiaohong Liu; Min Tang; Weisi Lin; Guangtao Zhai

name: ceLLMate: Sandboxing Browser AI Agents
summary: ceLLMate constrains browser-agent authority through an extension that applies policies at the HTTP layer. It evaluates this sandbox against prompt-injection attacks in WASP, avoiding dependence on brittle low-level click and keystroke policies.
authors: Luoxi Meng; Henry Feng; Ilia Shumailov; Earlence Fernandes

name: MobiBench: Multi-Branch, Modular Benchmark for Mobile GUI Agents
summary: MobiBench evaluates mobile GUI agents offline while allowing multiple valid action paths. It decomposes agent pipelines into modules to study component contributions, configurations, and performance bottlenecks.
authors: Youngmin Im; Byeongung Jo; Jaeyoung Wi; Seungwoo Baek; Tae Hoon Min; Joo Hyung Lee; Sangeun Oh; Insik Shin; Sunjae Lee

name: WebOperator: Action-Aware Tree Search for Autonomous Agents in Web Environment
summary: WebOperator uses tree search, action filtering, and path checks before replay to explore web tasks and backtrack while accounting for irreversible actions.
authors: Mahir Labib Dihan; Tanzima Hashem; Mohammed Eunus Ali; Md Rizwan Parvez

name: MobileWorldBench: Towards Semantic World Modeling For Mobile Agents
summary: Evaluates semantic world models for mobile interfaces and studies natural-language state transitions as a tool for agent planning.
authors: Shufan Li; Konstantinos Kallidromitis; Akash Gokul; Yusuke Kato; Kazuki Kozuka; Aditya Grover

name: Step-GUI Technical Report
summary: Step-GUI uses calibrated trajectory rewards to turn generated GUI interaction data into training signals for compact agent models. The report also introduces GUI-MCP for hierarchical GUI operations and local task delegation, and AndroidDaily for static-action and end-to-end mobile evaluation.
authors: Haolong Yan; Jia Wang; Xin Huang; Yeqing Shen; Ziyang Meng; Zhimin Fan; Kaijun Tan; Jin Gao; Lieyu Shi; Mi Yang; Shiliang Yang; Zhirui Wang; Brian Li; Kang An; Chenyang Li; Lei Lei; Mengmeng Duan; Danxun Liang; Guodong Liu; Hang Cheng; Hao Wu; Jie Dong; Junhao Huang; Mei Chen; Renjie Yu; Shunshan Li; Xu Zhou; Yiting Dai; Yineng Deng; Yingdan Liang; Zelin Chen; Wen Sun; Chengxu Yan; Chunqin Xu; Dong Li; Fengqiong Xiao; Guanghao Fan; Guopeng Li; Guozhen Peng; Hongbing Li; Hang Li; Hongming Chen; Jingjing Xie; Jianyong Li; Jingyang Zhang; Jiaju Ren; Jiayu Yuan; Jianpeng Yin; Kai Cao; Liang Zhao; Liguo Tan; Liying Shi; Mengqiang Ren; Min Xu; Manjiao Liu; Mao Luo; Mingxin Wan; Na Wang; Nan Wu; Ning Wang; Peiyao Ma; Qingzhou Zhang; Qiao Wang; Qinlin Zeng; Qiong Gao; Qiongyao Li; Shangwu Zhong; Shuli Gao; Shaofan Liu; Shisi Gao; Shuang Luo; Xingbin Liu; Xiaojia Liu; Xiaojie Hou; Xin Liu; Xuanti Feng; Xuedan Cai; Xuan Wen; Xianwei Zhu; Xin Liang; Xin Liu; Xin Zhou; Yifan Sui; Yingxiu Zhao; Yukang Shi; Yunfang Xu; Yuqing Zeng; Yixun Zhang; Zejia Weng; Zhonghao Yan; Zhiguo Huang; Zhuoyu Wang; Zihan Yan; Zheng Ge; Jing Li; Yibo Zhu; Binxing Jiao; Xiangyu Zhang; Daxin Jiang

name: OS-Oracle: A Comprehensive Framework for Cross-Platform GUI Critic Models
summary: OS-Oracle synthesizes GUI critic examples and trains a pre-action critic with supervised learning followed by consistency-preserving GRPO. It introduces OS-Critic Bench across mobile, web, and desktop settings and tests critic-assisted agents in OSWorld and AndroidWorld.
authors: Zhenyu Wu; Jingjing Xie; Zehao Li; Bowen Yang; Qiushi Sun; Zhaoyang Liu; Zhoumianze Liu; Yu Qiao; Xiangyu Yue; Zun Wang; Zichen Ding

name: VenusBench-GD: A Comprehensive Multi-Platform GUI Benchmark for Diverse Grounding Tasks
summary: VenusBench-GD is a bilingual, cross-platform GUI grounding benchmark organized into basic and advanced tasks. Its annotation pipeline and six-subtask taxonomy support comparisons of general multimodal models and GUI-specialized models across different grounding demands.
authors: Beitong Zhou; Zhexiao Huang; Yuan Guo; Zhangxuan Gu; Tianyu Xia; Zichen Luo; Fei Tang; Dehan Kong; Yanyi Shang; Suling Ou; Zhenlin Guo; Changhua Meng; Shuheng Shen

name: DAVE: A VLM Vision Encoder for Document Understanding and Web Agents
summary: DAVE trains a vision encoder for document images and web agents using self-supervised pretraining followed by supervised parsing and localization. It combines decoder-specific encoder merging with feature fusion and evaluates web localization and agent benchmarks alongside document tasks.
authors: Brandon Huang; Hang Hua; Zhuoran Yu; Trevor Darrell; Rogerio Feris; Roei Herzig

name: EchoTrail-GUI: Building Actionable Memory for GUI Agents via Critic-Guided Self-Exploration
summary: EchoTrail-GUI builds a memory of successful GUI trajectories through autonomous exploration filtered by a reward model. It retrieves relevant trajectories as in-context guidance for new tasks and evaluates the approach on AndroidWorld and AndroidLab.
authors: Runze Li; Yuwen Zhai; Bo Xu; LiWu Xu; Nian Shi; Wei Zhang; Ran Lin; Liang Wang

name: MobileWorld: Benchmarking Autonomous Mobile Agents in Agent-User Interactive and MCP-Augmented Environments
summary: Introduces long mobile workflows that combine agent-user interaction, cross-application tasks, and MCP-based tool access.
authors: Quyu Kong; Xu Zhang; Zhenyu Yang; Nolan Gao; Chen Liu; Panrong Tong; Chenglin Cai; Hanzhang Zhou; Jianan Zhang; Liangyu Chen; Zhidan Liu; Steven Hoi; Yue Wang

name: AndroidLens: Long-latency Evaluation with Nested Sub-targets for Android GUI Agents
summary: AndroidLens provides 571 extended mobile tasks in Chinese and English, with multiple valid paths and preserved environmental anomalies. Its dynamic evaluation uses nested milestones and Average Task Progress to measure partial completion of long workflows.
authors: Yue Cao; Yingyao Wang; Pi Bu; Jingxuan Xing; Wei Jiang; Zekun Zhu; Junpeng Ma; Sashuai Zhou; Tong Lu; Jun Song; Yu Cheng; Yuning Jiang; Bo Zheng

name: iSHIFT: Lightweight Slow-Fast GUI Agent with Adaptive Perception
summary: Introduces iSHIFT, which combines latent reasoning with perception-control tokens to adapt GUI inference. The agent switches between detailed regional grounding and faster use of global visual cues.
authors: Sarthak Mehrotra; Sairam V C Rebbapragada; Mani Hemanth Reddy Bonthu; Vineeth N Balasubramanian

name: MAI-UI Technical Report: Real-World Centric Foundation GUI Agents
summary: MAI-UI combines GUI navigation, native user interaction, and MCP tool calls in a family of policies trained through generated data and online reinforcement learning. The report also studies device-cloud routing and scaling of parallel environments and interaction budgets, with grounding and Android navigation evaluation.
authors: Hanzhang Zhou; Xu Zhang; Panrong Tong; Jianan Zhang; Liangyu Chen; Quyu Kong; Chenglin Cai; Chen Liu; Yue Wang; Jingren Zhou; Steven Hoi

name: SmartSnap: Proactive Evidence Seeking for Self-Verifying Agents
summary: SmartSnap trains GUI agents to collect concise screenshot evidence of task completion for an LLM judge, with experiments on mobile tasks.
authors: Shaofei Cai; Yulei Qin; Haojia Lin; Zihan Xu; Gang Li; Yuchen Shi; Zongyi Li; Yong Mao; Siqi Cai; Xiaoyu Tan; Yitao Liang; Ke Li; Xing Sun

name: DECEPTICON: How Dark Patterns Manipulate Web Agents
summary: DECEPTICON is an environment of 700 web navigation tasks that isolates dark patterns to measure how deceptive interface designs steer agent actions.
authors: Phil Cuvin; Hao Zhu; Diyi Yang
venue: International Conference on Learning Representations

name: It's a TRAP! Task-Redirecting Agent Persuasion Benchmark for Web Agents
summary: Introduces TRAP, which evaluates task-redirection attacks embedded in realistic web interfaces. Controlled website clones and a modular injection framework support comparisons of persuasion techniques and contextual changes across agents.
authors: Karolina Korgul; Yushi Yang; Arkadiusz Drohomirecki; Piotr Błaszczyk; Will Howard; Lukas Aichberger; Chris Russell; Philip H. S. Torr; Adam Mahdi; Adel Bibi

name: Nested Browser-Use Learning for Agentic Information Seeking
summary: NestBrowse organizes browser actions in a nested framework that separates interaction control from page exploration. It evaluates this design for deep information seeking beyond snippet retrieval and direct URL fetching.
authors: Baixuan Li; Jialong Wu; Wenbiao Yin; Kuan Li; Zhongwang Zhang; Huifeng Yin; Zhengwei Tao; Liwen Zhang; Pengjun Xie; Jingren Zhou; Yong Jiang

name: ShowUI-$π$: Flow-based Generative Models as GUI Dexterous Hands
summary: Models discrete clicks and continuous drags with flow-based action generation, and introduces drag trajectories and the ScreenDrag benchmark.
authors: Siyuan Hu; Kevin Qinghong Lin; Mike Zheng Shou

name: Permission Manifests for Web Agents
summary: Proposes agent-permissions.json, a website manifest for declaring which interactions web agents may perform, with optional references to APIs.
authors: Samuele Marro; Alan Chan; Xinxing Ren; Lewis Hammond; Jesse Wright; Gurjyot Wanga; Tiziano Piccardi; Nuno Campos; Tobin South; Jialin Yu; Sunando Sengupta; Eric Sommerlade; Alex Pentland; Philip Torr; Jiaxin Pei

name: ProSoftArena: Benchmarking Hierarchical Capabilities of Multimodal Agents in Professional Software Environments
summary: ProSoftArena evaluates 436 professional-software tasks across six disciplines and 13 applications in a Windows 11 virtual-machine environment. Its capability hierarchy, execution-based checks, and human-in-the-loop evaluation cover precise GUI operations and multi-software workflows.
authors: Jiaxin Ai; Yukang Feng; Fanrui Zhang; Jianwen Sun; Zizhen Li; Chuanhao Li; Yifan Chang; Wenxiao Wu; Ruoxi Wang; Mingliang Zhai; Kaipeng Zhang

name: WebGym: Scaling Training Environments for Visual Web Agents with Realistic Tasks
summary: WebGym supplies realistic web tasks with rubric-based evaluation and an asynchronous rollout system for reinforcement learning. It studies how training on an agent’s own interaction traces scales with task coverage and transfers to unseen websites.
authors: Hao Bai; Alexey Taymanov; Tong Zhang; Aviral Kumar; Spencer Whitehead

name: Agent-Dice: Disentangling Knowledge Updates via Geometric Consensus for Agent Continual Learning
summary: Agent-Dice fuses parameter updates to support continual learning in LLM agents, with GUI agent tasks evaluated alongside tool-use domains.
authors: Zheng Wu; Xingyu Lou; Xinbei Ma; Yansi Li; Weiwen Liu; Weinan Zhang; Jun Wang; Zhuosheng Zhang

name: FocusUI: Efficient UI Grounding via Position-Preserving Visual Token Selection
summary: FocusUI selects instruction-relevant screenshot patches while preserving their positional structure for GUI grounding. Its PosPad scheme replaces runs of dropped tokens with positional markers and is evaluated under reduced token budgets.
authors: Mingyu Ouyang; Kevin Qinghong Lin; Mike Zheng Shou; Hwee Tou Ng

name: MobileDreamer: Generative Sketch World Model for GUI Agent
summary: MobileDreamer predicts post-action GUI states as task-relevant textual sketches with an order-invariant learning objective. Agents use these predictions for lookahead action selection, evaluated on AndroidWorld.
authors: Yilin Cao; Yufeng Zhong; Zhixiong Zeng; Siran Dai; Liming Zheng; Jing Huang; Haibo Qiu; Peng Shi; Wenji Mao

name: InfiniteWeb: Scalable Web Environment Synthesis for GUI Agent Training
summary: InfiniteWeb generates functional, interconnected websites and task evaluators using shared specifications and task-driven development. It evaluates website construction and the transfer of GUI policies trained in these synthetic web environments to OSWorld and Online-Mind2Web.
authors: Ziyun Zhang; Zezhou Wang; Xiaoyi Zhang; Zongyu Guo; Jiahao Li; Bin Li; Yan Lu

name: FronTalk: Benchmarking Front-End Development as Conversational Code Generation with Multi-Modal Feedback
summary: FronTalk benchmarks multi-turn front-end code generation from text and visual feedback; a web agent explores generated sites for evaluation and in AceCoder.
authors: Xueqing Wu; Zihan Xue; Da Yin; Shuyan Zhou; Kai-Wei Chang; Nanyun Peng; Yeming Wen

name: GUITester: Enabling GUI Agents for Exploratory Defect Discovery
summary: Introduces GUITestBench for interactive defect discovery and GUITester, which separates task navigation from anomaly verification. Testing-oriented plans and history-based reflection help distinguish software defects from agent execution mistakes.
authors: Yifei Gao; Jiang Wu; Xiaoyi Chen; Yifan Yang; Zhe Cui; Tianyi Ma; Jiaming Zhang; Jitao Sang

name: From Off-Policy to On-Policy: Enhancing GUI Agents via Bi-level Expert-to-Policy Assimilation
summary: BEPA adapts a small set of expert GUI traces into policy-aligned guidance through trajectories reachable by the learner and a dynamically updated task cache. It evaluates this two-level approach to reinforcement learning on desktop and web benchmarks.
authors: Zezhou Wang; Ziyun Zhang; Xiaoyi Zhang; Zhuzhong Qian; Yan Lu

name: Beyond Clicking:A Step Towards Generalist GUI Grounding via Text Dragging
summary: GUI-Drag provides synthesized text-dragging examples, while ScreenDrag benchmarks selecting text by dragging across varied GUI contexts.
authors: Zeyi Liao; Yadong Lu; Boyu Gou; Huan Sun; Ahmed Awadallah

name: ShowUI-Aloha: Human-Taught GUI Agent
summary: Transforms human screen recordings and input events into annotated demonstrations used by planning and execution components for GUI tasks.
authors: Yichun Zhang; Xiangwu Guo; Yauhong Goh; Jessica Hu; Zhiheng Chen; Xin Wang; Difei Gao; Mike Zheng Shou

name: ColorBrowserAgent: Complex Long-Horizon Browser Agent with Adaptive Knowledge Evolution
summary: ColorBrowserAgent converts human feedback into reusable website knowledge and uses that knowledge to guide progressive context summaries. It evaluates the resulting memory and adaptation mechanisms on long browser workflows.
authors: Jihong Wang; Jiamu Zhou; Weiming Zhang; Teng Wang; Weiwen Liu; Zhuosheng Zhang; Xingyu Lou; Weinan Zhang; Huarong Deng; Jun Wang

name: When Bots Take the Bait: Exposing and Mitigating the Emerging Social Engineering Attack in Web Automation Agent
summary: Studies deceptive social-engineering web patterns targeting browser automation agents and proposes defenses against bait-based manipulation.
authors: Xinyi Wu; Geng Hong; Yueyue Chen; MingXuan Liu; Feier Jin; Xudong Pan; Jiarun Dai; Baojun Liu

name: OS-Symphony: A Holistic Framework for Robust and Generalist Computer-Using Agent
summary: OS-Symphony coordinates milestone-based reflection and memory with tools that build visually aligned tutorials through browser interaction. The framework evaluates trajectory correction and adaptation on online computer-use benchmarks including OSWorld.
authors: Bowen Yang; Kaiming Jin; Zhenyu Wu; Zhaoyang Liu; Qiushi Sun; Zehao Li; JingJing Xie; Zhoumianze Liu; Fangzhi Xu; Kanzhi Cheng; Qingyun Li; Yian Wang; Yu Qiao; Zun Wang; Zichen Ding

name: WebTrap Park: An Automated Platform for Systematic Security Evaluation of Web Agents
summary: Introduces WebTrap Park, a platform that turns web-agent security risks into executable tasks and assesses concrete interactions with live pages. It compares agent frameworks without requiring modifications to their implementations.
