authors: Xinyi Wu; Jiagui Chen; Geng Hong; Jiayi Dong; Xudong Pan; Jiarun Dai; Min Yang

name: ExpSeek: Self-Triggered Experience Seeking for Web Agents
summary: ExpSeek uses step-level entropy signals to decide when a web agent should request experience-based guidance. It supplies guidance tailored to the current step and evaluates the intervention across web-agent benchmarks.
authors: Wenyuan Zhang; Xinghua Zhang; Haiyang Yu; Shuaiyi Nie; Bingli Wu; Juwei Yue; Tingwen Liu; Yongbin Li

name: PersonalAlign: Hierarchical Implicit Intent Alignment for Personalized GUI Agent with Long-Term User-Centric Records
summary: Introduces AndroidIntent to evaluate how GUI agents infer omitted preferences and recurring routines from long-term user records. Its HIM-Agent maintains hierarchical memory of preferences and routines for personalized execution and proactive suggestions.
authors: Yibo Lyu; Gongwei Chen; Rui Shao; Weili Guan; Liqiang Nie

name: GUI-Eyes: Tool-Augmented Perception for Visual Grounding in GUI Agents
summary: GUI-Eyes trains GUI grounders to decide when and how to use visual tools such as crops and zooms. Its coarse-to-fine policy uses dense spatial rewards based on location proximity and region overlap, with evaluation on ScreenSpot-Pro.
authors: Chen Chen; Jiawei Shao; Dakuan Lu; Haoyi Hu; Xiangcheng Liu; Hantao Yao; Wu Liu

name: CaMeLs Can Use Computers Too: System-level Security for Computer Use Agents
summary: NOVA separates trusted task planning from screen-derived observations by producing a branching plan before execution and resolving runtime values through perception. Its OSWorld study examines security and utility while identifying remaining risks from perception-driven branch steering.
authors: Hanna Foerster; Tom Blanchard; Kristina Nikolić; Ilia Shumailov; Cheng Zhang; Robert Mullins; Nicolas Papernot; Florian Tramèr; Yiren Zhao

name: Compress to Focus: Efficient Coordinate Compression for Policy Optimization in Multi-Turn GUI Agents
summary: CCPO couples GUI policy optimization with coordinate-guided compression of past visual observations. It aggregates targets across rollouts to focus retained context and uses distance-based advantages to train grounding and compression together.
authors: Yurun Song; Jiong Yin; Rongjunchen Zhang; Ian G. Harris

name: Terminal-Bench: Benchmarking Agents on Hard, Realistic Tasks in Command Line Interfaces
summary: Terminal-Bench 2.0 benchmarks agents on 89 workflow-inspired tasks in computer terminal environments, with a distinct environment, human solution and verification tests for each task.
authors: Mike A. Merrill; Alexander G. Shaw; Nicholas Carlini; Boxuan Li; Harsh Raj; Ivan Bercovich; Lin Shi; Jeong Yeon Shin; Thomas Walshe; E. Kelly Buchanan; Junhong Shen; Guanghao Ye; Haowei Lin; Jason Poulos; Maoyu Wang; Marianna Nezhurina; Jenia Jitsev; Di Lu; Orfeas Menis Mastromichalakis; Zhiwei Xu; Zizhao Chen; Yue Liu; Robert Zhang; Leon Liangyu Chen; Anurag Kashyap; Jan-Lucas Uslu; Jeffrey Li; Jianbo Wu; Minghao Yan; Song Bian; Vedang Sharma; Ke Sun; Steven Dillmann; Akshay Anand; Andrew Lanpouthakoun; Bardia Koopah; Changran Hu; Etash Guha; Gabriel H. name: Mind the Gap: Action Rebinding Attacks against Android GUI Agents
summary: Studies action-rebinding attacks in which an Android GUI agent’s planned input is redirected to a different application during the observation–action delay. The evaluation examines cross-application execution and the consequences of treating an earlier screen as the current action target.
authors: Yi Qian; Kunwei Qian; Xingbang He; Ligeng Chen; Jikang Zhang; Tiantai Zhang; Haiyang Wei; Linzhang Wang; Hao Wu; Bing Mao

name: Agentic Artificial Intelligence (AI): Architectures, Taxonomies, and Evaluation of Large Language Model Agents
summary: Surveys LLM agent architectures, operating environments and evaluation, covering web navigation and native computer use alongside other agent domains.
authors: Arunkumar V; Gangadharan G. R.; Rajkumar Buyya

name: MirrorGuard: Toward Secure Computer-Use Agents via Simulation-to-Real Reasoning Correction
summary: MirrorGuard trains a reasoning-correction defense using GUI risk trajectories generated in a text-based neural-symbolic simulator. It evaluates whether corrections transfer to computer-use agents operating real interfaces, keeping simulated training separate from deployment tests.
authors: Wenqi Zhang; Yulin Shen; Changyue Jiang; Jiarun Dai; Geng Hong; Xudong Pan

name: MagicGUI-RMS: A Multi-Agent Reward Model System for Self-Evolving GUI Agents via Automated Feedback Reflux
summary: MagicGUI-RMS combines domain-specific and general reward models to assess GUI actions and propose corrections. A structured data pipeline and feedback-recycling process support repeated reward-model and agent improvement.
authors: Zecheng Li; Zhihui Cao; Wenke Huang; Yudong Zhang; Keying Qi; Rui Wang; Zeyu Zheng; Jian Zhao; Hao Zhu; Hengxin Wu; Yuran Wang; Guitao Fan; Guokun Wu; Yicong Liu; Zhilin Gao; Haikun Xu; He Yang; Minqi Xiang; Xingyu Liu; Zuojian Wang

name: EvoCUA: Evolving Computer Use Agents via Learning from Scalable Synthetic Experience
summary: EvoCUA combines task synthesis with executable validators, asynchronous sandbox rollouts and iterative policy updates. It turns successful routines and analyzed failures into supervision and evaluates the evolving agent on OSWorld.

name: Computer Environments Elicit General Agentic Intelligence in LLMs
summary: LLM-in-Sandbox gives agents a minimal computer environment for resource access, file management and code execution; LLM-in-Sandbox-RL trains models to use it.
authors: Daixuan Cheng; Shaohan Huang; Yuxian Gu; Huatong Song; Guoxin Chen; Li Dong; Wayne Xin Zhao; Ji-Rong Wen; Furu Wei

name: The Behavioral Fabric of LLM-Powered GUI Agents: Human Values and Interaction Outcomes
summary: Introduces a controlled web-task testbed for studying how stated preferences and human values influence GUI-agent decisions. It analyzes how personas alter navigation and how prominent interface cues can override the intended preference guidance.
authors: Simret Araya Gebreegziabher; Yukun Yang; Charles Chiang; Hojun Yoo; Chaoran Chen; Hyo Jin Do; Zahra Ashktorab; Werner Geyer; Diego Gómez-Zará; Toby Jia-Jun Li

name: GraphPilot: GUI Task Automation with One-Step LLM Reasoning Powered by Knowledge Graph
summary: GraphPilot builds app-specific knowledge graphs from explored pages, elements and transitions, then uses them to plan action sequences. It requests additional interface observations when uncertain and checks plans against graph transition rules before correction and execution.
authors: Mingxian Yu; Siqi Luo; Xu Chen

name: EntWorld: A Holistic Environment and Benchmark for Verifiable Enterprise GUI Agents
summary: Introduces EntWorld, an enterprise GUI benchmark built by deriving task logic from database schemas. Long workflows across enterprise domains are assessed with deterministic SQL-based state checks.
authors: Ying Mo; Yu Bai; Dapeng Sun; Yuqian Shi; Yukai Miao; Li Chen; Dan Li

name: From Struggle to Success: Context-Aware Guidance for Screen Reader Users in Computer Use
summary: Introduces AskEase, an on-demand assistant that combines contextual information to provide screen-reader-friendly computer-use guidance. A study with screen-reader users evaluates task completion and perceived workload while preserving human control of the interaction.
authors: Nan Chen; Jing Lu; Zilong Wang; Luna K. Qiu; Siming Chen; Yuqing Yang

name: MalURLBench: A Benchmark Evaluating Agents' Vulnerabilities When Processing Web URLs
summary: MalURLBench evaluates how LLM-based web agents handle disguised malicious URLs across attack scenarios; the paper also analyzes attack factors and proposes URLGuard.
authors: Dezhang Kong; Zhuxi Wu; Shiqi Liu; Zhicheng Tan; Kuichen Lu; Minghao Li; Qichen Liu; Shengyu Chu; Zhenhua Xu; Xuan Liu; Meng Han

name: GAIA: A Data Flywheel System for Training GUI Test-Time Scaling Critic Models
summary: GAIA trains a GUI action critic on positive and negative examples, then uses that critic to collect improved examples for another training round. It studies how recycling these data affects the test-time action choices of different GUI agents.
authors: Shaokang Wang; Pei Fu; Ruoceng Zhang; Shaojie Zhang; Xiuwen Xi; Jiahui Yang; Bin Qin; Ying Huang; Zhenbo Luo; Jian Luan

name: SwipeGen: Bridging the Execution Gap in GUI Agents via Human-like Swipe Synthesis
summary: Introduces SwipeGen for synthesizing varied swipe trajectories and SwipeBench for assessing their execution quality. The study examines how richer control of trajectory, speed, and timing changes GUI agents’ interaction performance.
authors: Xuan Wang; Siyuan Su; Quantong Fu; Yongxiang Hu; Yangfan Zhou

name: GUIGuard-Bench: Toward a General Evaluation for Privacy-Preserving GUI Agents
summary: Introduces GUIGuard-Bench, which annotates private regions in GUI trajectories with categories, risk levels, and relevance to the user’s task. It evaluates privacy recognition and the effect of screenshot protection on offline planning and task utility.
authors: Yanxi Wang; Zhiling Zhang; Wenbo Zhou; Weiming Zhang; Jie Zhang; Qiannan Zhu; Yu Shi; Shuxin Zheng; Jiyan He

name: MAGNET: Towards Adaptive GUI Agents with Memory-Driven Knowledge Evolution
summary: MAGNET maintains separate memories for stable interface functions and task procedures across changing layouts and workflows. It updates frequently used knowledge and evaluates adaptation in AndroidWorld and offline distribution-shift settings.
authors: Libo Sun; Jiwen Zhang; Siyuan Wang; Zhongyu Wei

name: Curiosity Driven Knowledge Retrieval for Mobile Agents
summary: Uses execution uncertainty to trigger retrieval from application documentation, code, and past trajectories, organizing the results into structured AppCards for Android agent planning.
authors: Sijia Li; Xiaoyu Tan; Shahir Ali; Niels Schmidt; Gengchen Ma; Xihe Qiu

name: Me-Agent: A Personalized Mobile Agent with Two-Level User Habit Learning for Enhanced Interaction
summary: Me-Agent personalizes mobile agent behavior through a preference reward model and hierarchical memory for long-term and app-specific habits, and introduces User FingerTip.
authors: Shuoxin Wang; Chang Liu; Gowen Loo; Lifan Zheng; Kaiwen Wei; Xinyi Zeng; Jingyuan Zhang; Yu Tian

name: MobileBench-OL: A Comprehensive Chinese Benchmark for Evaluating Mobile GUI Agents in Real-World Environment
summary: Introduces MobileBench-OL, an online benchmark of Chinese-app tasks spanning execution, reasoning, exploration, and noisy conditions. Its automatic evaluation and reset framework supports repeated testing of mobile GUI agents in real environments.
authors: Qinzhuo Wu; Zhizhuo Yang; Hanhao Li; Pengzhi Gao; Wei Liu; Jian Luan

name: OmegaUse: Building a General-Purpose GUI Agent for Autonomous Task Execution
summary: OmegaUse combines exploratory and taxonomy-guided data synthesis with supervised fine-tuning followed by GRPO for GUI control. The report introduces OS-Nav for offline Android and Ubuntu evaluation alongside established grounding and action-prediction benchmarks.
authors: Le Zhang; Yixiong Xiao; Xinjiang Lu; Jingjia Cao; Yusai Zhao; Jingbo Zhou; Lang An; Zikan Feng; Wanxiang Sha; Yu Shi; Congxi Xiao; Jian Xiong; Yankai Zhang; Hua Wu; Haifeng Wang

name: OS-Marathon: Benchmarking Computer-Use Agents on Vast-Horizon, Repetitive Tasks
summary: Introduces OS-Marathon to evaluate long repetitive computer-use workflows whose execution grows with the amount of input data. It studies failure accumulation under task decomposition and GraphDemo, which adapts agents using a demonstration of the recurring workflow.
authors: Jing Wu; Wenjie Ai; Daphne Barretto; Yiye Chen; Qingyu Chen; Yuhang He; Pranit Chawla; Nicholas Gydé; Yanan Jian; Vibhav Vineet

name: Continual GUI Agents
summary: Continual GUI Agents defines grounding under changing application domains and screen resolutions. Its GUI-AiF training framework uses separate point- and region-alignment rewards to adapt grounding as these distributions shift.
authors: Ziwei Liu; Borui Kang; Hangjie Yuan; Zixiang Zhao; Wei Li; Yifan Zhu; Tao Feng

name: CUA-Skill: Develop Skills for Computer Using Agent
summary: CUA-Skill encodes Windows application knowledge in parameterized skills and execution/composition graphs. Its agent retrieves and instantiates these skills and uses memory for failure recovery, with end-to-end evaluation on WindowsAgentArena.
authors: Tianyi Chen; Yinheng Li; Michael Solodko; Sen Wang; Nan Jiang; Tingyuan Cui; Junheng Hao; Jongwoo Ko; Sara Abdali; Leon Xu; Suzhen Zheng; Hao Fan; Pashmina Cameron; Justin Wagle; Kazuhito Koishida

name: CovAgent: Overcoming the 30% Curse of Mobile Application Coverage with Agentic AI and Dynamic Instrumentation
summary: CovAgent augments Android GUI fuzzers by analyzing decompiled app code and component transitions to identify unsatisfied activation conditions. A second agent generates instrumentation that enables otherwise difficult-to-reach activities, with coverage-based evaluation.
authors: Wei Minn; Biniam Fisseha Demissie; Yan Naing Tun; Jiakun Liu; Mariano Ceccato; Lwin Khin Shar; David Lo

name: BEAP-Agent: Backtrackable Execution and Adaptive Planning for GUI Agents
summary: BEAP-Agent treats GUI execution as depth-first search with coordinated planning, execution and task-state tracking. It supports backtracking across multiple levels of earlier states and evaluates recovery on OSWorld.
authors: Ziyu Lu; Tengjin Weng; Yiying Yang; Yuhang Zhao; Xinxin Huang; Wenhao Jiang

name: WebArbiter: A Principle-Guided Reasoning Process Reward Model for Web Agents
summary: WebArbiter generates reasoned action-preference verdicts for web navigation, using reasoning distillation followed by reinforcement learning. It introduces WebPRMBench and evaluates both preference judgments and reward-guided trajectory search.
authors: Yao Zhang; Shijie Tang; Zeyu Li; Zhen Han; Volker Tresp
venue: International Conference on Learning Representations

name: How do Visual Attributes Influence Web Agents? A Comprehensive Evaluation of User Interface Design Factors
summary: Introduces VAF, a controlled pipeline that varies webpage appearance while retaining item semantics. It measures both agent clicks and reasoning references to study which visual design factors change browsing decisions.
authors: Kuai Yu; Naicheng Yu; Han Wang; Rui Yang; Huan Zhang

name: DynaWeb: Model-Based Reinforcement Learning of Web Agents
summary: DynaWeb learns a world model that predicts web-page representations after actions and uses it to generate policy-training rollouts. It interleaves these rollouts with expert trajectories and evaluates the trained web agents on WebArena and WebVoyager.
authors: Hang Ding; Peidong Liu; Junqiao Wang; Ziwei Ji; Meng Cao; Rongzhao Zhang; Lynn Ai; Eric Yang; Tianyu Shi; Lei Yu

name: SSL: Sweet Spot Learning for Differentiated Guidance in Agentic Optimization
summary: SSL uses progressively tiered rewards for agent training, including distance-based guidance on GUI perception tasks alongside planning and reasoning tasks.
authors: Jinyang Wu; Changpeng Yang; Yuhao Shen; Fangzhi Xu; Bolin Ni; Chonghua Liao; Yuchen Liu; Hongzhen Wang; Shuai Nie; Shuai Zhang; Haoran Luo; Jiaming Xu

name: Darwinian Memory: A Training-Free Self-Regulating Memory System for GUI Agent Evolution
summary: Darwinian Memory splits GUI trajectories into reusable units and updates the memory by retaining useful paths and pruning poor ones. It evaluates this training-free memory mechanism on long multi-application tasks.
authors: Hongze Mi; Yibo Feng; WenJie Lu; Song Cao; Jinyuan Li; Yanming Li; Xuelin Zhang; Haotian Luo; Songyang Peng; He Cui; Tengfei Tian; Jun Fang; Hua Chai; Naiqiang Tan

name: Okara: Detection and Attribution of TLS Man-in-the-Middle Vulnerabilities in Android Apps with Foundation Models
summary: Okara uses foundation-model-driven GUI agents to explore Android apps for TLS vulnerability detection, then applies instrumentation and classification to attribute vulnerable code.
authors: Haoyun Yang; Ronghong Huang; Yong Fang; Beizeng Zhang; Junpu Guo; Zhanyu Wu; Xianghang Mi

name: Learning with Challenges: Adaptive Difficulty-Aware Data Generation for Mobile GUI Agent Training
summary: MobileGen estimates a mobile agent’s strengths across structural and semantic task difficulty, then samples new training targets around that profile. A controllable multi-agent generator creates the corresponding instructions and GUI trajectories.
authors: Linjia Kang; Zhimin Wang; Yongkang Zhang; Duo Wu; Jinghe Wang; Ming Ma; Haopeng Yan; Zhi Wang

name: Agentic Reward Modeling: Verifying GUI Agent via Progressive Trajectory-Grounded Interaction
summary: VAGEN verifies GUI trajectories by first extracting readily available evidence and escalating to tool-based environment probes when needed. Evaluation on OSWorld-Verified and AndroidWorld studies verification accuracy and its cost.
authors: Chaoqun Cui; Jing Huang; Shijing Wang; Liming Zheng; Qingchao Kong; Zhixiong Zeng

name: SimGym: Traffic-Grounded Browser Agents for Offline A/B Testing in E-Commerce
summary: SimGym runs traffic-grounded synthetic buyers as browser agents to compare e-commerce storefront variants offline, using buyer profiles derived from production interactions.
authors: Alberto Castelo; Zahra Zanjani Foumani; Ailin Fan; Keat Yang Koay; Vibhor Malik; Yuanzheng Zhu; Han Li; Meysam Feghhi; Ronie Uliana; Shuang Xie; Zhaoyu Zhang; Angelo Ocana Martins; Mingyu Zhao; Francis Pelland; Jonathan Faerman; Nikolas LeBlanc; Aaron Glazer; Andrew McNamara; Lingyun Wang; Zhong Wu

name: Generative Visual Code Mobile World Models
summary: gWorld predicts future mobile GUI states as renderable web code and supplies an automated pipeline for code-based training data. The study evaluates visual state prediction and how stronger world models affect downstream mobile policies.
authors: Woosung Koh; Sungjun Han; Segyu Lee; Se-Young Yun; Jamin Shin

name: SafePred: A Predictive Guardrail for Computer-Using Agents via World Models
summary: SafePred uses world-model risk forecasts to guide action filtering and task replanning. Its desktop and web safety evaluations distinguish policy compliance, task success and success under the specified policy.
authors: Yurun Chen; Zeyi Liao; Ping Yin; Taotao Xie; Keting Yin; Shengyu Zhang

name: SafeGround: Know When to Trust GUI Grounding Models via Uncertainty Calibration
summary: Introduces SafeGround, which estimates GUI-grounding uncertainty from the spatial dispersion of sampled predictions and calibrates a decision threshold before testing. It studies risk-aware selection on ScreenSpot-Pro, with statistical control scoped to the threshold’s false-discovery rate.
authors: Qingni Wang; Yue Fan; Xin Eric Wang

name: Avenir-Web: Human-Experience-Imitating Multimodal Web Agents with Mixture of Grounding Experts
summary: Avenir-Web combines multiple grounding specialists with procedural experience, a task checklist and adaptive memory. It evaluates this planning and execution framework on live Online-Mind2Web tasks.
authors: Aiden Yiliu Li; Xinyue Hao; Shilong Liu; Mengdi Wang

name: ToolTok: Tool Tokenization for Efficient and Generalizable GUI Agents
summary: ToolTok represents GUI operations with learned tool tokens and frames interaction as progressive tool selection. Semantic anchoring and an easy-to-hard curriculum teach tool meanings before visual pathfinding, with evaluation across grounding scenarios.
authors: Xiaoce Wang; Guibin Zhang; Junzhe Li; Jinzhe Tu; Chun Li; Ming Li

name: Agent Alpha: Tree Search Unifying Generation, Exploration and Evaluation for Computer-Use Agents
summary: Agent Alpha uses step-level Monte Carlo tree search to reuse successful prefixes and recover from early GUI mistakes. Comparison-based evaluation and diversity-constrained expansion guide the search, with experiments on OSWorld.
authors: Sizhe Tang; Rongqian Chen; Tian Lan

name: WebSentinel: Detecting and Localizing Prompt Injection Attacks for Web Agents
summary: WebSentinel identifies suspicious webpage segments and checks each against its surrounding page context to detect and locate prompt injections. Its evaluation uses both contaminated and clean webpage datasets.
authors: Xilong Wang; Yinuo Liu; Zhun Wang; Dawn Song; Neil Gong

name: Do Web Agents Investigate Before They Decide?
summary: Introduces MIRAGE, a web decision benchmark where agents must actively uncover evidence that can contradict the visible context. Separate investigation, reasoning, decision, and hallucination measures diagnose failures beyond reaching the right page.
authors: Syed Nazmus Sakib; Nafiul Haque; Tapodhir Karmakar Taton; Shahrear Bin Amin; Shifat E. Arman

name: M$^2$-Miner: Multi-Agent Enhanced MCTS for Mobile GUI Agent Data Mining
summary: M2-Miner uses multi-agent-guided Monte Carlo tree search to collect mobile GUI intent–trajectory pairs. Intent recycling and progressive collector training aim to increase the diversity and usefulness of the mined interaction data.
authors: Rui Lv; Juncheng Mo; Tianyi Chu; Chen Rao; Hongyi Jing; Jiajie Teng; Jiafu Chen; Shiqi Zhang; Liangzi Ding; Shuo Fang; Huaizhong Lin; Ziqiang Dang; Chenguang Ma; Lei Zhao

name: UI-Mem: Self-Evolving Experience Memory for Online Reinforcement Learning in Mobile GUI Agents
summary: UI-Mem stores workflows, skills and failure patterns as reusable templates to guide online GUI reinforcement learning. It varies guidance within rollout groups and continually updates the memory so an unguided policy can learn from guided experiences.
authors: Han Xiao; Guozhi Wang; Hao Wang; Shilong Liu; Yuxiang Chai; Yue Pan; Yufeng Zhou; Xiaoxin Chen; Yafei Wen; Hongsheng Li

name: MemGUI-Bench: Benchmarking Memory of Mobile GUI Agents in Dynamic Environments
summary: MemGUI-Bench evaluates short-term retention and cross-session experience reuse in mobile GUI agents using paired tasks and repeated-attempt protocols. Its staged evaluator measures memory fidelity, learning and execution efficiency.
authors: Guangyi Liu; Pengxiang Zhao; Yaozhen Liang; Qinyi Luo; Shunye Tang; Yuxiang Chai; Weifeng Lin; Han Xiao; WenHao Wang; Siheng Chen; Zhengxi Lu; Gao Wu; Hao Wang; Liang Liu; Yong Liu

name: Trifuse: Enhancing Attention-Based GUI Grounding via Multimodal Fusion
summary: Trifuse combines attention-based localization with OCR text cues and icon captions to ground GUI instructions. Its fusion procedure favors cross-modal agreement and sharp location peaks, and is evaluated without task-specific fine-tuning.
authors: Longhui Ma; Di Zhao; Siwei Wang; Zhao Lv; Miao Wang

name: POINTS-GUI-G: GUI-Grounding Journey
summary: Studies GUI-grounding development from a weakly grounded base model through data preparation, visual training, and verifiable rewards.
authors: Zhongyin Zhao; Yuan Liu; Yikun Liu; Haicheng Wang; Le Tian; Xiao Zhou; Yangxiu You; Zilin Yu; Yang Yu; Jie Zhou

name: Where Not to Learn: Prior-Aligned Training with Subset-based Attribution Constraints
summary: Proposes training with subset-based attribution constraints so models attend to intended evidence, evaluated on image classification and GUI-agent click decisions.
authors: Ruoyu Chen; Shangquan Sun; Xiaoqing Guo; Kangwei Liu; Sanyi Zhang; Zhangcheng Wang; Shiming Liu; Qunli Zhang; Hua Zhang; Wei Wang; Xiaochun Cao

name: ANCHOR: Branch-Point Data Generation for GUI Agents
summary: ANCHOR expands verified desktop demonstrations by generating new tasks at meaningful branch points and executing their instructions. State-aware verification and action filtering refine the resulting trajectories, which are evaluated through fine-tuned agents on OSWorld and WindowsAgentArena.
authors: Jinbiao Wei; Yilun Zhao; Kangqi Ni; Arman Cohan

name: Mapping the Design Space of User Experience for Computer Use Agents
summary: Develops a taxonomy of computer-use-agent interaction design through system review and practitioner interviews. A Wizard-of-Oz study then examines how users respond to normal, erroneous, and risky web-based execution, focusing on control, explanation, prompts, and mental models.
authors: Ruijia Cheng; Jenny T. Liang; Eldon Schoop; Jeffrey Nichols

name: Do Multi-Agents Dream of Electric Screens? Achieving Perfect Accuracy on AndroidWorld Through Task Decomposition
summary: Minitap coordinates six specialized agents for AndroidWorld tasks, checking text input against device state and detecting action loops to revise its strategy.
authors: Pierre-Louis Favreau; Jean-Pierre Lo; Clement Guiguet; Charles Simon-Meunier; Nicolas Dehandschoewercker; Allen G. Roush; Judah Goldfeder; Ravid Shwartz-Ziv

name: When Benign Inputs Lead to Severe Harms: Eliciting Unsafe Unintended Behaviors of Computer-Use Agents
summary: AutoElicit iteratively revises benign instructions using execution feedback to surface harmful unintended actions by computer-use agents in OS workflows.
authors: Jaylen Jones; Zhehao Zhang; Yuting Ning; Eric Fosler-Lussier; Pierre-Luc St-Charles; Yoshua Bengio; Dawn Song; Yu Su; Huan Sun

name: When Actions Go Off-Task: Detecting and Correcting Misaligned Actions in Computer-Use Agents
summary: MisActBench provides action-level labels for task alignment, while DeAction checks proposed computer-use actions and requests revisions through structured feedback. The paper separately evaluates offline detection and interactive operation in OSWorld and RedTeamCUA.
authors: Yuting Ning; Jaylen Jones; Zhehao Zhang; Chentao Ye; Weitong Ruan; Junyi Li; Rahul Gupta; Huan Sun

name: GUI-GenBench: Evaluating Image Generation Models as Interactive GUI Environments
summary: GUI-GenBench tests image-generation models as action-conditioned GUI environments across five suites, including transitions, trajectories and grounding. Its VLM-based GUI-Score separates goal completion, interaction logic, consistency and visual properties.
authors: Haodong Li; Jingwei Wu; Quan Sun; Guopeng Li; Juanxi Tian; Ziyu Guo; Donghao Zhou; Tianfei Ren; Huanyu Zhang; Yanlin Lai; Ruichuan An; Hongbo Peng; Yuhong Dai; Jia Wang; Ziyang Meng; Zheng Ge; Xiangyu Zhang; Daxin Jiang; Pheng-Ann Heng

name: Next-Gen CAPTCHAs: Leveraging the Cognitive Gap for Scalable and Diverse GUI-Agent Defense
summary: Next-Gen CAPTCHAs introduces generated interactive challenges intended to distinguish human users from GUI agents. The benchmark targets perception, memory, decisions and actions, with backend-supported challenge types designed for scalable instance generation.
authors: Jiacheng Liu; Yaxin Luo; Jiacheng Cui; Xinyi Shang; Xiaohan Zhao; Zhiqiang Shen

name: UI-Venus-1.5 Technical Report
summary: Describes a GUI-agent family combining broad intermediate training, full-trajectory online reinforcement learning, and merging of specialized models.
authors: Venus Team; Changlong Gao; Zhangxuan Gu; Yulin Liu; Xinyu Qiu; Shuheng Shen; Yue Wen; Tianyu Xia; Zhenyu Xu; Zhengwen Zeng; Beitong Zhou; Xingran Zhou; Weizhi Chen; Sunhao Dai; Jingya Dou; Yichen Gong; Yuan Guo; Zhenlin Guo; Feng Li; Qian Li; Jinzhen Lin; Yuqi Zhou; Linchao Zhu; Liang Chen; Zhenyu Guo; Changhua Meng; Weiqiang Wang

name: MUZZLE: Adaptive Agentic Red-Teaming of Web Agents Against Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks
summary: MUZZLE evaluates web-agent exposure to indirect prompt injection by finding attack surfaces in agent trajectories and refining injected instructions from execution feedback.
authors: Georgios Syros; Evan Rose; Brian Grinstead; Christoph Kerschbaumer; William Robertson; Cristina Nita-Rotaru; Alina Oprea

name: A11y-CUA Dataset: Characterizing the Accessibility Gap in Computer Use Agents
summary: Introduces A11y-CUA, a dataset comparing how blind or low-vision users and sighted users perform everyday computer tasks. It contrasts those traces with agent behavior under default, keyboard-only, and magnifier conditions to identify barriers to shared control.
authors: Ananya Gubbi Mohanbabu; Rosiana Natalie; Brandon Kim; Anhong Guo; Amy Pavel

name: TreeCUA: Efficiently Scaling GUI Automation with Tree-Structured Verifiable Evolution
summary: TreeCUA organizes GUI exploration trajectories as reusable trees and balances deeper tasks against broader coverage. Its data pipeline combines action verification, memory-backed recovery and a DPO variant that uses information from adjacent branches.
authors: Deyang Jiang; Jing Huang; Xuanle Zhao; Lei Chen; Liming Zheng; Fanfan Liu; Haibo Qiu; Peng Shi; Zhixiong Zeng

name: Code2World: A GUI World Model via Renderable Code Generation
summary: Code2World predicts future GUI screens through renderable code, trained on AndroidCode trajectories with supervised learning and render-aware reinforcement learning. It evaluates visual prediction and downstream AndroidWorld navigation with the learned world model.
authors: Yuhao Zheng; Li'an Zhong; Yi Wang; Rui Dai; Kaikui Liu; Xiangxiang Chu; Linyuan Lv; Philip Torr; Kevin Qinghong Lin

name: Anonymization-Enhanced Privacy Protection for Mobile GUI Agents: Available but Invisible
summary: An anonymization framework replaces sensitive screen content and instructions with consistent, type-preserving placeholders while mediating actions through a local interaction proxy. Experiments on AndroidLab and PrivScreen examine the privacy–utility trade-off when mobile GUI agents operate over these transformed interfaces.
authors: Lepeng Zhao; Zhenhua Zou; Shuo Li; Zhuotao Liu

name: Autonomous Continual Learning for Environment Adaptation of Computer-Use Agents
summary: ACuRL uses autonomous interface exploration and an adaptive task curriculum to continually train computer-use policies with reinforcement learning. CUAJudge supplies outcome feedback, and experiments study adaptation across desktop applications and environment changes.
authors: Tianci Xue; Zeyi Liao; Tianneng Shi; Zilu Wang; Kai Zhang; Dawn Song; Yu Su; Huan Sun

name: LHAW: Controllable Underspecification for Long-Horizon Tasks
summary: LHAW generates underspecified variants of long-horizon workflow tasks and uses agent trials to evaluate when missing information requires clarification.
authors: George Pu; Michael S. Lee; Udari Madhushani Sehwag; David J. Lee; Bryan Zhu; Yash Maurya; Mohit Raghavendra; Yuan Xue; Samuel Marc Denton

name: See, Plan, Snap: Evaluating Multimodal GUI Agents in Scratch
summary: ScratchWorld evaluates program construction through the Scratch interface using fine-grained drag-and-drop actions and a complementary semantic-API mode. Runtime tests assess the resulting programs, allowing analysis of the gap between program reasoning and GUI manipulation.
authors: Xingyi Zhang; Yulei Ye; Kaifeng Huang; Wenhao Li; Xiangfeng Wang

name: ICA: Information-Aware Credit Assignment for Visually Grounded Long-Horizon Information-Seeking Agents
summary: Information-Aware Credit Assignment scores intermediate information gathered by web agents, using rendered webpage snapshots to compare evidence across trajectories.
authors: Cong Pang; Xuyu Feng; Yujie Yi; Jiaqi Su; Zixuan Chen; Jiawei Hong; Tiankuo Yao; Nang Yuan; Jiapeng Luo; Lewei Lu; Xin Lou

name: Blind Gods and Broken Screens: Architecting a Secure, Intent-Centric Mobile Agent Operating System
summary: Analyzes security risks in screen-based mobile agents and proposes Aura, an agent runtime with structured interactions, app-agent isolation and mediated communication.
authors: Zhenhua Zou; Sheng Guo; Qiuyang Zhan; Lepeng Zhao; Shuo Li; Qi Li; Ke Xu; Mingwei Xu; Zhuotao Liu

name: How Smart Is Your GUI Agent? A Framework for the Future of Software Interaction
summary: Proposes GUI Agent Autonomy Levels (GAL), a six-level framework for describing autonomy and benchmarking GUI agents that navigate web, desktop, and mobile software.
authors: Sidong Feng; Chunyang Chen

name: Adaptive Milestone Reward for GUI Agents
summary: ADMIRE extracts milestones from successful GUI explorations to provide adaptive intermediate rewards. It assigns credit differently to successful and failed trajectories and evaluates training on AndroidWorld, with additional transfer studies in web and embodied settings.
authors: Congmin Zheng; Xiaoyun Mo; Xinbei Ma; Qiqiang Lin; Yin Zhao; Jiachen Zhu; Xingyu Lou; Jun Wang; Zhaoxiang Wang; Weiwen Liu; Zhuosheng Zhang; Yong Yu; Weinan Zhang

name: WebTestPilot: Agentic End-to-End Web Testing against Natural Language Specification by Inferring Oracles with Symbolized GUI Elements
summary: WebTestPilot turns natural-language requirements into web test steps with inferred preconditions and postconditions over symbolized GUI elements. A benchmark of bug-injected web applications tests whether these context-aware oracles distinguish application defects from agent mistakes.
authors: Xiwen Teoh; Yun Lin; Duc-Minh Nguyen; Ruofei Ren; Wenjie Zhang; Jin Song Dong

name: AmbiBench: Benchmarking Mobile GUI Agents Beyond One-Shot Instructions in the Wild
summary: AmbiBench evaluates mobile GUI agents under four levels of instruction clarity, including tasks requiring active clarification. Its MUSE evaluator separately audits outcomes, execution quality and interaction quality to study alignment with user intent.
authors: Jiazheng Sun; Mingxuan Li; Yingying Zhang; Jiayang Niu; Yachen Wu; Ruihan Jin; Shuyu Lei; Pengrongrui Tan; Zongyu Zhang; Ruoyi Wang; Jiachen Yang; Boyu Yang; Jiacheng Liu; Xin Peng

name: Agentic Test-Time Scaling for WebAgents
summary: CATTS allocates additional inference computation when an agent’s action votes show uncertainty. The paper compares voting and arbiter strategies and evaluates this selective scaling on WebArena-Lite, Online-Mind2Web and GoBrowse.
authors: Nicholas Lee; Lutfi Eren Erdogan; Chris Joseph John; Surya Krishnapillai; Michael W. Mahoney; Kurt Keutzer; Amir Gholami

name: Agent Skills for Large Language Models: Architecture, Acquisition, Security, and the Path Forward
summary: This survey organizes agent skills by architecture, acquisition, deployment and security, including their role in computer-use systems and GUI grounding. It also proposes a permission and lifecycle governance framework for skill deployment.
authors: Renjun Xu; Yang Yan

name: Scaling Web Agent Training through Automatic Data Generation and Fine-grained Evaluation
summary: This work uses constraint-based progress evaluation to retain partially successful web trajectories for training. It introduces BookingArena for structured booking tasks and studies a distilled agent trained with the resulting data.
authors: Lajanugen Logeswaran; Jaekyeom Kim; Sungryull Sohn; Creighton Glasscock; Honglak Lee

name: SPILLage: Agentic Oversharing on the Web
summary: Formalizes and measures natural agentic oversharing when browser agents handle private user emails and calendars across live websites.
authors: Jaechul Roh; Eugene Bagdasarian; Hamed Haddadi; Ali Shahin Shamsabadi

name: OpAgent: Operator Agent for Web Navigation
summary: OpAgent combines multi-task GUI fine-tuning with online web reinforcement learning using outcome judgments and rule-based progress rewards. A modular planner, grounder, reflector and summarizer support navigation and recovery, evaluated separately from the underlying trained policy.
authors: Yuyu Guo; Wenjie Yang; Siyuan Yang; Ziyang Liu; Cheng Chen; Yuan Wei; Yun Hu; Yang Huang; Guoliang Hao; Dongsheng Yuan; Jianming Wang; Xin Chen; Hang Yu; Lei Lei; Peng Di

name: Building Autonomous GUI Navigation via Agentic-Q Estimation and Step-Wise Policy Optimization
summary: This framework learns an agentic-Q model to estimate individual actions’ contributions to GUI task completion. It then optimizes a policy with step-level samples from its own trajectories, decoupling policy updates from environment interaction.
authors: Yibo Wang; Guangda Huzhang; Yuwei Hu; Yu Xia; Shiyin Lu; Qing-Guo Chen; Zhao Xu; Weihua Luo; Kaifu Zhang; Lijun Zhang

name: GUI-GENESIS: Automated Synthesis of Efficient Environments with Verifiable Rewards for GUI Agent Post-Training
summary: GUI-GENESIS reconstructs applications as lightweight web environments with executable assertions for reward computation. It evaluates the cost of these training environments and transfer from synthetic interaction training to held-out real tasks.
authors: Yuan Cao; Dezhi Ran; Mengzhou Wu; Yuzhe Guo; Xin Chen; Ang Li; Gang Cao; Gong Zhi; Hao Yu; Linyi Li; Wei Yang; Tao Xie

name: ScreenParse: Moving Beyond Sparse Grounding with Complete Screen Parsing Supervision
summary: ScreenParse supplies dense annotations of UI elements, types and text in web screenshots through an automated rendering and filtering pipeline. ScreenVLM learns to output structured screen markup, and the study evaluates dense parsing and transfer to GUI grounding.
authors: A. Said Gurbuz; Sunghwan Hong; Ahmed Nassar; Marc Pollefeys; Peter Staar

name: AutoWebWorld: Synthesizing Infinite Verifiable Web Environments via Finite State Machines
summary: AutoWebWorld turns finite-state task models into interactive websites whose actions and goal states can be checked programmatically. It generates verified trajectories for training and evaluates transfer to WebVoyager and Online-Mind2Web.
authors: Yifan Wu; Yiran Peng; Yiyu Chen; Jianhao Ruan; Zijie Zhuang; Cheng Yang; Jiayi Zhang; Man Chen; Yenchi Tseng; Zhaoyang Yu; Liang Chen; Yuyao Zhai; Bang Liu; Chenglin Wu; Yuyu Luo

name: A Trajectory-Based Safety Audit of Clawdbot (OpenClaw)
summary: Audits Clawdbot safety through logged action and tool-call trajectories across local execution and web-mediated workflows, using automated and human review.
authors: Tianyu Chen; Dongrui Liu; Xia Hu; Jingyi Yu; Wenjie Wang

name: WebWorld: A Large-Scale World Model for Web Agent Training
summary: Introduces WebWorld, an open-web simulator trained on interaction trajectories for generating agent training data and testing candidate actions. WebWorld-Bench evaluates simulated transitions, alongside downstream web-agent training experiments.
authors: Zikai Xiao; Jianhong Tu; Chuhang Zou; Yuxin Zuo; Zhi Li; Peng Wang; Bowen Yu; Fei Huang; Junyang Lin; Zuozhu Liu

name: EmbeWebAgent: Embedding Web Agents into Any Customized UI
summary: EmbeWebAgent embeds agent access into existing web applications through frontend observations and a page-specific function registry. Its workflow combines GUI primitives, composite actions and MCP tools, demonstrated in a live interface.
authors: Chenyang Ma; Clyde Fare; Matthew Wilson; Dave Braines

name: World-Model-Augmented Web Agents with Action Correction
summary: WAC has a web-agent action model consult a world model, simulate action outcomes and use judge feedback to correct actions before execution.
authors: Zhouzhou Shen; Xueyu Hu; Xiyun Li; Tianqing Fang; Juncheng Li; Shengyu Zhang

name: HiPER: Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning with Explicit Credit Assignment for Large Language Model Agents
summary: HiPER trains interactive LLM agents with separate subgoal planning and multi-step execution, assigning reinforcement-learning credit at both levels.
authors: Jiangweizhi Peng; Yuanxin Liu; Ruida Zhou; Charles Fleming; Zhaoran Wang; Alfredo Garcia; Mingyi Hong

name: MemoryArena: Benchmarking Agent Memory in Interdependent Multi-Session Agentic Tasks
summary: MemoryArena links tasks across sessions so that agents must distill earlier interaction experience and use it in later decisions. Its evaluation includes web navigation alongside planning, search and formal reasoning, testing memory through subsequent actions.
authors: Zexue He; Yu Wang; Churan Zhi; Yuanzhe Hu; Tzu-Ping Chen; Lang Yin; Ze Chen; Tong Arthur Wu; Siru Ouyang; Zihan Wang; Jiaxin Pei; Julian McAuley; Yejin Choi; Alex Pentland

name: Mobile-Agent-v3.5: Multi-platform Fundamental GUI Agents
summary: Presents GUI-Owl-1.5 variants and a hybrid data pipeline for multimodal GUI interaction, tool use, memory, and multi-platform tasks.
authors: Haiyang Xu; Xi Zhang; Haowei Liu; Junyang Wang; Zhaozai Zhu; Shengjie Zhou; Xuhao Hu; Feiyu Gao; Junjie Cao; Zihua Wang; Zhiyuan Chen; Jitong Liao; Qi Zheng; Jiahui Zeng; Ze Xu; Shuai Bai; Junyang Lin; Jingren Zhou; Ming Yan

name: Persona2Web: Benchmarking Personalized Web Agents for Contextual Reasoning with User History
summary: Persona2Web tests whether web agents can resolve ambiguous requests using preferences implicit in a user’s history. Its reasoning-aware evaluation compares agent architectures and history-access strategies on personalized tasks on the open web.
authors: Serin Kim; Sangam Lee; Dongha Lee

name: IntentCUA: Learning Intent-level Representations for Skill Abstraction and Multi-Agent Planning in Computer-Use Agents
summary: IntentCUA coordinates planner and critic agents through shared intent-aligned memory, retrieving reusable skills for long-horizon automation across desktop applications.
authors: Seoyoung Lee; Seobin Yoon; Seongbeen Lee; Yoojung Chun; Dayoung Park; Doyeon Kim; Joo Yong Sim

name: Web Agents Should Use Typed Actions Instead of Click-Based Browsing
summary: Proposes web verbs as typed actions for web agents, exposing operations with structured inputs, outputs and conditions so agents can compose auditable workflows.
authors: Linxi Jiang; Rui Xi; Zhijie Liu; Shuo Chen; Zhiqiang Lin; Suman Nath

name: Computer-Using World Model
summary: Presents a desktop world model that predicts textual UI changes before synthesizing the next screenshot. It learns from Microsoft Office transitions and is evaluated by letting a frozen agent compare simulated actions before execution.
authors: Yiming Guan; Rui Yu; John Zhang; Lu Wang; Chaoyun Zhang; Liqun Li; Bo Qiao; Si Qin; He Huang; Fangkai Yang; Pu Zhao; Lukas Wutschitz; Samuel Kessler; Huseyin A Inan; Robert Sim; Saravan Rajmohan; Qingwei Lin; Dongmei Zhang

name: Modeling Distinct Human Interaction in Web Agents
summary: CowCorpus records interleaved human and agent actions during web navigation and identifies distinct patterns of user intervention. Models trained to anticipate these interventions are integrated into live web agents and assessed in a user study.
authors: Faria Huq; Zora Zhiruo Wang; Zhanqiu Guo; Venu Arvind Arangarajan; Tianyue Ou; Frank Xu; Shuyan Zhou; Graham Neubig; Jeffrey P. Bigham

name: ActionEngine: From Reactive to Programmatic Web Agents via State Machine Memory
summary: ActionEngine explores web applications to build an updateable state-machine memory of GUI states, operations and transitions. It generates complete task programs from that memory, using reactive repair to handle changed interfaces or missing knowledge.
authors: Hongbin Zhong; Fazle Faisal; Luis França; Tanakorn Leesatapornwongsa; Adriana Szekeres; Kexin Rong; Suman Nath

name: ProactiveMobile: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Boosting Proactive Intelligence on Mobile Devices
summary: ProactiveMobile benchmarks mobile agents on inferring latent user intent from device context and generating executable sequences from a pool of 63 APIs.
authors: Dezhi Kong; Zhengzhao Feng; Qiliang Liang; Hao Wang; Haofei Sun; Changpeng Yang; Yang Li; Peng Zhou; Shuai Nie; Hongzhen Wang; Linfeng Zhou; Hao Jia; Jiaming Xu; Runyu Shi; Ying Huang

name: GUI-Libra: Training Native GUI Agents to Reason and Act with Action-aware Supervision and Partially Verifiable RL
summary: GUI-Libra trains GUI agents with action-aware supervision, a curated reasoning dataset and reinforcement learning adapted to partially verifiable actions across web and mobile tasks.
authors: Rui Yang; Qianhui Wu; Zhaoyang Wang; Hanyang Chen; Ke Yang; Hao Cheng; Huaxiu Yao; Baolin Peng; Huan Zhang; Jianfeng Gao; Tong Zhang

name: Spatio-Temporal Token Pruning for Efficient High-Resolution GUI Agents
summary: GUIPruner compresses high-resolution screenshots and interaction history for GUI navigation through training-free resizing and layout-aware token pruning.
authors: Zhou Xu; Bowen Zhou; Qi Wang; Shuwen Feng; Jingyu Xiao

name: CoME: Empowering Channel-of-Mobile-Experts with Informative Hybrid-Capabilities Reasoning
summary: Introduces Channel-of-Mobile-Experts (CoME), a mobile agent with experts for screen summary, subtask planning, action decisions and action functions, trained in stages with InfoGain-Driven DPO (Info-DPO).
authors: Yuxuan Liu; Weikai Xu; Kun Huang; Changyu Chen; Jiankun Zhao; Pengzhi Gao; Wei Liu; Jian Luan; Shuo Shang; Bo Du; Ji-Rong Wen; Rui Yan

name: ST-Lite: Training-Free KV Cache Compression with Spatio-Trajectory Guidance for Long-Horizon GUI Agents
summary: Introduces ST-Lite, a training-free KV cache compression scheme for vision-language GUI agents that filters redundant frames and preserves small UI elements in interaction traces.
authors: Bowen Zhou; Zhou Xu; Wanli Li; Jingyu Xiao; Pingan Gan; Haoqian Wang

name: Atomicity for Agents: Exposing, Exploiting, and Mitigating TOCTOU Vulnerabilities in Browser-Use Agents
summary: Identifies time-of-check to time-of-use (TOCTOU) race vulnerabilities when web pages mutate between agent planning and action execution.
authors: Linxi Jiang; Zhijie Liu; Haotian Luo; Zhiqiang Lin

name: M$^2$: Dual-Memory Augmentation for Long-Horizon Web Agents via Trajectory Summarization and Insight Retrieval
summary: Introduces M², a training-free memory framework for long-horizon web agents that summarizes interaction history and retrieves task guidance from an offline insight bank.
authors: Dawei Yan; Haokui Zhang; Guangda Huzhang; Yang Li; Yibo Wang; Qing-Guo Chen; Zhao Xu; Weihua Luo; Ying Li; Wei Dong; Chunhua Shen

name: K^2-Agent: Co-Evolving Know-What and Know-How for Hierarchical Mobile Device Control
summary: Introduces K2-Agent, a hierarchical mobile-control framework that refines task knowledge through a reasoning loop and trains an executor with curriculum-guided reinforcement learning.
authors: Zhe Wu; Donglin Mo; Hongjin Lu; Junliang Xing; Jianheng Liu; Yuheng Jing; Kai Li; Kun Shao; Jianye Hao; Yuanchun Shi

name: CGL: Advancing Continual GUI Learning via Reinforcement Fine-Tuning
summary: Combines supervised and reinforcement fine-tuning for continual GUI learning, using policy entropy to adjust their proportions and gradient projection to limit conflicting updates. AndroidControl-CL groups applications into sequential tasks to evaluate adaptation and retention.
authors: Zhenquan Yao; Zitong Huang; Yihan Zeng; Jianhua Han; Hang Xu; Chun-Mei Feng; Jianwei Ma; Wangmeng Zuo

name: PlugMem: A Task-Agnostic Plugin Memory Module for LLM Agents
summary: Introduces PlugMem, a knowledge-graph memory module for general LLM agents, evaluated on web-agent tasks alongside conversational question answering and knowledge retrieval.
authors: Ke Yang; Zixi Chen; Xuan He; Jize Jiang; Michel Galley; Chenglong Wang; Jianfeng Gao; Jiawei Han; ChengXiang Zhai

name: Dual-Modality Multi-Stage Adversarial Safety Training: Robustifying Multimodal Web Agents Against Cross-Modal Attacks
summary: Studies webpage injections that affect both screenshots and accessibility trees, then trains web agents through teacher imitation, supervised adversarial examples, and adversarial reinforcement learning. The evaluation tests defenses on MiniWoB++ and held-out tasks.
authors: Haoyu Liu; Dingcheng Li; Lukas Rutishauser; Zeyu Zheng

name: TimeWarp: Evaluating Web Agents by Revisiting the Past
summary: TimeWarp tests web agents across multiple versions of the same sites, varying visual design, frontend code and workflows. TimeTraj transfers plans across versions to collect training trajectories and study robustness to interface change.
authors: Md Farhan Ishmam; Kenneth Marino

name: WebFactory: Automated Compression of Foundational Language Intelligence into Grounded Web Agents
summary: Introduces WebFactory, a GUI-agent training pipeline that synthesizes websites, generates tasks and trajectories, and trains with decomposed rewards. Offline and online transfer evaluations examine agents trained on the generated environments.
authors: Sicheng Fan; Qingyun Shi; Shengze Xu; Shengbo Cai; Tieyong Zeng; Li Ling; Yanyi Shang; Dehan Kong

name: STRUCTUREDAGENT: Planning with AND/OR Trees for Long-Horizon Web Tasks
summary: Introduces STRUCTUREDAGENT, a web-agent planning framework that interleaves execution with dynamic AND/OR trees, supporting node repair and exploration of alternative plans.
authors: ELita Lobo; Xu Chen; Jingjing Meng; Nan Xi; Yang Jiao; Chirag Agarwal; Yair Zick; Yan Gao

name: WebChain: A Large-Scale Human-Annotated Dataset of Real-World Web Interaction Traces
summary: WebChain aligns human web-interaction trajectories with visual, structural and action data for agent training. It also introduces WebChainBench and a mid-training approach that separates spatial grounding from planning.
authors: Sicheng Fan; Rui Wan; Yifei Leng; Gaoning Liang; Li Ling; Yanyi Shang; Dehan Kong

name: Enhancing Web Agents with a Hierarchical Memory Tree
summary: Introduces Hierarchical Memory Tree (HMT), which organizes web-agent trajectories by intent, stage and action, then uses the hierarchy to plan and act on websites.
authors: Yunteng Tan; Zhi Gao; Xinxiao Wu

name: Generalization in Online Reinforcement Learning for Mobile Agents
summary: Introduces AndroidWorld-Generalization with separate tests for unseen task instances, templates, and applications. A GRPO training system combines containerized environments with asynchronous trajectory collection to study these generalization regimes.
authors: Li Gu; Zihuan Jiang; Zhixiang Chi; Huan Liu; Ziqiang Wang; Yuanhao Yu; Glen Berseth; Yang Wang

name: Ares: Adaptive Reasoning Effort Selection for Efficient LLM Agents
summary: Introduces Ares, a router that selects a reasoning level for each step of a general LLM agent from its interaction history, with web agents among the evaluation settings.
authors: Jingbo Yang; Bairu Hou; Wei Wei; Yujia Bao; Shiyu Chang

name: OSExpert: Computer-Use Agents Learning Professional Skills via Exploration
summary: Uses GUI-based depth-first exploration to verify elementary software functions, assemble action primitives, and construct curricula of composed skills. OSExpert-Eval examines how the resulting procedural knowledge supports complex computer-use tasks.
authors: Jiateng Liu; Zhenhailong Wang; Rushi Wang; Bingxuan Li; Jeonghwan Kim; Aditi Tiwari; Pengfei Yu; Denghui Zhang; Heng Ji

name: PIRA-Bench: A Transition from Reactive GUI Agents to GUI-based Proactive Intent Recommendation Agents
summary: PIRA-Bench evaluates proactive intent recommendations from noisy GUI screenshot sequences containing interleaved tasks and user context. Its PIRF baseline combines memory and state tracking to maintain multiple task threads and identify opportunities to assist.
authors: Yuxiang Chai; Shunye Tang; Han Xiao; Rui Liu; Hongsheng Li

name: SlowBA: An efficiency backdoor attack towards VLM-based GUI agents
summary: Introduces SlowBA, a backdoor attack on vision-language GUI agents that uses pop-up triggers to induce longer reasoning chains and increase response latency.
authors: Junxian Li; Tu Lan; Haozhen Tan; Yan Meng; Haojin Zhu

name: SecAgent: Efficient Mobile GUI Agent with Semantic Context
summary: Presents a Chinese mobile GUI dataset and navigation benchmark together with SecAgent, which compresses previous screenshots and actions into semantic summaries. The agent is trained with supervised and reinforcement fine-tuning to use this compact interaction context.
authors: Yiping Xie; Song Chen; Jingxuan Xing; Wei Jiang; Zekun Zhu; Yingyao Wang; Pi Bu; Jun Song; Yuning Jiang; Bo Zheng

name: Agentic Critical Training
summary: Introduces Agentic Critical Training (ACT), a reinforcement-learning warm-up that teaches general agents to choose expert actions over alternatives, with WebShop among its evaluations.
authors: Weize Liu; Minghui Liu; Sy-Tuyen Ho; Yongkyun Lee; Andrew Adams Schoen; Souradip Chakraborty; Xiyao Wang; Furong Huang

name: AgentOS: From Application Silos to a Natural Language-Driven Data Ecosystem
summary: Proposes Personal Agent Operating System (AgentOS), with a natural language or voice portal and an Agent Kernel that coordinates agents and tasks in place of a GUI desktop.
authors: Rui Liu; Tao Zhe; Dongjie Wang; Zijun Yao; Kunpeng Liu; Yanjie Fu; Huan Liu; Jian Pei

name: Video-Based Reward Modeling for Computer-Use Agents
summary: Builds ExeVR-53k from execution-video, instruction and reward triplets, including negative instructions with step annotations. A reward model uses spatiotemporal token pruning to judge task completion from the instruction and execution keyframes.
authors: Linxin Song; Jieyu Zhang; Huanxin Sheng; Taiwei Shi; Gupta Rahul; Yang Liu; Ranjay Krishna; Jian Kang; Jieyu Zhao

name: SpecOps: A Fully Automated AI Agent Testing Framework in Real-World GUI Environments
summary: SpecOps divides testing of GUI-based agents into test generation, environment setup, execution and validation handled by specialist agents. Its evaluation spans five real-world agents, including web applications and browser extensions, and measures execution reliability and bug discovery.
authors: Syed Yusuf Ahmed; Shiwei Feng; Chanwoo Bae; Calix Barrus Xiangyu Zhang

name: Hybrid Self-evolving Structured Memory for GUI Agents
summary: Introduces HyMEM, a graph-based memory for GUI agents that links symbolic task knowledge with trajectory embeddings and refreshes working memory during computer-use tasks.
authors: Sibo Zhu; Wenyi Wu; Kun Zhou; Stephen Wang; Biwei Huang

name: Safe and Scalable Web Agent Learning via Recreated Websites
summary: Introduces VeriEnv, which recreates websites as executable training environments and exposes internal state through a Python SDK for task generation and deterministic reward checks. Experiments examine web-agent learning across new and expanded site environments.
authors: Hyungjoo Chae; Jungsoo Park; Alan Ritter

name: CUAAudit: Meta-Evaluation of Vision-Language Models as Auditors of Autonomous Computer-Use Agents
summary: CUAAudit examines vision-language models that judge computer-use task completion from an instruction and final environment state. Across macOS, Windows and Linux benchmarks, it measures accuracy, confidence calibration and disagreement between auditors.
authors: Marta Sumyk; Oleksandr Kosovan

name: Terminal Is All You Need: Design Properties for Human-AI Agent Collaboration
summary: This position paper derives interface design principles from terminal-based human-agent collaboration: representational compatibility, transparent actions and low participation barriers. It argues that graphical and other agent-facing modalities should provide these properties explicitly.
authors: Alexandre De Masi

name: You Told Me to Do It: Measuring Instructional Text-induced Private Data Leakage in LLM Agents
summary: Introduces ReadSecBench, a README-based benchmark for measuring whether high-privilege agents follow injected instructions that leak private data; a computer-use agent is evaluated.
authors: Ching-Yu Kao; Xinfeng Li; Shenyu Dai; Tianze Qiu; Pengcheng Zhou; Eric Hanchen Jiang; Philip Sperl

name: HATS: Hardness-Aware Trajectory Synthesis for GUI Agents
summary: Introduces HATS, which directs GUI trajectory exploration toward semantically ambiguous actions and iteratively checks instruction-execution alignment. Feedback from trajectory refinement updates the exploration signal used to collect subsequent training examples.
authors: Rui Shao; Ruize Gao; Bin Xie; Yixing Li; Kaiwen Zhou; Shuai Wang; Weili Guan; Gongwei Chen

name: AI Planning Framework for LLM-Based Web Agents
summary: Introduces a planning taxonomy and trajectory-quality metrics for web agents, supported by 794 human-labeled WebArena trajectories and a comparison of two planning styles.
authors: Orit Shahnovsky; Rotem Dror

name: Adaptive Vision-Language Model Routing for Computer Use Agents
summary: Adaptive VLM Routing estimates GUI-action difficulty and small-model confidence to select a model under a predicted reliability threshold. Grounding and agent-routing benchmarks assess the cost–accuracy trade-off, with prior interaction context used for warm agents.
authors: Xunzhuo Liu; Bowei He; Xue Liu; Andy Luo; Haichen Zhang; Huamin Chen

name: Why Do LLM-based Web Agents Fail? A Hierarchical Planning Perspective
summary: Presents a hierarchical planning framework for evaluating web agents at planning, execution and replanning stages, and reports low-level execution as the main failure source.
authors: Mohamed Aghzal; Gregory J. Stein; Ziyu Yao

name: Zoom to Essence: Trainless GUI Grounding by Inferring upon Interface Elements
summary: Presents ZoomUI, a training-free grounding method that expresses instructions as visual element descriptions and uses model attention to zoom progressively into relevant interface regions. Evaluation examines instruction-to-element localization on GUI benchmarks.
authors: Ziwei Liu; Tao Feng; Borui Kang; Yanbing Yang; Jun Luo

name: Visual Confused Deputy: Exploiting and Defending Perception Failures in Computer-Using Agents
summary: Formalizes a visual confused-deputy failure in which a computer agent acts on a misperceived UI object. A separate guardrail checks both the visual target and the agent's action reasoning against deployment-specific knowledge before permitting execution.
authors: Xunzhuo Liu; Bowei He; Xue Liu; Andy Luo; Haichen Zhang; Huamin Chen

name: GUI-CEval: A Hierarchical and Comprehensive Chinese Benchmark for Mobile GUI Agents
summary: GUI-CEval evaluates Chinese mobile GUI agents through a hierarchy of atomic abilities and application-level tasks collected on physical devices. Its diagnostics cover perception, planning, reflection, execution and post-action evaluation across a broad set of apps.
authors: Yang Li; Yuchen Liu; Haoyu Lu; Zhiqiang Xia; Hongzhen Wang; Kaiyang Han; Changpeng Yang; Jinyang Wu; Jiaming Xu; Runyu Shi; Ying Huang

name: How Vulnerable Are AI Agents to Indirect Prompt Injections? Insights from a Large-Scale Public Competition
summary: This public red-teaming study evaluates indirect prompt injection that both changes agent behavior and hides the compromise from the final response. Its scenarios include computer use alongside tool calling and coding, with analyses of transfer and model-dependent vulnerability.
authors: Mateusz Dziemian; Maxwell Lin; Xiaohan Fu; Micha Nowak; Nick Winter; Eliot Jones; Andy Zou; Lama Ahmad; Kamalika Chaudhuri; Sahana Chennabasappa; Xander Davies; Lauren Deason; Benjamin L. Edelman; Tanner Emek; Ivan Evtimov; Jim Gust; Maia Hamin; Kat He; Klaudia Krawiecka; Riccardo Patana; Neil Perry; Troy Peterson; Xiangyu Qi; Javier Rando; Zifan Wang; Zihan Wang; Spencer Whitman; Eric Winsor; Arman Zharmagambetov; Matt Fredrikson; Zico Kolter

name: WebPII: Benchmarking Visual PII Detection for Computer-Use Agents
summary: WebPII provides synthetic e-commerce screenshots with fine-grained annotations for sensitive information, including partially filled forms and transaction identifiers. It also trains WebRedact to detect visual PII as a privacy component for computer-use agents.
authors: Nathan Zhao

name: AdaZoom-GUI: Adaptive Zoom-based GUI Grounding with Instruction Refinement
summary: Combines instruction rewriting with conditional second-stage zooming for small GUI targets. A grounding dataset and GRPO training support joint prediction of click coordinates and element bounding boxes.
authors: Siqi Pei; Liang Tang; Tiaonan Duan; Long Chen; Shuxian Li; Kaer Huang; Yanzhe Jing; Yiqiang Yan; Bo Zhang; Chenghao Jiang; Borui Zhang; Jiwen Lu

name: AndroTMem: From Interaction Trajectories to Anchored Memory in Long-Horizon GUI Agents
summary: Introduces AndroTMem-Bench for Android tasks whose later actions depend on earlier UI states. Anchored State Memory retains causally linked intermediate states for subgoal-specific retrieval and evaluates them against full-history and summary-based memory.
authors: Yibo Shi; Jungang Li; Linghao Zhang; Zihao Dongfang; Biao Wu; Sicheng Tao; Yibo Yan; Chenxi Qin; Weiting Liu; Zhixin Lin; Hanqian Li; Yu Huang; Song Dai; Yonghua Hei; Yue Ding; Xiang Li; Shikang Wang; Chengdong Xu; Jingqi Liu; Xueying Ma; Zhiwen Zheng; Xiaofei Zhang; Bincheng Wang; Nichen Yang; Jie Wu; Lihua Tian; Chen Li; Xuming Hu

name: ClawTrap: A MITM-Based Red-Teaming Framework for Real-World OpenClaw Security Evaluation
summary: Presents a man-in-the-middle network red-teaming framework for evaluating autonomous OpenClaw agents under live traffic manipulation.
authors: Haochen Zhao; Shaoyang Cui

name: OS-Themis: A Scalable Critic Framework for Generalist GUI Rewards
summary: Presents OS-Themis, a multi-agent critic that divides GUI trajectories into verifiable milestones and reviews their evidence before assigning an outcome. OGRBench evaluates GUI rewards across platforms, with AndroidWorld experiments examining training and trajectory filtering.
authors: Zehao Li; Zhenyu Wu; Yibo Zhao; Bowen Yang; Jingjing Xie; Zhaoyang Liu; Zhoumianze Liu; Kaiming Jin; Jianze Liang; Zonglin Li; Feng Wu; Bowen Zhou; Zun Wang; Zichen Ding

name: A Subgoal-driven Framework for Improving Long-Horizon LLM Agents
summary: The framework separates inference-time subgoal planning from MiRA, a reinforcement-learning method that supplies milestone rewards. WebArena-Lite experiments evaluate these mechanisms for long-horizon web navigation.
authors: Taiyi Wang; Sian Gooding; Florian Hartmann; Oriana Riva; Edward Grefenstette

name: MedSPOT: A Workflow-Aware Sequential Grounding Benchmark for Clinical GUI
summary: Benchmarks sequential target localization in clinical software workflows, emphasizing how early mistakes affect subsequent interaction steps.
authors: Rozain Shakeel; Abdul Rahman Mohammad Ali; Muneeb Mushtaq; Tausifa Jan Saleem; Tajamul Ashraf

name: ContractSkill: Repairable Contract-Based Skills for Multimodal Web Agents
summary: Turns draft web-agent skills into structured executable artifacts that support deterministic checks, fault localization and local repair. VisualWebArena and MiniWoB experiments examine execution and reuse within the same benchmark family.
authors: Zijian Lu; Yiping Zuo; Yupeng Nie; Xin He; Weibei Fan; Lianyong Qi; Shi Jin

name: MANA: Towards Efficient Mobile Ad Detection via Multimodal Agentic UI Navigation
summary: MANA combines visual, temporal and exploration signals to guide navigation toward mobile advertisements. It evaluates ad detection and interaction cost on commercial smartphones, including obfuscated-ad cases.
authors: Yizhe Zhao; Yongjian Fu; Zihao Feng; Hao Pan; Yongheng Deng; Yaoxue Zhang; Ju Ren

name: Ego2Web: A Web Agent Benchmark Grounded in Egocentric Videos
summary: Ego2Web pairs first-person videos with online tasks that require agents to connect the user’s physical context to web actions. It also evaluates an automatic task judge against human judgments and analyzes failures in video understanding and web execution.
authors: Shoubin Yu; Lei Shu; Antoine Yang; Yao Fu; Srinivas Sunkara; Maria Wang; Jindong Chen; Mohit Bansal; Boqing Gong

name: The Evolution of Tool Use in LLM Agents: From Single-Tool Call to Multi-Tool Orchestration
summary: Surveys multi-tool LLM agents across planning, training, safety, efficiency, and evaluation, including GUI and mobile systems among its application areas.
authors: Haoyuan Xu; Chang Li; Xinyan Ma; Xianhao Ou; Zihan Zhang; Tao He; Xiangyu Liu; Zixiang Wang; Jiafeng Liang; Zheng Chu; Runxuan Liu; Rongchuan Mu; Dandan Tu; Ming Liu; Bing Qin

name: IntentWeave: A Progressive Entry Ladder for Multi-Surface Browser Agents in Cloud Portals
summary: Introduces IntentWeave, a design space and browser-extension prototype for placing web-agent assistance across browser surfaces, evaluated through a study of three entry strategies.
authors: Wanying Mo; Jijia Lai; Xiaoming Wang

name: AgentRAE: Remote Action Execution through Notification-based Visual Backdoors against Screenshots-based Mobile GUI Agents
summary: AgentRAE studies notification-based visual backdoors that redirect mobile GUI-agent actions. Its training separates sensitivity to icon differences from trigger/action association, with evaluations of clean behavior and targeted redirection.
authors: Yutao Luo; Haotian Zhu; Shuchao Pang; Zhigang Lu; Tian Dong; Yongbin Zhou; Minhui Xue

name: CAPTCHA Solving for Native GUI Agents: Automated Reasoning-Action Data Generation and Self-Corrective Training
summary: Introduces ReCAP, a native GUI agent for interactive CAPTCHA challenges, trained with generated interaction trajectories, reasoning traces and self-correction data.
authors: Yuxi Chen; Haoyu Zhai; Chenkai Wang; Rui Yang; Lingming Zhang; Gang Wang; Huan Zhang

name: The Cognitive Firewall:Securing Browser Based AI Agents Against Indirect Prompt Injection Via Hybrid Edge Cloud Defense
summary: Proposes a split-compute browser defense pairing a local visual sentinel, a cloud planner, and deterministic policy enforcement against indirect prompt injection.
authors: Qianlong Lan; Anuj Kaul

name: CarePilot: A Multi-Agent Framework for Long-Horizon Computer Task Automation in Healthcare
summary: CareFlow benchmarks long healthcare-software workflows, while CarePilot coordinates action proposals, execution checks and corrective feedback using short- and long-term memory. Its actor consumes visual interfaces and system state to select semantic actions.
authors: Akash Ghosh; Tajamul Ashraf; Rishu Kumar Singh; Numan Saeed; Sriparna Saha; Xiuying Chen; Salman Khan
topics: automation; planning; memory; evaluation; long-horizon; workflow

name: Towards Automated Crowdsourced Testing via Personified-LLM
summary: Introduces PersonaTester, a framework that gives LLM agents tester personas to vary their exploration and interaction habits during automated crowdsourced GUI testing.
authors: Shengcheng Yu; Yuchen Ling; Chunrong Fang; Zhenyu Chen; Chunyang Chen

name: CUA-Suite: Massive Human-annotated Video Demonstrations for Computer-Use Agents
summary: CUA-Suite combines continuous expert desktop demonstrations in VideoCUA with the UI-Vision evaluation benchmark and GroundCUA grounding data. Screen recordings, cursor traces and layered annotations support study of temporal behavior and professional software workflows.
authors: Xiangru Jian; Shravan Nayak; Kevin Qinghong Lin; Aarash Feizi; Kaixin Li; Patrice Bechard; Spandana Gella; Sai Rajeswar

name: UI-Voyager: A Self-Evolving GUI Agent Learning via Failed Experience
summary: Introduces a two-stage mobile GUI learner that first co-evolves trajectories and policies through rejection fine-tuning. Group Relative Self-Distillation then uses successful rollout branches to provide step-level supervision for failed trajectories, evaluated on AndroidWorld.
authors: Zichuan Lin; Feiyu Liu; Yijun Yang; Jiafei Lyu; Yiming Gao; Yicheng Liu; Zhicong Lu; Yangbin Yu; Mingyu Yang; Junyou Li; Deheng Ye; Jie Jiang

name: WebTestBench: Evaluating Computer-Use Agents towards End-to-End Automated Web Testing
summary: Introduces WebTestBench for end-to-end website testing, separating checklist generation from defect detection. Its WebTester baseline evaluates test coverage, detection and sustained interaction across web application categories.
authors: Fanheng Kong; Jingyuan Zhang; Yang Yue; Chenxi Sun; Yang Tian; Shi Feng; Xiaocui Yang; Daling Wang; Yu Tian; Jun Du; Wenchong Zeng; Han Li; Kun Gai

name: GUIDE: A Benchmark for Understanding and Assisting Users in Open-Ended GUI Tasks
summary: GUIDE evaluates whether models can recognize a user’s behavior, infer intent and decide when to offer help during open-ended software tasks. It uses narrated screen recordings of novice users and studies the effect of additional user context on these assistance decisions.
authors: Saelyne Yang; Jaesang Yu; Yi-Hao Peng; Kevin Qinghong Lin; Jae Won Cho; Yale Song; Juho Kim

name: Where and How to Prune: An Empirical Study of Visual Token Pruning for GUI Agent Navigation
summary: Studies visual token pruning for GUI navigation, separating reusable screenshot encoder embeddings from later language-model computation. The analysis examines foreground-background token allocation and spatial coverage when pruning historical screenshots.
authors: Daiqiang Li; Zihao Pan; Zeyu Zhang; Xuyang Liu; Shijia Xu; Ronghao Chen; Huacan Wang; Honggang Chen; Linfeng Zhang; Zhangquan Chen; Haiyun Jiang

name: Towards GUI Agents: Vision-Language Diffusion Models for GUI Grounding
summary: Adapts a discrete vision-language diffusion model to single-turn GUI action and bounding-box prediction, using a hybrid masking schedule for coordinate geometry. Experiments across web, desktop and mobile datasets examine grounding accuracy and inference tradeoffs.
authors: Shrinidhi Kumbhar; Haofu Liao; Srikar Appalaraju; Kunwar Yashraj Singh

name: GUIDE: Resolving Domain Bias in GUI Agents through Real-Time Web Video Retrieval and Plug-and-Play Annotation
summary: GUIDE retrieves relevant software tutorials through subtitle-based video search, then infers planning and grounding knowledge from consecutive annotated keyframes. It inserts that knowledge into existing GUI-agent modules without parameter updates and evaluates the plug-in on OSWorld.
authors: Rui Xie; Zhi Gao; Chenrui Shi; Zirui Shang; Lu Chen; Qing Li

name: Vision2Web: A Hierarchical Benchmark for Visual Website Development with Agent Verification
summary: Introduces Vision2Web, a benchmark for website development from images, spanning UI-to-code, multi-page frontend and full-stack tasks, with a GUI agent verifier and VLM-based judge.
authors: Zehai He; Wenyi Hong; Zhen Yang; Ziyang Pan; Mingdao Liu; Xiaotao Gu; Jie Tang

name: MolmoPoint: Better Pointing for VLMs with Grounding Tokens
summary: MolmoPoint replaces textual coordinate generation with pointing tokens that select visual regions and refine them through subpatches. The general image/video method includes GUI-pointing evaluation on ScreenSpotPro alongside other visual grounding tasks.
authors: Christopher Clark; Yue Yang; Jae Sung Park; Zixian Ma; Jieyu Zhang; Rohun Tripathi; Mohammadreza Salehi; Sangho Lee; Taira Anderson; Winson Han; Ranjay Krishna

name: "What Did It Actually Do?": Understanding Risk Awareness and Traceability for Computer-Use Agents
summary: Presents an interview study of computer-use agent risks and AgentTrace, a prototype interface showing agent actions, resource access, permission history, and lasting changes.
authors: Zifan Peng; Mingchen Li

name: Emergence WebVoyager: Toward Consistent and Transparent Evaluation of (Web) Agents in The Wild
summary: Audits sources of ambiguity and operational variation in WebVoyager evaluation and introduces standardized guidance for task setup, failure handling, annotation and reporting. Emergence WebVoyager applies this protocol to a web-agent evaluation.
authors: Deepak Akkil; Mowafak Allaham; Amal Raj; Tamer Abuelsaad; Ravi Kokku

name: PSPA-Bench: A Personalized Benchmark for Smartphone GUI Agent
summary: PSPA-Bench evaluates personalized smartphone GUI behavior using user-specific instructions and a process-aware assessment of interaction traces. Its comparison of GUI agents diagnoses weaknesses in adapting workflows and preferences.
authors: Hongyi Nie; Xunyuan Liu; Yudong Bai; Yaqing Wang; Yang Liu; Quanming Yao; Zhen Wang

name: Terminal Agents Suffice for Enterprise Automation
summary: Studies enterprise automation by terminal agents that call platform APIs, comparing their task results and cost with other agent approaches, including web agents using graphical interfaces.
authors: Patrice Bechard; Orlando Marquez Ayala; Emily Chen; Jordan Skelton; Sagar Davasam; Srinivas Sunkara; Vikas Yadav; Sai Rajeswar

name: PixelPrune: Pixel-Level Adaptive Visual Token Reduction via Predictive Coding
summary: PixelPrune removes pixel-redundant patches before the vision encoder, reducing both encoding and downstream language-model work. The training-free method evaluates lossless and controlled-lossy compression on document and GUI tasks.
authors: Nan Wang; Zhiwei Jin; Chen Chen; Haonan Lu

name: When Users Change Their Mind: Evaluating Interruptible Agents in Long-Horizon Web Navigation
summary: Introduces InterruptBench, a WebArena-Lite-derived benchmark that tests how long-horizon web-navigation agents handle mid-task user additions, revisions, and retractions.
authors: Henry Peng Zou; Chunyu Miao; Wei-Chieh Huang; Yankai Chen; Yue Zhou; Hanrong Zhang; Yaozu Wu; Liancheng Fang; Zhengyao Gu; Zhen Zhang; Kening Zheng; Fangxin Wang; Yi Nian; Shanghao Li; Wenzhe Fan; Langzhou He; Weizhi Zhang; Xue Liu; Philip S. Yu

name: Do Phone-Use Agents Respect Your Privacy?
summary: Introduces MyPhoneBench to verify whether phone-use agents minimize personal data disclosure when filling forms during benign mobile tasks.
authors: Zhengyang Tang; Ke Ji; Xidong Wang; Zihan Ye; Xinyuan Wang; Yiduo Guo; Ziniu Li; Chenxin Li; Jingyuan Hu; Shunian Chen; Tongxu Luo; Jiaxi Bi; Zeyu Qin; Shaobo Wang; Xin Lai; Pengyuan Lyu; Junyi Li; Can Xu; Chengquan Zhang; Han Hu; Ming Yan; Benyou Wang

name: Read More, Think More: Revisiting Observation Reduction for Web Agents
summary: Studies HTML and accessibility-tree observations for web agents, relating their usefulness to model capability and thinking budget, and proposes diff-based observation history to save tokens.
authors: Masafumi Enomoto; Ryoma Obara; Haochen Zhang; Masafumi Oyamada

name: GPA: Learning GUI Process Automation from Demonstrations
summary: Presents demonstration-based GUI process replay with Sequential Monte Carlo localization and readiness checks. GPA executes the learned workflow locally and can serve as the GUI execution component of an agent using MCP or CLI tools.
authors: Zirui Zhao; Jun Hao Liew; Yan Yang; Wenzhuo Yang; Ziyang Luo; Doyen Sahoo; Silvio Savarese; Junnan Li

name: UI-Oceanus: Scaling GUI Agents with Synthetic Environmental Dynamics
summary: UI-Oceanus converts autonomous GUI exploration and execution feedback into supervision for predicting future interface states. It compares forward and inverse objectives during continual pretraining and examines downstream offline and online navigation as synthetic data scales.
authors: Mengzhou Wu; Yuzhe Guo; Yuan Cao; Haochuan Lu; Songhe Zhu; Pingzhe Qu; Xin Chen; Kang Qin; Zhongpu Wang; Xiaode Zhang; Xinyi Wang; Wei Dai; Gang Cao; Yuetang Deng; Zhi Gong; Dezhi Ran; Linyi Li; Wei Yang; Tao Xie

name: Poison Once, Exploit Forever: Environment-Injected Memory Poisoning Attacks on Web Agents
summary: Studies persistent web-agent memory contamination introduced through environmental observations. Experiments on WebArena and VisualWebArena examine cross-session effects and how interaction failures alter susceptibility.
authors: Wei Zou; Mingwen Dong; Miguel Romero Calvo; Shuaichen Chang; Jiang Guo; Dongkyu Lee; Xing Niu; Xiaofei Ma; Yanjun Qi; Jiarong Jiang

name: AgentHazard: A Benchmark for Evaluating Harmful Behavior in Computer-Use Agents
summary: Introduces AgentHazard, a benchmark of harmful multi-step behavior by computer-use agents acting through tools, files, and execution environments.
authors: Yunhao Feng; Yifan Ding; Yingshui Tan; Xingjun Ma; Yige Li; Yutao Wu; Yifeng Gao; Kun Zhai; Yanming Guo

name: The Tool Illusion: Rethinking Tool Use in Web Agents
summary: Presents a controlled study of higher-level tool use in web agents across tool sources, backbone models, frameworks, and evaluation benchmarks.
authors: Renze Lou; Baolin Peng; Wenlin Yao; Qianhui Wu; Hao Cheng; Suman Nath; Wenpeng Yin; Jianfeng Gao

name: GUIDE: Interpretable GUI Agent Evaluation via Hierarchical Diagnosis
summary: GUIDE evaluates GUI trajectories by segmenting them into subtasks, diagnosing each segment, and aggregating structured findings into a task verdict. It tests diagnostic judgments on e-commerce, web-agent and Android-control traces.
authors: Yuwen Zhai; Runze Li; Liang Wang; Nian Shi; Liwu Xu; Wei Zhang; Ran Lin; Bo Xu; Benlei Cui

name: Your Agent, Their Asset: A Real-World Safety Analysis of OpenClaw
summary: Introduces a safety evaluation of OpenClaw and the CIK taxonomy for analyzing how changes to a personal agent's persistent state affect attacks on its local and service access.
authors: Zijun Wang; Haoqin Tu; Letian Zhang; Hardy Chen; Juncheng Wu; Xiangyan Liu; Zhenlong Yuan; Tianyu Pang; Michael Qizhe Shieh; Fengze Liu; Zeyu Zheng; Huaxiu Yao; Yuyin Zhou; Cihang Xie

name: Comparing Human Oversight Strategies for Computer-Use Agents
summary: Compares four human oversight strategies during live web-agent sessions, examining exposure to problematic actions and opportunities to intervene. The analysis identifies timing and attention problems in control handoffs and upfront plan approval.
authors: Chaoran Chen; Zhiping Zhang; Zeya Chen; Eryue Xu; Yinuo Yang; Ibrahim Khalilov; Simret A Gebreegziabher; Yanfang Ye; Ziang Xiao; Yaxing Yao; Tianshi Li; Toby Jia-Jun Li

name: IntentScore: Intent-Conditioned Action Evaluation for Computer-Use Agents
summary: Trains IntentScore on offline desktop GUI interactions to assess candidate actions using both their state relevance and planning intent. The reward model is evaluated as an action reranker for Agent S3 on OSWorld.
authors: Rongqian Chen; Yu Li; Zeyu Fang; Sizhe Tang; Weidong Cao; Tian Lan

name: Don't Act Blindly: Robust GUI Automation via Action-Effect Verification and Self-Correction
summary: Introduces VeriGUI, which checks expected action effects and reasons about recovery before subsequent GUI actions. Training combines synthetic failure trajectories with verification-weighted GRPO, evaluated on an AndroidControl-based robustness benchmark.
authors: Yuzhe Zhang; Xianwei Xue; Xingyong Wu; Mengke Chen; Chen Liu; Xinran He; Run Shao; Feiran Liu; Huanmin Xu; Qiutong Pan; Haiwei Wang

name: Gym-Anything: Turn any Software into an Agent Environment
summary: Introduces Gym-Anything, where a setup agent configures software environments and an independent auditor checks the resulting evidence. CUA-World supplies long-horizon tasks across professional applications, with experiments on trajectory distillation and test-time auditing.
authors: Pranjal Aggarwal; Graham Neubig; Sean Welleck

name: MAESTRO: Adapting GUIs and Guiding Navigation with User Preferences in Conversational Agents with GUIs
summary: Introduces MAESTRO, a conversational GUI system that remembers user preferences, adapts interface options, and guides backtracking in multistep booking decisions.
authors: Sangwook Lee; Adnan Abbas; Sang Won Lee; Young-Ho Kim; Yan Chen

name: VenusBench-Mobile: A Challenging and User-Centric Benchmark for Mobile GUI Agents with Capability Diagnostics
summary: Introduces VenusBench-Mobile, an online benchmark for mobile GUI agents with user-intent-driven tasks and capability annotations for analyzing agent behavior and failures.
authors: Yichen Gong; Zhuohan Cai; Sunhao Dai; Yuqi Zhou; Zhangxuan Gu; Changhua Meng; Shuheng Shen

name: The Art of Building Verifiers for Computer Use Agents
summary: Describes a web-trajectory verifier built around structured rubrics, separate process and outcome judgments, and explicit treatment of uncontrollable failures. CUAVerifierBench supplies human labels for evaluating these choices and screenshot-based context management.
authors: Corby Rosset; Pratyusha Sharma; Andrew Zhao; Miguel Gonzalez-Fernandez; Ahmed Awadallah

name: WebSP-Eval: Evaluating Web Agents on Website Security and Privacy Tasks
summary: WebSP-Eval evaluates agents carrying out website security and privacy tasks such as preference changes and session management. A browser extension controls account and initial state across runs, enabling analysis of failures on stateful UI controls.
