summary: HiViG combines a compact history of completed actions with a visually grounded critic that checks proposed coordinates before execution. Its evaluations separate history-related planning failures from errors caused by targeting the wrong screen element.
authors: Jaewoo Lee; Zaid Khan; Archiki Prasad; Justin Chih-Yao Chen; Supriyo Chakraborty; Kartik Balasubramaniam; Sambit Sahu; Elias Stengel-Eskin; Hyunji Lee; Mohit Bansal
topics: interaction-history; memory; grounding; reward-models; long-horizon; evaluation

name: Speculative Rollback Correction for Quality-Diverse Web Agent Imitation
summary: Speculative Rollback Correction lets a student web agent execute short branches before teacher review localizes harmful deviations. Verified continuations and localized corrections feed supervised training while an archive retains diverse successful solutions.
authors: Longkun Hao; Hongyu Lin; Hao Li; Zhuowen Liu; Zhichao Yang; Haojie Hao; Dongshuo Huang; Haitao Yang; Hongyu Ge; Ming jie Xie; Yanjun Wu; Zi Hao Yin; Yan Bai; Yihang Lou

name: CAPED: Context-Aware Privacy Exposure Defense for Mobile GUI Agents
summary: CAPED filters mobile screenshots before upload by combining task requirements, screen context and parsed UI elements to mask incidental private content. AndroidWorld and a controlled seeded privacy evaluation examine leakage reduction alongside task utility and prototype costs.
authors: Siyu Shen; Fenghao Xu; Wenrui Diao; Kehuan Zhang

name: Reasoning for Mobile User Experience with Multimodal LLMs: Task, Benchmark, and Approach
summary: Introduces UXBench for diagnosing usability issues from UI screenshots and UI-UX, a reinforcement-trained model for reasoning about those interface problems.
authors: Ruichao Mao; Zhou Fang; Teng Guo; Hao Yang; Yaping Li; Shaohua Peng; Maji Huang; Xiaoyu Lin; Shuoyang Liu; Xuepeng Li; Yuyu Zhang; Hai Rao

name: ComAct: Reframing Professional Software Manipulation via COM-as-Action Paradigm
summary: ComAct proposes COM program synthesis as an alternative interface for manipulating professional software and introduces ComCADBench with GUI-based comparison agents. ComActor adds a staged training and correction approach, supported by a Windows-container training platform.
authors: Jiaxin Ai; Tao Hu; Xuemeng Yang; Shu Zou; Hairong Zhang; Daocheng Fu; Yu Yang; Hongbin Zhou; Nianchen Deng; Pinlong Cai; Zhongyuan Wang; Botian Shi; Kaipeng Zhang; Licheng Wen

name: Who Pays the Price? Stakeholder-Centric Prompt Injection Benchmarking for Real-world Web Agents
summary: StakeBench evaluates prompt-injection harm to different stakeholders in shopping web-agent workflows. Its executable cases separate attack objectives and assess both outcomes and execution processes to reveal how the same attack pattern can affect different parties.
authors: Zihao Wang; Yiming Li; Yutong Wu; Kangjie Chen; Zheyu Liu; Fok Kar Wai; Pin-Yu Chen; Vrizlynn L. L. Thing; Bo Li; Dacheng Tao; Tianwei Zhang

name: Benchmarking Web Agent Safety under E-commerce Deceptive Interfaces
summary: Introduces WebDecept, a plugin for injecting deceptive e-commerce interface patterns during web-agent tasks and evaluating how multimodal agents respond.
authors: Zijing Shi; Meng Fang; Ling Chen

name: A Benchmark and Framework for Evaluating Next Action Predictions in Spreadsheets
summary: Introduces a benchmark and online evaluation method for predicting the next spreadsheet action from a user's action history, using curated action sequences.
authors: Tejas Agrawal; Vu Le; Sumit Gulwani; Gust Verbruggen

name: Naive Visual Memory is Not Enough: A Failure-Mode Study of GUI Agents
summary: This study finds that full-image visual memory can reduce some state errors while worsening action-level failures. Its AGMem alternative stores local crops associated with successful actions or recovery and evaluates their use in desktop GUI tasks.
authors: Seoyoung Choi; Minseok Ko; Hyunseok Lee; Kunwoong Kim; Woomin Song; Chanseok Jeon; Jinwoo Shin

name: Running the Gauntlet: Hard Agentic Tasks
summary: Introduces GauntletBench, a web-based benchmark of vision-intensive tasks in five professional applications for assessing agent perception, 3D reasoning, and generalisation.
authors: Mykola Vysotskyi; Runqi Lin; Grzegorz Biziel; Michal Zakrzewski; Sebastian Montagna; Damian Rynczak; Shreyansh Padarha; Kumail Alhamoud; Zihao Fu; William Lugoloobi; Kai Rawal; Hanna Yershova; Taras Rumezhak; Guohao Li; Fazl Barez; Baoyuan Wu; Arkadiusz Drohomirecki; Chris Russell; Christopher Summerfield; Adam Mahdi; Volodymyr Karpiv; Philip Torr; Adel Bibi

name: VISTA: View-Consistent Self-Verified Training for GUI Grounding
summary: VISTA forms GRPO comparison groups from target-preserving crops of the same GUI instance with exactly remapped target boxes. A conditional, advantage-weighted cross-view anchor supplies additional supervision without entering the group baseline, and evaluation includes view-consistency robustness.
authors: Xinyu Qiu; Yunzhu Zhang; Heng Jia; Shuheng Shen; Changhua Meng; Linchao Zhu

name: PhoneHarness: Harnessing Phone-Use Agents through Mixed GUI, CLI, and Tool Actions
summary: PhoneHarness routes phone workflows across GUI actions, device-side commands and host tools while retaining auditable execution traces. Its accompanying benchmark checks observable task side effects, separating mixed-action execution from plausible final-answer generation.
authors: Chenxin Li; Zhengyao Fang; Zhengyang Tang; Pengyuan Lyu; Xingran Zhou; Xin Lai; Fei Tang; Liang Wu; Yiduo Guo; Weinong Wang; Junyi Li; Yi Zhang; Yang Ding; Huawen Shen; Sunqi Fan; Shangpin Peng; Zheng Ruan; Anran Zhang; Benyou Wang; Chengquan Zhang; Han Hu

name: Are Online Skill and Memory Modules Always Worth Their Tokens? A Budget-Constrained Study of Web Agents
summary: Compares online skill and memory augmentations with a vanilla web agent given the same total inference-token budget. Across WebArena and WorkArena settings, it studies when module overhead removes aggregate gains and how rerun variability changes conclusions.
authors: Sina Hajimiri; Masih Aminbeidokhti; Jose Dolz; Ismail Ben Ayed; Issam H. Laradji; Spandana Gella; Nicolas Gontier

name: OSGuard: A Benchmark for Safety in Computer-Use Agents
summary: Evaluates action-level guardrails and full computer tasks with environment-dependent safety constraints, separating safe completion from nominal success.
authors: Mina Mohammadmirzaei; Jeffrey Flanigan

name: Where Did It Go Wrong? Process-Level Evaluation of Web Agents with Semantic State Tracking
summary: Introduces WebStep, a web-agent benchmark that records semantic states behind GUI interactions to analyze exploration, execution accuracy, and decisive errors across task steps.
authors: Jiwan Chung; JiHyuk Byun; Vibhav Vineet; Seon Joo Kim

name: LLM-as-Code: Agentic Programming for Agent Harness
summary: Proposes Agentic Programming, where code controls agent loops and invokes LLM-as-Code for reasoning; a computer-use case study examines long visual action sequences.
authors: Junjia Qi; Zichuan Fu; Jingtong Gao; Wenlin Zhang; Hanyu Yan; Xian Wu; Xiangyu Zhao

name: FraudSMSWalker: Benchmarking Agentic Large Language Models for SMS-to-Webpage Fraud Detection
summary: FraudSMSWalker tests browser agents on bilingual SMS-to-webpage fraud judgments while hiding URL and reputation shortcuts. Its controlled chains include difficult benign login/payment cases and evaluate whether classifications remain supported by the visible message and page evidence.
authors: Y. H. Zhou; Z. M. Ma; Y. J. Zhou; Y. T. Li; H. X. Xiang; Y. M. Cheng; T. L. Chen; K. J. Zhang; Z. H. Nan; J. H. Ni; Z. Wu; Q. Y. Pan; S. Zhang; S. Cheng; M. Y. Luo

name: MyPCBench: A Benchmark for Personally Intelligent Computer-Use Agents
summary: MyPCBench tests personal-assistant tasks on a Linux desktop with simulated web applications and data for a single fictional persona. A shared computer-and-shell interface enables evaluation of cross-application workflows that depend on personal context and account-like state.
authors: Lawrence Keunho Jang; Andrew Keunwoo Jang; Jing Yu Koh; Ruslan Salakhutdinov

name: LabOSBench: Benchmarking Computer Use Agents for Scientific Instrument Control
summary: LabOSBench evaluates GUI agents on browser-based scientific instrument simulators with configurable tasks and execution-based checks. Its subtask and end-to-end tests examine feedback-driven adjustment and long workflows without controlling physical instruments.
authors: Anqi Zou; Han Deng; Chengyu Zhang; Junquan Hu; Yu Wang; Yuxiang Xing; Aokai Zhang; Hanling Zhang; Zhaoyang Liu; Ben Fei; Zhihui Wang; Wanli Ouyang

name: ProCUA-SFT Technical Report
summary: ProCUA-SFT generates tasks and synthetic trajectories on live desktops seeded with document content, checking task preconditions before rollout. The resulting step-prefix examples are formatted to match inference context and used for supervised GUI-agent fine-tuning.
authors: Jaehun Jung; Ximing Lu; Brandon Cui; Muhammad Khalifa; Shaokun Zhang; Hao Zhang; Jin Xu; Amala Sanjay Deshmukh; Karan Sapra; Andrew Tao; Yejin Choi; Jan Kautz; Mingjie Liu; Yi Dong

name: Beyond Domains: Reusing Web Skills via Transferable Interaction Patterns
summary: Introduces SkillMigrator, a web agent that turns successful interactions into reusable skills and transfers them between sites by matching page layouts and live element references.
authors: Shiqi He; Yue Cui; Feijie Wu; Xinyu Ma; Jiaheng Lu; Yaliang Li; Bolin Ding; Mosharaf Chowdhury

name: PreAct: Computer-Using Agents that Get Faster on Repeated Tasks
summary: PreAct compiles successful screen-interaction runs into guarded state-machine programs for repeated tasks. It validates programs from clean states before storage and returns control to the agent when replayed screen expectations fail, with tests across mobile, desktop and web.
authors: Bojie Li

name: Trust the Right Teacher: Quality-Aware Self-Distillation for GUI Grounding
summary: Proposes quality-aware self-distillation for GUI coordinate generation under student-produced prefixes. A correctness-aware gate suppresses coordinate-token supervision outside the target box, while teacher-probability scaling adjusts the remaining signal strength.
authors: Jingyuan Huang; Zuming Huang; Yucheng Shi; Tianze Yang; Xiaoming Zhai; Wei Chu; Ninghao Liu

name: VISUALSKILL: Multimodal Skills for Computer-Use Agents
summary: VISUALSKILL organizes application-specific text and figures into hierarchical skills retrieved on demand through an MCP tool. Skills combine authored documentation with live UI exploration, and matched multimodal/text-only comparisons test their utility for interface identification and workflow-state verification.
authors: Ziyan Jiang; Li An; Yujian Liu; Jiabao Ji; Qiucheng Wu; Jacob Andreas; Yang Zhang; Shiyu Chang

name: HANSEL: Extracting Breadcrumbs from Web Agent Trajectories for Interactive Verification
summary: HANSEL extracts evidence pages and snippets from browser-agent traces and preserves relevant page state in interactive verification views. It flags untraceable answers and evaluates evidence selection and human verification effort separately.
authors: Yujin Zhang; Daye Nam

name: Skill-Guided Continuation Distillation for GUI Agents
summary: Skill-Guided Continuation Distillation first lets a policy reach its own off-trajectory states, then uses skill guidance to collect successful continuations. Mixing those continuations with expert traces supplies supervision for recovery states absent from demonstrations.
authors: Zhimin Fan; Hongwei Yu; Yeqing Shen; Haolong Yan; Guozhen Peng; Tianhao Peng; Yudong Zhang; Xiaowen Zhang; Kaijun Tan; Zheng Ge; Xiangyu Zhang; Daxin Jiang

name: Beyond the GUI Paradigm: Do Mobile Agents Need the Phone Screen?
summary: This study compares general coding agents using mobile command-line access with reproducible GUI agents on AndroidWorld and MobileWorld. It also supplies oracle CLI analyses and a separate task suite for operations such as bulk changes, filtering and hidden device state.
authors: Li Gu; Zihuan Jiang; Linqiang Guo; Zhixiang Chi; Ziqiang Wang; Huan Liu; Yuanhao Yu; Tse-Hsun Chen; Yang Wang

name: MemGUI-Agent: An End-to-End Long-Horizon Mobile GUI Agent with Proactive Context Management
summary: MemGUI-Agent makes context management an action chosen by the same policy that controls the mobile UI. Structured history, UI-state and recent-step fields are trained from annotated trajectories to retain cross-app facts while limiting context growth.
authors: Guangyi Liu; Gao Wu; Congxiao Liu; Pengxiang Zhao; Liang Liu; Mading Li; Qi Zhang; Mengyan Wang; Liang Guo; Yong Liu

name: MobileForge: Annotation-Free Adaptation for Mobile GUI Agents with Hierarchical Feedback-Guided Policy Optimization
summary: MobileForge couples real-app exploration and generated tasks with hierarchical feedback for mobile-agent adaptation. Its optimizer turns trajectory outcomes, step feedback and corrective hints into contextualized GRPO updates, with evaluation on AndroidWorld and a GUI-only MobileWorld split.
authors: Guangyi Liu; Pengxiang Zhao; Gao Wu; Yiwen Yin; Mading Li; Liang Liu; Congxiao Liu; Zhang Qi; Mengyan Wang; Liang Guo; Jiangning Zhang; Yong Liu

name: Automating SKILL.md Generation for Computer-Using Agents via Interaction Trajectory Mining
summary: Segments and clusters GUI trajectories into inspectable skills, then trains a skill-aware policy from those annotations. Its diagnostic results distinguish readable source-domain clusters from reliable transfer and report limited or absent downstream gains.
authors: Yuexing Hao; Xiaomin Li

name: OctoNest: Adaptive Cross-Device Execution through Stateful Control
summary: Introduces OctoNest, which coordinates device agents, revises task assignments from execution feedback, and switches local interaction modalities; CAPEBench evaluates cross-device tasks.
authors: Shu Yao; Yuhua Luo; Qian Long; Jingru Fan; Yuheng Wang; Lin Wu; Zhuoyuan Yu; Yufan Dang; Huatao Li; Chen Qian

name: Darwin Mobile Agent: A Roadmap for Self-Evolution
summary: Describes asynchronous reinforcement-learning infrastructure using parallel cloud-hosted Android instances, explicit task lifecycles, and persistent-state management for mobile GUI interaction.
authors: Daniel Beechey; Derek Yuen; Jianheng Liu; Dezhao Luo; Tiantian He; Weilin Luo; Jun Wang; Kun Shao

name: SkillHarness: Harnessing Safe Skills for Computer-Use Agents
summary: Introduces SkillHarness, a framework for computer-use agents to learn and reuse skills under safety constraints when interactions include prompt injections or pop-ups.
authors: Yurun Chen; Biao Yi; Keting Yin; Shengyu Zhang

name: MIRAGE: Stealthy Visual Prompt Injection for Vulnerability Detection in Web Agents
summary: MIRAGE evaluates targeted next-action hijacking from adversarial images restricted to legitimate third-party webpage regions. It combines diffusion-based image generation with execution-aware optimization and tests the constrained visual-injection setting on web-agent frameworks.
authors: Xuelong Dai; Jianyu Ma; Boyang Ma; Biwei Yan; Yijun Yang; Yue Zhang

name: When Web Agents Finish but Still Fail: Reproducible Triggers and Trace Diagnostics for Parallel Web Exploration
summary: Introduces Parallel WebBench for parallel web exploration and uses verified URL trajectories to diagnose search loops, incomplete answers, and failures after evidence retrieval.
authors: Aagam Sogani; Botao Rui; Swetha Vaidyanathan; Rishi Agarwal; Minghao Yan; Shivaram Venkataraman

name: Fara-1.5: Scalable Learning Environments for Computer Use Agents
summary: Builds browser-agent training trajectories with live and synthetic environments, solvers, user simulation, and complementary correctness and efficiency verifiers.
authors: Ahmed Awadallah; Sahil Gupta; Yash Lara; Yadong Lu; Hussein Mozannar; Akshay Nambi; Zach Nussbaum; Yash Pandya; Aravind Rajeswaran; Corby Rosset; Alexey Taymanov; Luiz do Valle; Vibhav Vineet; Spencer Whitehead; Andrew Zhao

name: Whose Agent Are You? Multi-Layer Fingerprinting and Attribution of Autonomous Web Agents
summary: Builds a logging framework that combines network/protocol fingerprints with browser interaction behavior to attribute web-agent traffic. A decision-tree classifier is evaluated across six agent implementations, human browsing and conventional crawlers.
authors: Dayeon Kang; Hyejun Jeong; Jade Sheffey; Pubali Datta; Amir Houmansadr

name: ChainWorld: Composing Long-Horizon Desktop Workloads from Atomic OSWorld Tasks
summary: ChainWorld composes compatible atomic OSWorld tasks into multi-objective desktop chains while preserving their evaluators. It compares giving the full sequence at once with revealing goals turn by turn, exposing different state and session-management failures.
authors: Vincent Siu; Manasi Sharma; Dawn Song; Daniel Yue Zhang; Chenguang Wang; Ying Liu

name: MacAgentBench: Benchmarking AI Agents on Real-World macOS Desktop
summary: Introduces macOS tasks spanning GUI and command-line interaction, with deterministic checks and intermediate-progress scoring for application workflows.
authors: Yikun Fu; Bowen Fu; Zhenyu Wu; Shuang Cheng; Xiaowei Sun; Bowen Yang; Zehao Li; Yibo Zhao; Zichen Ding; Zhoumianze Liu; Shijie Wang; Biqing Qi; Bowen Zhou

name: Agent MechSuits: Mechanistic Subspace Safety Steering for Multi-Turn CLI Agents
summary: Introduces Agent MechSuits, a framework that detects unsafe states and steers multi-turn CLI agents through hidden-representation interventions, alongside the MAS trajectory benchmark.
authors: Weidi Luo; Qiming Zhang; Yihao Quan; Mingyu Jin; Jie Cai; Chaowei Xiao; Jingcheng Niu; Zhen Xiang

name: When AUC 0.998 Is Not Enough: A Candidate Evaluation Protocol for Hidden-State Probes of Indirect Prompt Injection in Multimodal Computer-Use Agents
summary: Proposes diagnostic controls for hidden-state probes of indirect prompt injection in multimodal computer-use agents, using a teacher-forced Mind2Web case study.
authors: Yanhang Li; Zhichao Fan; Zexin Zhuang

name: ENVS: Environment-Native Verified Search for Long-Horizon GUI Agents
summary: ENVS branches over GUI actions in live desktop VMs, verifies successful leaves, and converts them into balanced step-level training supervision. It also introduces OSWorld-Noisy to test recovery from dynamic interruptions while retaining the underlying tasks.
authors: Yincheng Zhou; Athena Zhuoming Zhong; Shijie Zhang; Kevin Zhang; Teresa Xiaotao Shang; Shanghang Zhang

name: Capable but Careless: Do Computer-Use Agents Follow Contextual Integrity?
summary: AgentCIBench evaluates whether computer-use agents disclose information in ways that violate its original context. Deterministically scored scenarios test nearby sensitive UI content, ambiguous requests and recipient mismatches, including end-to-end agent execution.
authors: Anmol Goel; Iryna Gurevych

name: AOHP: An Open-Source OS-Level Agent Harness for Personalized, Efficient and Secure Interaction
summary: Introduces AOHP, an Android OS-level harness that treats agents as system actors and provides adaptive interfaces, agent interfaces, and information-flow controls.
authors: Shanhui Zhao; Jiacheng Liu; Guohong Liu; Jichao Yan; Jialei Ye; Yuhao Yang; Hao Wen; Shizuo Tian; Yizhen Yuan; Yuxuan Chen; Yunxin Liu; Ju Ren; Ya-Qin Zhang; Chao Huang; Yao Guo; Yuanchun Li

name: Reinforcement Learning for Computer-Use Agents with Autonomous Evaluation
summary: The framework uses a vision-language judge’s final-screen assessment as a terminal reward for GUI reinforcement learning. It models evaluator noise and corrects the reward estimator used by PPO across desktop benchmarks.
authors: Marta Sumyk; Oleksandr Kosovan

name: VisCritic: Visual State Comparison as Process Reward for GUI Agents
summary: VisCritic compares before/after screenshots through change-aware visual features and an action-conditioned critic. Weakly supervised samples from existing traces train judgments of action success, progress and error type for GUI-agent verification.
authors: Jiachen Qian

name: GUI vs. CLI: Execution Bottlenecks in Screen-Only and Skill-Mediated Computer-Use Agents
summary: This benchmark matches desktop goals, initial states and final-state verifiers across screen-only GUI and skill-mediated CLI agents. Its experiments separate graphical execution failures from missing CLI skill coverage, including a verifier-guided skill-augmentation condition.
authors: Xiao Zhou; Siyue Zhang; Yilun Zhao; Jinbiao Wei; Tingyu Song; Arman Cohan; Chen Zhao

name: GUI agent: Guided Exploration of User-Sensitive Screens
summary: This short paper develops an explorer agent that expands from a demonstrated GUI task to discover requests likely to reach user-sensitive screens. The proposed exploration supports identifying situations where task execution should be handed back to the user.
authors: Aradhana Nayak; Mussadiq Nazeer; Wang Peng; Feng Liu

name: Uncertainty Quantification for Computer-Use Agents: A Benchmark across Vision-Language Models and GUI Grounding Datasets
summary: Argus benchmarks post-hoc uncertainty methods for single-step GUI grounding across open-weight and closed-source observation regimes. It tests calibration, rejection, error severity and conformal click regions, finding that uncertainty rankings transfer less reliably across model/interface regimes than across datasets for one model.
authors: Divake Kumar; Sina Tayebati; Devashri Naik; Amanda Sofie Rios; Nilesh Ahuja; Omesh Tickoo; Ranganath Krishnan; Amit Ranjan Trivedi

name: WinDOM: Self-Family Distillation for Small-Model GUI Grounding
summary: WinDOM obtains bounding-box supervision from a Windows 11 web reimplementation driven through Playwright, and studies rejection-sampling distillation for small GUI grounders. It treats the depth of the supervised cold start as a GRPO choice, comparing same-size EMA and larger same-family teachers.
authors: Chengheng Li-Chen; Zhiqian Zhou; Hao Chen; Nicolas Chauvin

name: Empowering GUI Agents via Autonomous Experience Exploration and Hindsight Experience Utilization for Task Planning
summary: PEEU explores web environments and turns hindsight experience into aligned high-level planning supervision. A hierarchical task-decomposition analysis examines why atomic-skill competence alone falls short of planning generalization across websites.
authors: Tianyi Men; Zhuoran Jin; Pengfei Cao; Yubo Chen; Kang Liu; Jun Zhao

name: Ko-WideSearch: A Korean Breadth-Search Benchmark for Exhaustive Set Enumeration by Web Agents
summary: Introduces Ko-WideSearch, a Korean web-agent benchmark that asks agents to find every member of a set and fill a table of attributes for each member.
authors: Minbyul Jeong

name: TUA-Bench: A Benchmark for General-Purpose Terminal-Use Agents
summary: TUA-Bench evaluates terminal-use agents on general digital tasks, including document editing, email, web information seeking and specialist software workflows. Tasks run in real terminals with deterministic setup and execution-based scoring.
authors: Shoufa Chen; Luyuan Wang; Xuan Yang; Zhiheng Liu; Yuren Cong; Yuanfeng Ji; Feiyan Zhou; Xiaohui Zhang; Fanny Yang; Belinda Zeng

name: Bridging VideoQA and Video-Guided Agentic Tasks via Generalized Keyframe Extraction
summary: Introduces VG-GUIBench to evaluate GUI agents following video tutorials, and TASKER to select task-relevant keyframes for video-guided tasks and VideoQA.
authors: Sunqi Fan; Qingle Liu; Runqi Yin; Meng-Hao Guo; Shuojin Yang

name: Agent-Computer Observation Interfaces Enable Dynamic Computer Use
summary: The Agent-Computer Observation Interface separates continuous perception from discrete computer actions using captured frames, audio transcription and persistent visual narration. DynaCU-Bench tests these components on dynamic browser tasks and static controls, with model-specific ablations showing that additional observations can also hurt.
authors: Bojie Li; Noah Shi

name: OSWorld 2.0: Benchmarking Computer Use Agents on Long-Horizon Real-World Tasks
summary: Introduces extended computer-use workflows with realistic artifacts, changing information, hidden state, and partial-progress and safety assessments.
authors: Mengqi Yuan; Zilong Zhou; Xinzhuang Xiong; Weiming Wu; Jiayang Sun; Jiamin Song; Kaiqian Cui; Bowen Wang; Haoyuan Wu; Yitong Li; Dunjie Lu; Haikong Lu; Qi Zhen; Xinyuan Wang; Jiaqi Deng; Yuhao Yang; Cheng Chen; Boyuan Zheng; Alex Su; Xiao Yu; Hao Zou; Saaket Agashe; Xing Han Lu; Manpreet Kaur; Zhengyang Qi; Vincent Sunn Chen; Frederic Sala; Dayiheng Liu; Junyang Lin; Zhou Yu; Yu Su; Siva Reddy; Xin Eric Wang; Peng Qi; Tianbao Xie; Tao Yu

name: GUICrafter: Weakly-Supervised GUI Agent Leveraging Massive Unannotated Screenshots
summary: GUICrafter first learns grounding from large collections of unannotated screenshots and webpages, then uses a smaller high-quality dataset for reinforcement-learning calibration. The curriculum targets reduced dependence on manually annotated GUI training data.
authors: Sunqi Fan; Lingshan Chen; Runqi Yin; Qingle Liu; Yongming Rao; Meng-Hao Guo; Shi-Min Hu

name: SpreadsheetBench 2: Evaluating Agents on End-to-End Business Spreadsheet Workflows
summary: Introduces SpreadsheetBench 2, a benchmark of multi-sheet business spreadsheet workflows for agents, covering generation, debugging, and visualization tasks.
authors: Jian Zhu; Yuzheng Zhang; Zeyao Ma; Bohan Zhang; Armin Schoepf; Daniel Woloch; Peter Yiliu Wang; Guangyu Robert Yang; Samuel Jacob; Siddharth Nagisetty; Abhiram Chundru; Jean Lin; Spencer Mateega; Jing Zhang

name: One Forward Beats Two: InnerZoom for Accurate and Efficient GUI Grounding
summary: InnerZoom preserves target-region cues from intermediate decoder layers and reinjects a compact evidence state during coordinate decoding. Its single-forward GUI grounder is compared with crop-and-rerun zooming and matched supervised/RL baselines for accuracy and inference cost.
authors: Chen Liu; Ling Chen; Hanzhang Zhou; Liangyu Chen; Chenglin Cai; Xin Yu; Steven Hoi; Yue Wang

name: On the Internet, Nobody Knows You're an LLM Bot: Unmasking Web Agents with Multi-Layer Fingerprinting
summary: Evaluates web agents against anti-bot mechanisms on instrumented honeysites and analyzes network, HTTP and browser fingerprints. The study compares resistance to blocking with the ability to distinguish agents, humans and agent implementations.
authors: Iliana Fayolle; Sihem Bouhenniche; Samuel Pélissier; Pierre Laperdrix; Clémentine Maurice; Walter Rudametkin

name: LUMOS: A Semantic Operating-System Layer for Accessibility-Grounded AI Agents
summary: LUMOS converts native accessibility metadata and browser UI structure into semantic interface blueprints with stable element identifiers and available actions. It combines live pointer-to-element grounding with an observe-act loop constrained to visible-UI primitives.
authors: Yogeswar Reddy Thota

name: PPT-Eval: A Benchmark for Computer-Use Agents on PowerPoint Tasks
summary: Introduces PPT-Eval, a benchmark of PowerPoint creation and editing tasks for computer-use agents, with rubrics that score partial progress and presentation quality.
authors: Apurva Gandhi; Vishwas Suryanarayanan; Raja Hasnain Anwar; Firoz Shaik; Shubhang Desai; Thong Q. Nguyen; Muhammad Taqi Raza; Vishal Chowdhary; Graham Neubig

name: Learning from Failure: Inference-Time Self-Improvement for Computer-Use Agents
summary: Uses failed computer-use trajectories to diagnose failure modes and generate inference-time agent code patches, with light human verification. An OSWorld study evaluates this failure-driven improvement loop without additional model training.
authors: Xueqiao Sun; Xiaohan Wang; Ludwig Schmidt; Serena Yeung-Levy; Yuhui Zhang

name: Xiaomi-GUI-0 Technical Report
summary: Describes a mobile GUI agent trained through real-device interaction, corrected failure trajectories, supervised learning, and reinforcement learning.
authors: Wanxia Cao; Chengzhen Duan; Pei Fu; Pengzhi Gao; Niu Lian; Fazhan Liu; Hui Liu; Heng Qu; Qinzhuo Wu; Zhehao Yu; Tongbo Chen; Shiqi Cui; Anan Du; Shukai Jia; Yuanfa Li; Wei Liu; Yike Liu; Wenchao Lu; Zhenbo Luo; Haoyuan Sun; Jiatong Sun; Cheng Tan; Yajie Wang; Changqiao Wu; Tao Xiong; Jiahui Yang; Yuxuan Yuan; Ruoceng Zhang; Shaojie Zhang; Jian Zhu; Jian Luan; Cong Zou

name: What Memory Do GUI Agents Really Need? From Passive Records to Active Task-Driving States
summary: Proposes ATMem, an updated execution-state memory for long mobile GUI tasks, and STR-GRPO to train selective memory use; also introduces a mobile task benchmark.
authors: Chen Liu; Ling Chen; Hanzhang Zhou; Xu Zhang; Quyu Kong; Panrong Tong; Wenhao Wang; Xin Yu; Steven Hoi; Yue Wang

name: DigitalCoach: Communication and Grounding Gaps in Human and Agentic Computer Use Coaching
summary: DigitalCoach records expert–novice software coaching conversations aligned with screen and input events. Automated and interactive evaluations examine how model coaches differ from humans in explanation, error diagnosis and visual grounding when helping a learner operate software.
authors: Meng Chen; Anya Ji; Tsung-Han Wu; Tobias Maringgele; David M. Chan; Alane Suhr; Amy Pavel

name: BaRA: Budget-constrained and Reliable Web Data Collection Agent
summary: Introduces BaRA, a web data-collection agent that discovers live site links, checks extracted text, images, and videos, and uses history to recover from failures.
authors: Soojeong Lee; Joseph Lee; Yongseong Cho; Sunjae Kim; Youngwoo Moon; Kyungwoo Song

name: (A)I Sees What You Don't: Exploiting New Attack Surfaces in Third-Party Mobile Agents
summary: Analyzes cross-app privilege escalation and visual attack surfaces introduced by third-party VLM-powered mobile agents.
authors: Zidong Zhang; Zhentao Xie; Wenrui Diao; Jianliang Wu

name: A Task-State Representation for Long-Horizon Mobile GUI Agents
summary: Introduces TSR, a training-free wrapper for long-horizon mobile GUI agents that tracks instructions, subgoal progress, and action outcomes separately from screen observations.
authors: Yujie Zheng; Zikang Liu; Xin Zhao; Ji-Rong Wen

name: Do GUI Agents Believe Their Eyes? Diagnosing State-Belief Reliance on Pixels versus Structure
summary: Defines visual state reliance and probes whether GUI agents resolve screenshot/structure conflicts using pixels, serialized interface structure or prior beliefs. Paired interventions and live multi-step tests connect misattributed state beliefs to failures and compare consistency-based mitigations.
authors: Guijia Zhang; Yuxun Chen; Yuheng Qi; Harry Yang

name: UI-MOPD: Multi-Platform On-Policy Distillation for Unified GUI Agents
summary: Introduces Uni-GUI, a collection of executable desktop and mobile trajectories, and UI-MOPD, which trains a shared policy from its own rollouts using platform-specific teachers. The distillation procedure routes each visited state to the appropriate teacher to preserve distinct interaction conventions.
authors: Niu Lian; Tongbo Chen; Zhehao Yu; Chengzhen Duan; Fazhan Liu; Hui Liu; Pei Fu; Jian Luan; Heng Qu; Shu-Tao Xia; Jinpeng Wang

name: Agent Data Injection Attacks are Realistic Threats to AI Agents
summary: This study examines agent data injection, where untrusted content impersonates trusted metadata or tool-context data. It reports arbitrary-click vulnerabilities in web agents alongside separate coding-agent attacks, highlighting trust-boundary failures beyond instruction injection.
authors: Woohyuk Choi; Juhee Kim; Taehyun Kang; Jihyeon Jeong; Luyi Xing; Byoungyoung Lee

name: Untrusted Content Masking for Web Agents with Security Guarantees
summary: Untrusted Content Masking uses DOM structure to redact untrusted webpage regions before agent observation. A sandboxed interaction interface separates privileges so browser actions can proceed under the proposed trust-boundary model without exposing protected content to the planner.
authors: Kristina Nikolić; Egor Zverev; Javier Rando; Matthew Jagielski; Edoardo Debenedetti; Florian Tramèr

name: TurnOPD: Making On-Policy Distillation Turn-Aware for Efficient Long-Horizon Agent Training
summary: Proposes TurnOPD, a rollout-depth and loss-budgeting method for training long-horizon language agents; WebShop is one of its evaluation settings.
authors: Yuhang Zhou; Kai Zheng; Haoling Li; Dengyun Peng; Can Xu; Jingjing Chen

name: WebRetriever: A Large-Scale Comprehensive Benchmark for Efficient Web Agent Evaluation
summary: WebRetriever evaluates navigation, knowledge-assisted interaction and end-to-end information-extraction workflows under separate protocols. Its NavEval judge uses richer interaction context to diagnose cases where navigation success and useful task completion diverge.
authors: Wei Dong; Tianyu Fu; Zhe Yu; Hanning Wang; Anyang Su; Zhizhou Fang; Yuyang Chen; Shuo Wang; Minghui Wu; Ping Jiang; Zhen Lei; Chenxu Zhao

name: Prismata: Confining Cross-Site Prompt Injection in Web Agents
summary: Introduces Prismata, a defense for web agents that assigns trust labels to page content and enforces them by redacting content and restricting agent actions.
authors: Corban Villa; Alp Eren Ozdarendeli; Sijun Tan; Raluca Ada Popa

name: UniClawBench: A Universal Benchmark for Proactive Agents on Real-World Tasks
summary: Introduces UniClawBench, a benchmark of proactive agents on bilingual real-world tasks, evaluated in live Docker containers with stepwise checkpoints and simulated user feedback.
authors: Zhekai Chen; Chengqi Duan; Kaiyue Sun; Bohao Li; Yuqing Wang; Manyuan Zhang; Xihui Liu

name: EvoCUA-1.5: Online Reinforcement Learning for Multi-turn Computer-Use Agents
summary: EvoCUA-1.5 trains multi-turn desktop agents through online reinforcement learning in executable sandboxes. It combines step-level policy optimization, task filtering and calibration, an adaptive curriculum, and asynchronous rollout handling with staleness control.
authors: Mianqiu Huang; Taofeng Xue; Chong Peng; Jinrui Ding; Jie Yang; Sicheng Fan; Jiale Hong; Yufei Gao; Xiaocheng Zhang; Linsen Guo; Xin Yang; Dengchang Zhao; Yuchen Xie; Peng Pei; Xunliang Xie; Xipeng Qiu

name: MAG: A Web-Agent Benchmark and Harness for Multimodal Action and Guide Generation
summary: MAG jointly evaluates browser task actions and user-facing guides grounded in screenshots through element marks or pixel coordinates. Its harness covers annotation, live evaluation and joint metrics, with an expert-trajectory-augmented GRPO training study.
authors: Chengguang Gan; Hanjun Wei; Yunhao Liang; Zhixi Cai; Qinghao Zhang; Shiwen Ni

name: The Compliance Trap: Diagnosing How AI Agents Consume Conflicting Memory
summary: The Entry–Propagation–Recovery framework traces where conflicting memory first changes an agent action, how the effect propagates and whether recovery occurs. WebArena and the controlled MemTrapBench separate memory-consumption failures across these stages.
authors: Yixiong Chen; Xinyi Bai; Alan Yuille

name: SCALECUA: Scaling Computer Use Agents with Verifiable Task Synthesis and Efficient Online RL
summary: Scales computer-agent reinforcement learning through verifiable task generation, capability-aware rollout allocation, and segmented visual context.
authors: Bowen Lv; Xiao Liu; Yanyu Ren; Hanyu Lai; Bohao Jing; Hanchen Zhang; Yanxiao Zhao; Shuntian Yao; Jie Tang; Yuxiao Dong

name: StructAgent: Harness Long-horizon Digital Agents with Unified Causal Structure
summary: StructAgent maintains compact task state and regulates long-horizon execution through verified transitions and progress checkpoints. Its workflow supports evidence-based completion and targeted recovery, with desktop computer-use evaluation and a separate Minecraft extension.
authors: Wenyi Wu; Sibo Zhu; Kun Zhou; Aayush Salvi; Zixuan Song; Biwei Huang

name: Designing Agent-Ready Websites for AI Web Agents: A Framework for Machine Readability, Actionability, and Decision Reliability
summary: Proposes an agent-ready website design framework for e-commerce browser agents and compares it with a human-oriented site on shopping tasks, outcomes, steps, and token use.
authors: Said Elnaffar; Farzad Rashidi

name: KnowAct-GUIClaw: Know Deeply, Act Perfectly, Personal GUI Assistant with Self-Evolving Memory and Skill
summary: KnowAct-GUIClaw combines a host planner with pluggable GUI subagents, attributable experience memory and an evolving skill library. It uses user profiles and feedback for task decomposition and evaluates transfer across Android, iOS, HarmonyOS and Windows.
authors: Yunxin Li; Jinchao Li; Shibo Su; Zhenran Xu; Chenrui Zhao; Tongshu Bian; Xiaoman Liang; Meishan Zhang; Baotian Hu; Min Zhang

name: A Learning-Rate-Gated Failure of GRPO in a Small Language and Vision-Language Model Web Agent: A Controlled Null and Its Mechanism
summary: Studies a controlled setting where GRPO fails to improve a strong small web agent and can reduce text-track performance. Matched reachable-reward tasks and component grafting distinguish limited optimization headroom from learning-rate-dependent failure mechanisms.
authors: Chengguang Gan; Zhixi Cai; Yunhao Liang; Hanjun Wei; Shiwen Ni; Qinghao Zhang

name: PalmClaw: A Native On-Device Agent Framework for Mobile Phones
summary: Introduces PalmClaw, an on-device phone agent framework that manages sessions, memory, and tools, exposing mobile capabilities through structured device-tool calls.
authors: Hongru Cai; Yongqi Li; Ran Wei; Wenjie Li

name: Multi-Head Latent Control: A Unified Interface for LLM Agent Decision Making
summary: Introduces Multi-Head Latent Control, a layer that reads frozen LLM or VLM hidden-state trajectories to signal when an agent should defer, seek clarification, use tools, abstain, or answer.
authors: Amirhosein Ghasemabadi; Ruichen Chen; Bahador Rashidi; Di Niu

name: Tactile: Giving Computer-Using Agents Hands and Feet
summary: Tactile turns accessibility, OCR and visual evidence into explicit desktop targets with executable actions and verification cues. Its execution loop chooses semantic actions or coordinate fallbacks while retaining provenance for replay and diagnosis.
authors: Yong Liu; Zhenyi Zhong; Zhanpeng Shi
topics: grounding; automation; observability; tool-integration; robustness; evaluation

name: HyMobileAgent: Data-Environment Co-Scaling for Efficient GUI Agents
summary: Combines GUI perception data, instructional videos, real and simulated devices, and planning with reflection to develop a mobile agent.
authors: Hy Vision Team; Huawen Shen; Zhengyang Tang; Shangpin Peng; Liang Wu; Anran Zhang; Weinong Wang; Yiduo Guo; Chenxin Li; Zhengyao Fang; Yang Ding; Junyi Li; Fei Tang; Zheng Ruan; Yi Zhang; Xingran Zhou; Dingchen Yang; Sunqi Fan; Zhiyi Wan; Han Hu; Xin Lai; Pengyuan Lyu; Chengquan Zhang

name: Plover: Steering GUI Agents through Plan-Centric Interaction
summary: Plover exposes GUI-agent plans and replanning as persistent artifacts that users can inspect and edit during execution. Its planner–executor design supports localized correction through plan edits, language guidance and screenshot-grounded interventions, studied through failure repair and workflow scenarios.
authors: Madhumitha Venkatesan; Shicheng Wen; Jiajing Guo; Jorge Piazentin Ono; Liu Ren; Dongyu Liu

name: SeerGuard: A Safety Framework for Mobile GUI Agents via World Model Prediction
summary: Uses instruction screening and a safety-augmented world model to assess likely consequences of mobile GUI actions before execution.
authors: Xue Yu; Bo Yuan; Kailin Zhao; Pengshuai Yang; Hong Hu; Junlan Feng

name: Just A Rather Very Intelligent Spoken Agent
summary: Introduces JarvisBench, a benchmark for spoken mediation during long-horizon agent workflows, measuring task collaboration and how users follow ongoing execution.
authors: Chen Chen; Zhehuai Chen

name: EvoGUI: An Evolution-Aware Benchmark for GUI State-Transition Understanding
summary: Introduces EvoGUI, which derives temporal ordering, inverse action/value prediction, and successor-discrimination probes from recorded GUI trajectories. Its web-derived benchmark isolates transition understanding from the other abilities involved in end-to-end task success.
authors: Yaohan Yang; Minglei Shi; Borui Zhang; Jie Zhou; Jiwen Lu

name: Teach it to stop, not just to click
summary: Studies verifier-guided repair of a 35B computer-use agent across five environments, examining variation across runs and data draws in done detection, GUI clicks, and field entry.
authors: Barada Sahu; Shivesh Pandey

name: Sidekick: Designing Communication for Effective Multitasking with Computer Use Agents
summary: Introduces Sidekick, a communication interface that uses ambient status cues, multimodal action summaries, and visual and verbal explanations of reasoning to help people monitor computer-use agents. A user study examines progress awareness, error traceability, and multitasking across background and foreground interaction.
authors: Ruei-Che Chang; Wenqian Xu; Dingzeyu Li; Bryan Wang; Anhong Guo

name: SEE: Structure-aware Exploring & Exploiting for Long-horizon GUI Agent Trajectory Synthesis
summary: Introduces SEE, which first explores mobile interfaces to build a screen-and-element transition graph, then composes task trajectories through graph planning and controlled sampling. It studies coverage, loop avoidance, and transfer after training agents on the generated sequences.
authors: Zhuohang Fan; Beichen Zhang; Yuanfa Li; Changqiao Wu; Wei Liu; Jian Luan; Weigang Zhang

name: Broken Gates: Re-evaluating Web Bot Defenses in the Age of LLM Agents
summary: Measures how autonomous LLM browser agents interact with commercial bot-management and anti-automation defenses on the web.
authors: Behzad Ousat; Nikita Turkmen; Lalchandra Rampersaud; Dillan Bailey; Amin Kharraz

name: DocOps: A Verifiable Benchmark for Autonomous Agents in Complex Document Operations
summary: Introduces DocOps, a verifiable benchmark for agents handling complex digital-document workflows, with analysis of state tracking, semantic checks, and structural edits.
authors: Jiazhen Jiang; Boxi Cao; Lingyong Yan; Yaojie Lu; Hongyu Lin; Shuaiqiang Wang; Dawei Yin; Xianpei Han; Le Sun

name: PersonaTrail: Benchmarking Personalized Web Agents through Browsing Trails
summary: Introduces PersonaTrail, a benchmark for personalized web agents using browsing histories, and PACMem, a structured memory method for guiding navigation.
authors: Seungbin Yang; Chaewoon Ki; Dohyun Lee; Jaegul Choo; ChaeHun Park

name: OpenForgeRL: Train Harness-native Agents in Any Environment
summary: OpenForgeRL connects stateful agent harnesses to reinforcement-learning infrastructure through a model-call recording proxy and isolated rollout containers. Its validation includes browser and computer-use agents, alongside tool-oriented agents, and examines how harness choice affects learned reliability.
authors: Xiao Yu; Baolin Peng; Ruize Xu; Hao Zou; Qianhui Wu; Hao Cheng; Wenlin Yao; Nikhil Singh; Zhou Yu; Jianfeng Gao

name: Beyond Sequential Interaction: Benchmarking Parallel Execution and Coordination for GUI Agents
summary: Introduces ParaGUIBench, with tasks and efficiency measurements for coordinated GUI agents operating separate desktop instances over a shared file system. Its ParaGUI planner-worker system decomposes tasks and dispatches concurrent subtasks for comparison with serial execution.
authors: Zedong Yu; Qianxing Li; Zhi Gao; Liuyu Xiang; Chenrui Shi; Yang Liu; Huiming Wu; Yujie Wei; Yuhao Fei; Yubo Fu; Zhaofeng He

name: StepX-Edge: An On-Device UI Vision-Language Model via Architecture-Training-Deployment Co-Design
summary: Introduces StepX-Edge, an on-device UI vision-language model for screen understanding, OCR, question answering, and element grounding on mobile chips.
authors: Yin Wang; Haotian Hu; Jineng Han; Wentao Qiu; Zhenhua Ge; Liujian Tang; Fanyi Wang

name: StateAct: Program State, before Pixels, for Long-Horizon Computer-Use Agents
summary: Introduces StateAct, a code-first computer-use harness that manipulates program state directly and delegates screenshot-and-click subgoals to a GUI agent. An independent completion gate checks saved outputs, while fresh subagents handle subgoals to limit accumulated context.
authors: Yan Yang; Xiangru Jian; Ziyang Luo; Zirui Zhao; Yutong Dai; Ziji Shi; Hanshu Yan; Jun Hao Liew; Silvio Savarese; Junnan Li

name: SeekJudge: A Practical Reward Framework for Reinforcement Learning in Computer-Use Agents
summary: Introduces SeekJudge, which iteratively searches and analyzes GUI trajectories to assess instruction fulfillment. The work combines dense judgment-data synthesis, a step-label benchmark, and reward-server scheduling to study accurate and practical reward feedback for agent training.
authors: Yang Wan; Zhenhao Zhang; Jierui Wang; Xiangxin Zhou; Linchao Zhu

name: Scaling GUI Agents with Visual State Transitions
summary: Introduces State Transition Pretraining, which jointly learns to infer actions from GUI changes and predict future states from current screens and actions. Subsequent instruction-trajectory fine-tuning tests whether these representations transfer to desktop and mobile agent tasks.
authors: Xiangyan Liu; Kaixin Li; Haonan Wang; Biao Wu; Meng Fang; Longxu Dou; Chao Du; Michael Qizhe Shieh; Tianyu Pang

name: Falsifiable Commitment Planning for Self-Correcting Web Agents
summary: Introduces FCPAgent, which attaches confirming and falsifying evidence to each skill-grounded plan step. A plan–test–repair loop checks actions and observations, then localizes contradictions so execution, skills, or plans can be revised at the appropriate level.
authors: Guangyi Liu; Huan Zhao; Quanming Yao

name: SafeFlow: Semantic Information-Flow Control for Blocking Malicious Propagation in Multi-Agent Systems
summary: Introduces SafeFlow, a semantic information-flow defense for multi-agent delegation, evaluated on safety tasks that include harmful web-agent behavior.
authors: Haowen Dai; Zonghao Ying; Wenfeng Li; Xiangfan Wu; Yisong Xiao; Tianyuan Zhang; Jiaye Lin; Lei Wei; Guangyuan Dong; Xitong Ling; Xixun Lin; Quanchen Zou; Xiangzheng Zhang

name: Interactive Reward Agent: GUI Task Evaluation via Environment-State Verification
summary: Introduces an Interactive Reward Agent that proposes completion conditions and verifies them using system, application, and GUI tools after execution. GUI-RewardBench provides annotated desktop trajectories for evaluating these evidence-based judgments and their use in reinforcement learning.
authors: Chenrui Shi; Yuwei Wu; Yang Liu; Ruining Feng; Zirui Shang; Zhi Gao; Lifeng Fan; Che Sun

name: Desktop-Delta Bench: Do Computer-Use Models Understand Desktop GUI Transitions?
summary: Introduces Desktop-Delta Bench, an offline diagnostic of GUI transition understanding using temporal-ordering tasks and before/after action inference. It includes decoy observations to test whether models track the source and task relevance of screen changes.
authors: Abhishek Pillai; Samir Kumar Nayak; Yuan Chen

name: OmegaUse-OfficeVal: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Long-Horizon Office-Suite Tasks with Economic Grounding
summary: Introduces OmegaUse-OfficeVal, a benchmark for long-horizon office-suite agent tasks with labor-time and price signals, plus rubric-based code verifiers.
authors: Jingbo Zhou; Yusai Zhao; Qi Bao; Jingjia Cao; Zhenghai Chen; Chang Gao; Kaiqi Guo; Muxin Guo; Mingxuan Li; Xinjiang Lu; Yanru Ma; Yixiong Xiao; Zenghui Zhang; Le Zhang; Hua Wu

name: Echoverse: Deep, Evolving Environments for Training Computer-Use Agents at Scale
summary: Introduces Echoverse, which compiles specifications into stateful applications with database-grounded graders and uses rollouts to improve both the environments and agent policies. It examines behavioral depth, targeted interface practice, and environment repair as sources of training value.
authors: Yash Pandya; Sahil Gupta; Sarthak Harne; Archana Yadav; Kavyansh Chourasia; Hussein Mozannar; Vibhav Vineet; Sara Abdali; Corby Rosset; Yash Lara; Ahmed Awadallah; Ece Kamar; Akshay Nambi

name: Qwen-UI-Agent Technical Report: Toward Next-Generation Real-World Centric Foundation GUI Agents
summary: Describes a foundation GUI agent with combined GUI and command-line actions, large-scale interaction infrastructure, and iterative environment and task generation.
authors: Hanzhang Zhou; Panrong Tong; Xu Zhang; Quyu Kong; Chenglin Cai; Tianyu Xia; Gongjie Zhang; Jianan Zhang; Long Li; Long Chen; Lei Wang; Gaole Dai; Pengxiang Li; Liangyu Chen; Yue Wang; Steven Hoi

name: MemHarness: Memory Is Reconstructed, Not Replayed
summary: Introduces MemHarness, which trains agents to critique and reconstruct retrieved experience before acting; WebShop is one of two evaluation environments.
authors: Rong Wu; Daocheng Fu; Licheng Wen; Xuemeng Yang; Shu Zou; Jianbiao Mei; Yuxin Wang; Hairong Zhang; Yu Yang; Tao Hu; Cong Zhang; Botian Shi; Pinlong Cai

name: How Benchmarks Mis-Score Computer-Use Agents
summary: Audits failure-scored computer-use trajectories to distinguish agent errors from broken tasks and evaluator false negatives. It organizes reliability issues across task construction, trajectory evidence, scoring, and reporting, then derives corresponding evaluation design practices.
authors: Zihan Dong; Zhiyuan Ma; Zekun Wang; Yunqing Li; Zirou Liu; Ruixuan Deng; Qishi Zhan; Rui Qian

name: Why Are GUI Agents Correct but Late? Decode on the Decision-Time Critical Path, Tested with Pre-Compiled Policy Trees
summary: Introduces Adaptive Anticipatory Policy Trees, which precompute guarded actions and deadlines during idle periods so transient GUI events can be handled without new text generation. Paired experiments examine when this prepared execution helps and when reactive control remains preferable.
authors: Zihan Dong; Rui Qian; Qishi Zhan; Dongshen Peng; Kaixin Li; Yu Li

name: Rethinking Inference-Time Scaling in Local Computer-Use Agents: Failure Modes and Compute Tradeoffs
summary: Examines inference-time scaling for local computer-use models by varying context, step budgets, decomposition, and parallel execution. OSWorld experiments track both task performance and changing failure modes, exposing cases where extra computation extends errors or adds coordination overhead.
authors: Woongkyu Lee; Jungwook Choi

name: OSReward: Instituting Standardized Evaluation for Cross-Platform Computer-Use Reward Models
summary: Introduces OSReward and its harder and multidimensional variants for assessing judgments of computer-use trajectories. It also releases a reasoning-annotated judgment corpus and trains reward models, examining reliability, leniency bias, and evaluation cost.
authors: Qiushi Sun; Kanzhi Cheng; Yian Wang; Bowen Yang; Hang Yan; Liheng Chen; Fangzhi Xu; Zichen Ding; Nuo Chen; Jialin Cao; Xingdong Gong; Zehao Li; Kaiming Jin; Xinfeng Yuan; Zhoumianze Liu; Jingyang Gong; Zhangyue Yin; Jiahui Gao; Zhiyong Wu; Tianbao Xie; Jianbing Zhang; Ben Kao; Lingpeng Kong

name: Alignment Is Local: A Paired Diagnostic for GUI Agents under User-Side Persuasion
summary: Presents a paired diagnostic of prompt guardrails in GUI agents under screen-grounded user persuasion, comparing single-turn probes with four-turn escalation.
authors: Haoxin An; Yunpeng Song; Zihao Bai; Zhongmin Cai; Guojun Xiong; Chenhao Lin; Wentao Chen; Feng Wei; Chao Shen

name: MAGA: Multi-Platform Self-Fusion of GUI Agents via Structured Action Distillation
summary: MAGA distills specialized GUI agents into one policy by allocating supervision according to structured-action correctness. A training-only teacher hint supports fusion across mobile, web and desktop settings without changing student inputs.
authors: Hang Yan; Zhangxuan GU; Beitong Zhou; Jiaxuan Chen; Runze Li; Yusong Hu; Shuheng Shen; Changhua Meng

name: From Monoliths to Swarms: A Study of Attack Surface Evolution in the Transition to Multi-Agent Web Systems
summary: Categorizes structural attack surfaces that emerge when single-agent browser systems are decomposed into multi-agent web workflows.
authors: Yashaswi Malla; Sandra Siby

name: RMSWeb: Reflection, Failure-Mode Mining, and Salvage-DS for Web Agent Reinforcement Learning
summary: Introduces RMSWeb, a training recipe for web agents that uses reflection retries, failure-mode mining, and Salvage-DS reward and sampling methods for web actions.
authors: Chengbo Liu; Lifang Zhou; Ruijie Yan; Pei Tan; Ao Sun; Haojun Huang; Guichun Hua; Sining Wei; Yining Chen; Yingying He; Yutao Xie

name: LongHorizon-Harness: Advancing Long-Horizon Agents for Real-World Tasks
summary: Introduces LongHorizon-Harness, which maintains verified task state outside an agent's execution context and audits subtasks; its evaluations include OSWorld~2.0.
authors: Ziyu Ma; Hailang Huang; Shun Zou; Yong Wang; Shidong Yang; Yiming Hu; Fei Wei; XiangXiang Chu

name: Invisible Ink Threats: Adversarial Goals Behind Legitimate Tasks in Computer-Use Agents
summary: Introduces II-Bench for low-harm indirect prompt injections against computer-use agents and HITLCUA for testing them in virtual-machine and web environments with simulated user review.
authors: Jia-Chen Zhang; Ze-Yu Zhang; Kai-Wei Zhang

name: Qwen-CUA: Native Computer Use for (almost) Everything
summary: Qwen-CUA operates through screenshots and keyboard/mouse events while compressing older visual history into reusable context blocks. Its report combines verifiable task generation, trajectory-based training and separate browser and Bash-augmented studies.
authors: Dunjie Lu; Shuai Bai; Tianyi Bai; Sicheng Fan; Chang Gao; Jian Guan; Feng Hu; Mianqiu Huang; Xingyang Huang; Yizhen Jiang; Yuheng Jing; Dehui Kong; Ning Li; Dayiheng Liu; Shixuan Liu; Zheng Liu; Que Shen; Bowen Wang; Junli Wang; Chencan Wu; Rui Xie; Tianbao Xie; Zhihui Xie; Haiyang Xu; An Yang; Tao Yu; Wenzhen Yuan; Xi Zhang; Zhenru Zhang; Mingkang Zhu; Zhaoqing Zhu; Yizhong Cao; Kai Dang; Binyuan Hui; Kaixin Li; Junyang Lin; Haiquan Wang; Zekun Wang; Yiheng Xu; Fan Yan; Mengqi Yuan; Danyang Zhang; Jiajun Zhang; Zhipeng Zhang; Fan Zhou; Fan Zhou
topics: reinforcement-learning; imitation-learning; data-generation; interaction-history; long-horizon; evaluation

name: CUADebug: Diagnosing and Repairing Computer-Use Agent Failures
summary: CUADebug combines a failure taxonomy and human-annotated OSWorld failure trajectories with an agent that locates causal steps and proposes corrections from screenshots and action traces. It evaluates root-cause diagnosis separately from controlled task re-execution and failure recovery.
authors: Weijia Zhang; Kunlun Zhu; Zeyi Liu; Yinting Chen; Tianyi Ma; Jiateng Liu; Jiaxun Zhang; Bingxuan Li; Xiangru Tang; Heng Ji; Jiaxuan You

name: GUI-Lens: Coarse-to-Fine Cropping for GUI Grounding with General-Purpose VLMs
summary: GUI-Lens uses OCR and detected interface components as coordinate references while a general-purpose VLM selects progressively enlarged screenshot crops. Instruction-conditioned checks constrain the crop and click proposals before mapping the final location back to the original screen.
authors: Zichuan Fu; Shirong Wang; Wenlin Zhang; Guojing Li; Yimin Deng; Jingtong Gao; Junjia Qi; Hanyu Yan; Yefeng Zheng; Xiaopeng Li; Wanyu Wang; Xian Wu; Xiangyu Zhao

name: Screenshots or Tools? Eliciting Tool Use and Managing Multimodal Context in Hybrid GUI-MCP Computer-Use Agents
summary: This study separates tool-adoption behavior from task competence in hybrid GUI–MCP agents. It tests tool-use incentives and screenshot-history compression, showing that changed action preferences can coexist with unchanged held-out accuracy.
authors: Siqi Fan; Minghao Li; Xiaoqian Ma; Wenhui Tan; Xiusheng Huang; Juntong Wu; Liujie Zhang; Shuo Shang; Weihang Chen

name: MissClick: Execution-Aware Adversarial Attacks on Coordinate Generation in GUI Grounding Models
summary: MissClick designs white-box attacks around the numerical effect of coordinate digits on executable GUI clicks. Separate untargeted displacement and targeted place-weighted objectives are evaluated across desktop, web and mobile grounding settings.
authors: Yu Ran; Wentao Zhao

name: FocusMem: Factorizing Content, Readout, and Trust in Latent GUI Memory
summary: Introduces FocusMem, a latent memory interface for GUI agents that separates stored content, state-conditioned readout, and a gate for irrelevant retrieved experience.
authors: Zhuoran Zhang; Bowen Li; Jingcheng Ju; Yang Shi; Qixun Wang; Haotian Wang; Wei Chen; Tengjiao Wang

name: LoginTrap: Uncovering Task-Agnostic Phishing-Style Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks against LLM-based Web Agents
summary: Introduces LoginTrap, a black-box indirect-injection evaluation in which attacker-controlled page context and login flows induce unauthorized authentication. It measures end-to-end private-data leakage across web-agent backbones, architectures and defenses.
authors: Longtao Guo; Zelin Zhang; Kaifeng Huang; Yang Shi

name: "Allow" to Achieve, Over-Privileged Inadvertently: The Unintended Cost of Task-Completion-Driven Pop-up Decisions in Mobile GUI Agents
summary: This permission-literacy study tests whether mobile GUI agents grant only task-necessary permissions. Controlled changes to task context and requester identity expose authorization biases and the trade-off between suppressing unnecessary and legitimate grants.
authors: Dongsheng Chen; Yuxuan Li; Guanhua Chen; Jiaxin Zhang; Xiangyu Zhao; Lei Ma; Xin Yao; Xuetao Wei

name: StepReflect: Structured UI Transition Reflection for Mobile GUI Agents
summary: StepReflect predicts structured per-action reflections from transition specifications and paired visual evidence. The paper distinguishes offline transition-label accuracy from online task success when the reflection model is integrated into mobile agents.
authors: Linqiang Guo; Wei Liu; Li Gu; Yang Wang; Tse-Hsun; Chen
topics: self-reflection; state-tracking; imitation-learning; reward-models; evaluation; efficiency

name: Activity Frames: Deterministic Screen-Activity Compilation for Agent Memory and Replay
summary: Introduces Activity Frames, a deterministic pipeline that turns captured screen activity into typed episodes for computer-use agent memory and routine replay.
authors: Nossa Iyamu

name: AppDeltaWorld: Transition-Grounded Delta Code World Model for Mobile GUI Agents
summary: AppDeltaWorld predicts executable code updates for the next mobile UI state, using transition-constrained retrieval and rendered visual assets. It evaluates reconstruction fidelity separately from policy training and adaptation using generated environments.
authors: Weikai Xu; Yunren Feng; Haoxiang Lei; Kun Huang; Yuxuan Liu; Kang Zhao; Xiaolin Hu; Shuo Shang; Bo An

name: The Next Screenshot Knows: Gated Hindsight Distillation for Mobile GUI Agents
summary: Gated Hindsight Distillation gives a teacher access to the next screenshot during training while the student sees only the available trajectory prefix. Distillation is applied when hindsight repairs a student failure, and the resulting policies are evaluated on Android tasks.
authors: Weiwei Li; Junzhuo Liu; Tong Chu; Hengfu Yu; Wen Li

name: Routing Is Least Learnable Where It Is Most Valuable: Bounds on Representation Routing for Web Agents
summary: Measures the complementarity, cost and rerun variability of six browser observation modes on WebArena and VisualWebArena. Its routing experiments distinguish an oracle cost opportunity from policies that fail to robustly outperform a fixed observation mode.
authors: Jiaming Wei; Zekun Wu; Adriano Koshiyama; Maria Perez-Ortiz

name: WebGrader: Training LLMs for Web Development with Self-Evolving Programmatic Grader
summary: Introduces WebGrader, a programmatic grader for website generation that plans interaction flows, runs them in a live browser, and uses observed outcomes as RL rewards.
authors: Boshui Chen; Huiping Liu; Shaolei Zhang

name: StepJack: Benchmarking Computer-Use Agent Safety Against Multi-Step Indirect Prompt Injection
summary: Introduces StepJack, a benchmark of indirect prompt injections that split an adversarial goal across pages on a computer-use agent's web navigation path.
authors: Zhuoxin Zhan; Akbar Rafiey; Avery Ma; Leila Pishdad; Layla El Asri

name: WebRider: Persona-Conditioned Intent Controllers for Live-Web Assistance
summary: Introduces WebRider, a live-web agent that maintains intent contracts while carrying out guarded browser actions, and RiderBench for auditing those contracts across websites.
authors: Zhi Li; Tao Zhou; Yeqing Li; Eugene Ie; Demetri Terzopoulos

name: MemPrism: Task-Conditioned Relational Memory Views for Long-Horizon Agents
summary: Introduces MemPrism, which records prior interactions and builds task-conditioned relational memory views for decisions in long-horizon web-agent tasks.
authors: Bingfan Zeng; Zhisheng Chen; Zhengwei Xie; Bangde Cao; Yuxuan Li; Jinhan Li; Zheng Lu; Xiangchen Guan; Zikai Xiao; Rui Qian; Jingwei Song

name: SynChain: Inducing Computer-Use Agent Systems to Construct Their Own Attack Chains
summary: Introduces SynChain, an attack that induces persistent agents to create poisoned skills or memory entries, and CUAChain for evaluating later attack-chain activation.
authors: Fuyao Zhang; Jiaming Zhang; Che Wang; Boyang Chen; Yurong Hao; Xiongtao Sun; Guowei Guan; Blaise Delattre; Yang Cao; Wei Yang Bryan Lim

name: AndroidReality: How Far Are Mobile Agents from the Real World?
summary: Extends AndroidWorld with controlled state, transition, and action perturbations to test mobile-agent robustness, and studies a training-free introspective recovery mechanism.
authors: Xiaoou Liu; Longchao Da; Hanyang Chen; Yuan Ling; Hua Wei

name: Back to the Future: A workbook time machine for spread sheet creation benchmarks
summary: Introduces the workbook time machine to create spreadsheet-object tasks and wtmbench to evaluate spreadsheet manipulation agents using different control interfaces.
authors: Mansi Uniyal; Agamdeep Singh; Ananya Singha; Priyanshu Gupta; Mukul Singh; Gust Verbruggen; Vu Le; Sumit Gulwani

name: CAP: A Scalable Benchmark for Evaluating Cross-Site Browser Agents with Complex Actions and Perception
summary: CAP builds cross-site browser workflows by decomposing websites into operation and perception requirements and recomposing them into tasks. Its judge-based evaluation diagnoses complex interactions and visual-perception failures across real websites.
authors: Zejun Xu; Taiyi Chen; Jin Li; Yongtong Gu; Qi Cheng; Aixuan Lv; Shuai Zhu; Pengfei Zhu; Kaichen Yang; Boyu Sun; Yixian Yang; Mulong Xie; Xin Liu; Dagang Li; Xiaoteng Ma; Hongru Wang

name: Not an A11y: How Android Accessibility Exposes Mobile AI Agents to Indirect Prompt Injection
summary: Demonstrates that unsanitized Android accessibility tree metadata exposes mobile GUI agents to stealthy indirect prompt injection attacks.
authors: Rahul Deivasigamani; Sayeda Faatin Alvi; Derqui Andrea; Kaushal Punjabi; Stjepan Picek

name: Software Engineering for and with GUI Agent
summary: Surveys 336 GUI-agent papers through a software engineering lens, covering architectures, evaluation, and lifecycle concerns in mobile and web settings.
authors: Shengcheng Yu; Yuchen Ling; Junyang Xing; Quan Zhou; Chunrong Fang; Zhenyu Chen

name: Hallucination-Free GUI Grounding via Regression-Free Layout-Aware Matching
summary: This framework separates frozen-model instruction expansion from a trained layout-aware matcher that localizes GUI elements without coordinate regression. Binary text/icon supervision supports the matcher, with evaluations on GUI grounding and Mind2Web element-selection tasks.
authors: Yuke Li; Xuehan Hou

name: LookAgain: Closed-Loop GUI Grounding with Visually Grounded Reflection
summary: LookAgain treats a GUI coordinate as a revisable hypothesis, rendering its marker and a local screenshot patch before confirmation. Reflective supervised trajectories provide a cold start, followed by GRPO using terminal grounding correctness.
authors: Renshan Zhang; Haoyang Meng; Yixiao He; Rui Shao; April Hua Liu; Liqiang Nie

name: Navigation Alone Is Not Enough: Evaluating Explanatory Assistive UI Agents
summary: Introduces NeXUI, an assistive UI-agent benchmark that evaluates navigation together with interface-grounded explanations and user oversight in recorded interface states.
authors: Santosh Patapati

name: DSAgentBench: Can Agents Automate End-to-End Data-Science Workflows in Real Computer Environments?
summary: DSAgentBench evaluates end-to-end data-science workflows spanning analysis, modeling and visualization inside a real desktop environment. Task evaluators check produced analytical and visual artifacts, while the released interface supports screenshot or accessibility observations and GUI actions.
authors: Mizanur Rahman; Mohammed Saidul Islam; Ridwan Mahbub; Md Tahmid Rahman Laskar; Shafiq Joty; Enamul Hoque Prince

name: SkillLens: Visual Skill Cards for Retrieval-Augmented GUI Action Prediction and On-Policy Distillation
summary: Introduces SkillLens visual skill cards for retrieved GUI action guidance and CardDistill for training an action-prediction student that runs without retrieval on website tasks.
authors: Zhou Liu; Chenxu Zhang; Ligang Huang; Zeli Su; Zewei Pan; Changhang Tian; Zhaoyang Han; Xing Chen; Yuanfeng Song; Wentao Zhang

name: Test-Time Self-Evolving GUI Visual Grounding via Reflection-Guided On-Policy Self-Distillation
summary: Introduces a Test-Time Self-Evolving framework for GUI grounding that explores unseen interfaces, reflects on predicted coordinates, and distills those reflections into the model.
authors: Shiyu Xuan; Zechao Li

name: Benchmarking LLM Judges for Mobile Agent Evaluation
summary: MobileJudgeBench compares completion judges against human labels on mobile-agent trajectories. It studies screenshot-sampling baselines, model-dependent error profiles and how judge quality relates to agent rankings and reinforcement-learning rewards.
authors: Ziqiang Wang; Li Gu; Zhixiang Chi; Zhi Liu; Seyed Mehdi Ayyoubzadeh; Yuanhao Yu; Yang Wang

name: CoAdapt-GUI: Joint Workflow Context and Policy Adaptation for Unseen GUI Applications
summary: Introduces CoAdapt-GUI, which adapts workflow context and policy from a mobile GUI agent's own rollouts and rewards when it encounters unseen applications.
authors: Linqiang Guo; Li Gu; Zihuan Jiang; Zhixiang Chi; Siobhan Reid; Ziqiang Wang; Yuanhao Yu; Wei Liu; Yang Wang; Tse-Hsun; Chen

name: SynWeaver: Website-Prior Task and Trajectory Co-Synthesis for Web Agents
summary: SynWeaver explores a website to build a map of page states and executable interactions, then learns website priors for task proposals. Joint task/trajectory synthesis revises inconsistent pairs and verifies or repairs the resulting supervision.
authors: Ruitao Wang; Yuwen Hao; Menglin Yang

name: LegacyWorld: Atomicity-Aware Evaluation of GUI Agents for Legacy Workflows
summary: LegacyWorld evaluates Windows GUI workflows under an atomicity criterion: finish correctly or fail without persistent unintended changes. It compares expert prompts with prompts derived from recorded golden paths and separates useful completion, safe failure and non-atomic side effects.
authors: Thilo Reintjes; Sivajeet Chand; Derui Zhu; Sushant Kumar Pandey; Alexander Pretschner

name: Act2Intention: A Benchmark For Developing Active Mobile Agents Through Inferring User Intention from GUI Actions
summary: Introduces intention understanding, prediction, and confirmed execution tasks over mobile GUI trajectories, with a proactive agent combining personalized intention models and experience-guided actions.
authors: Xiaokai Yan; Jingtao Ding; Yong Li; Zhiwen Yu

name: StateM: Reaching 95.3% Raw Accuracy, or a \$15 Frontier Run, on Terminal-Bench 2.1 via Harness Scaling
summary: Introduces StateM, a stateful runtime with checked transitions and reusable runbooks for long-horizon agents; its reported evaluations use terminal and business tasks.
authors: Ziheng Qin; Yaxin Lu; Zhangyang Atlas Wang; Kai Wang

name: UI-Mate: Advancing Open-Weight Foundation GUI Agents with In-Context Demonstrations
summary: Combines environment-grounded training with demonstration-conditioned workflows, and introduces OSWorkerBench for extended office-task evaluation.
authors: Zihan Ding; Longxu Dou; Qi Gao; Xiangwu Guo; Shengchao Hu; Zilong Huang; Zihang Jiang; Lei Ke; Mengcheng Lan; Weixian Lei; Hanxuan Li; Honglin Li; Xiyun Li; Zaitang Li; Leowei Liang; Xin Luo; Haozhe Ma; Jiayi Mao; Zhoujie Pan; Can Qin; Tianyuan Qu; Weiqi Wang; Wenkai Wang; Yonglin Wang; Yuxin Wang; Chenxu Wu; Yingchen Yu; Chenyu Zhang; Yuhao Zheng

name: Agentic ESOpt: Fine-Tuning Long-Horizon LLM Agents with Minimal GPU Requirements
summary: Introduces Agentic ESOpt, an evolution-strategies fine-tuning framework for long-horizon agents, evaluated on WebArena-Lite web tasks and automatic heuristic design.
authors: Zhi Zheng; Rongsheng Chen; Yunpeng Ba; Zhenkun Wang; Yee Whye Teh; Wee Sun Lee

name: Wuying-Browser-Agent: Real-World Centric Fundamental Long-Horizon Browser Agents
summary: Combines a browser execution framework, recovery-oriented supervision, and online reinforcement learning, with a bilingual live-web task benchmark.
authors: AIMAE Team; Tianxiang Chen; Yan Cheng; Zhangye Han; Xiaowei Li; Chang Liu; Cheng Liu; Zhongqiang Ma; Long Peng; Xiaobing Tu; Yinggui Wang; Hongliang Wei; Chen Wu; Daiping Xin; Kunyu Zhou; Pengyang Zhou; Peiyuan Chen; Ziyuan Chen; Yutao Deng; Chunyu Dong; Xiangyu Fu; Yicheng Feng; Ruian He; Haochen Li; Miancan Liu; Zhengqin Liu; Wei Peng; Jinkui Ren; Haoyu Tan; Dong Xiao; Rongkun Xue; Shujian Yang; Xianhang Ye; Ziqi Yuan; Ziyang Yu; Linghan Zhang; Xiantao Zhang; Xuanpu Zhao; Yinan Zhao; Zhenghui Zhao; Bin Zhu; Likai Zou

name: MobileWorldSafety: Benchmarking GUI Agent Safety Against Environmental Injection Attacks in Android Apps
summary: Evaluates environmental injection risks in Android tasks using programmatic risk checks and model-based adjudication of ambiguous cases.
authors: Sujin Chen; Lijun Li; Tianyi Du; Jing Shao

name: ComponentBench: Diagnosing Component-Level Failures in Computer-Use Agents
summary: ComponentBench evaluates short interactions with canonical web UI components using verified tasks and matched human reference trajectories. Its diagnostic pipeline compares observation/action representations and analyzes structural difficulty, failure patterns and interaction efficiency.
authors: Tianchen Guan; Xinlei Lin; Royce Cheng-Yue; Xiangjun Wang; Shuyan Zhou

name: Inducing Task Models from Computer-Use Traces
summary: Task Model Induction disentangles concurrent activities in screenshot and mouse/keyboard traces, then constructs hierarchical goals and procedural control flow for each task. Evaluation tests reconstruction of observed execution and reuse of derived skills on held-out tasks.
authors: Yucheng Jiang; Zora Zhiruo Wang; Ruishi Chen; Diyi Yang

name: Towards Faithful Simulation of Human Shopping Behavior
summary: Presents RecVerse, a screenshot-based shopping simulation agent with hierarchical memory and trajectory-level RL, alongside USB, an interactive e-commerce GUI trajectory dataset.
authors: Jiakai Tang; Yan Mi; Jing Yu; Yang Zhang; See-Kiong Ng; Qi Cao; Fei Sun; Xu Chen; Wen Chen; Jian Wu; Han Zhu; Bo Zheng

name: Automated Trajectory Evaluation for Mobile Agents via Step-Level Consequence Reasoning and Aggregation
summary: Introduces CRATE, a step-level visual judge for mobile-agent trajectories, and CRATE-S for assessing operational safety from action-conditioned state changes.
authors: Pengshuai Yang; Zijing Gao; Xue Yu; Benhui Zhuang; Bo Yuan; Junlan Feng

name: Lexical Coupling in GUI Element Grounding: Sentence Embeddings Track Labels across Mobile and Web
summary: Studies whether text-embedding GUI grounding scores reflect semantic matching or recovery of visible labels. Same-screen ranking comparisons with lexical baselines expose differences between deployable fusion, oracle selection, and performance on label-poor targets.
authors: Qijia Chen; Giulio Jacucci

name: Beyond Success and Failure: Length-Aware Contrastive Learning for GUI Agents
summary: Introduces LACL-GUI, a contrastive learning objective that distinguishes trajectory quality within both successful and failed GUI executions. It favors concise successes and uses divergence from successful trajectories to differentiate failures during policy optimization.
authors: Chengyang Gu; Le Zhang; Jingbo Zhou; Yize Chen; Yu Shi; Siqi Bao; Zheng-Fan Wu; Hua Wu; Hui Xiong

name: GUI-Primitives: Diagnosing Spatial Reasoning Failures in Vision-Language GUI Grounding
summary: Introduces GUI-Primitives, a paired-instruction benchmark that changes a spatial relation while holding the screenshot and anchor fixed. Its diagnostics separate failure to localize either candidate from failure to choose the candidate satisfying the relation.
authors: Md Abrar Jahin; Md Rizwan Parvez

name: Training Needs Trustworthy Worlds: Verified Synthetic Web Environments for Agent Learning
summary: Builds synthetic websites with verified navigation, backend state, and feasible tasks to provide reliable supervision for web-agent training.
authors: Chenghao Zhang; Yuxi Cheng; Saisai Hu; Canran Xiao; Yikai Mao; Dan Roth

name: Spine-Branch Coordination for Multi-agent Computer Use
summary: Introduces Spine-Branch Coordination, which assigns a main task flow to one virtual-machine state and uses parallel branch machines to gather information for computer-use agents.
authors: Mian Zhang; Manasi Sharma; Sheng Zhang; Minglai Yang; Kejian Shi; Ying Liu; Zhiyu Zoey Chen; Daniel Yue Zhang

name: ClawProBench: Trace-Aware Evaluation of AI Agents with Runtime Coverage and Frozen Workplace-Style Holdouts
summary: Introduces ClawProBench, a trace-aware benchmark for agents on OpenClaw that scores workspace and native-runtime tasks using execution traces, safety checks, and process quality.
authors: YuanHang Xiao

name: CausalCache: Conditional High-Fidelity Restoration for Long-Horizon GUI Agents
summary: Introduces CausalCache, which selects archived screenshots to restore alongside text summaries under a fixed visual-memory budget. A history-gated adapter processes restored images, with evaluation distinguishing standard step limits from longer-horizon and mobile-transfer settings.
authors: Jiaxuan Luo; Zhanfeng Liao; Jiayao Teng; Yuan Wang

name: GSAR: Goal-State-Anchor Rewards for Mobile GUI Agents with Self-Evolving Data Synthesis
summary: Introduces GSAR, which synthesizes GUI tasks and successful goal states, then annotates task-relevant interface elements as reward anchors. These anchors support offline trajectory verification and online policy training.
authors: Long Zhang; Yuhan Chen; Chaoran Zhang; Wanxia Cao; Kun Huang; Pengzhi Gao; Wei Liu; Jian Luan; Chenliang Li; Lixin Zou

name: Reflection with Action-Induced Visual Differences for Desktop GUI Agents
summary: Introduces Evidence-First Reflection, which separates extraction of action-induced screen changes from judgment of whether an operation achieved its objective. It filters visual differences into relevant evidence before a desktop agent’s reflector decides how execution should continue.
authors: Yijie Ma; Chaoyue Niu; Fan Wu; Guihai Chen

name: WebMCP-Phalanx: Enforcing and Characterizing Trust Boundaries for Browser-Integrated LLM Agents
summary: Proposes WebMCP-Phalanx, a browser-integrated runtime that binds page-exposed tools to their registering principals and separates content inspection from privileged invocation. It studies lifecycle and prompt-injection attacks, including a timing bypass that motivates validating all visible metadata before tool use.
authors: Lin-Fa Lee; YI-YU Chang; Kuo-Hui Yeh

name: Are Android GUI Agents Robust Against Runtime Anomalies? AnTrap: Evaluating Agents in Dynamic Adversarial Environments
summary: Introduces AnTrap, which injects task-solvable runtime anomalies into Android GUI-agent trajectories using a layered failure taxonomy. It compares model robustness and adversarial reinforcement learning to distinguish recoverable interface traps from persistent contextual failures.
authors: Guo Gan; Yilun Zhao; Cong Chen; Jinbiao Wei; Tingyu Song; Zheyuan Yang; Lin Fu; Hong Zhou

name: Task-Adaptive Rubrics for GUI Reward Modeling
summary: Introduces AdaptRubric, which retrieves reusable criteria for a GUI task family and then generates instruction-specific checks for concrete values and constraints. It evaluates these adaptive rubrics in offline reward assessment and online agent optimization.
authors: Tao Xiong; Xavier Hu; Wenkai Wang; Qinzhuo Wu; Changqiao Wu; Pengzhi Gao; Wei Liu; Jian Luan; Shengyu Zhang

name: BrowserForge: Scaling Web Episode via Parallel Browser Sandboxes
summary: Introduces BrowserForge, which combines broad website sourcing, parallel browser sandboxes, and task-proposer/solver interaction to collect verified web trajectories. The pipeline uses page structure during synthesis but trains a policy that acts from screenshots.
authors: Fei Tang; Huawen Shen; Zhiqiong Lu; Zhengxi Lu; Pengyuan Lyu; Chengquan Zhang; Weiming Lu; Jun Xiao; Yueting Zhuang; Yongliang Shen

name: MCP-Driven Accessibility Tree Standardization for AI-Powered Screen Reader Agents
summary: Proposes an MCP architecture that presents accessibility trees from Windows, macOS, Android, and web frameworks in a common form for LLM assistive agents interacting with GUIs.
authors: Vishnu Ramineni; Nitin Saksena; Akash Kumar Agarwal; Darshan Mohan Bidkar; Balakrishna Pothineni; Durgaraman Maruthavanan; Lokesh Butra; Siva Kumar Chintham

name: From Blind Edits to Verified Repair: Building Trustworthy User-Side LLM Agents for Web Accessibility
summary: Builds a local browser-extension agent that generates and verifies additive CSS repairs for WCAG web accessibility violations.
authors: Lily Bundgaard Wanscher; Markus Heidemann Lorensen; Mohammed Ammad Shafiq; Mahyar Tourchi Moghaddam; Mina Alipour

name: LocalLSTC: A Long Short-Term Control Architecture for Locally Deployed GUI Agents
summary: Introduces LocalLSTC, a training-free control architecture that maintains persistent task state and uses it to form short execution commitments. Outcomes feed back into that state for progress checks, recovery, and termination in locally deployed desktop agents.
authors: Weiming Li; Helen Paik; Yulei Sui

name: GameWAM: A World Action Model for Video Games
summary: Introduces GameWAM, a model for native game play and GUI control that predicts future visuals and keyboard-mouse actions from synchronized gameplay and GUI trajectories.
authors: Yuncheng Guo; Zhanqiu Zhang; Yiwen Guo; Weijia Li

name: ADeptS-Bench: Measuring the Trustworthiness of Computer Use Agents Across Devices
summary: Evaluates interface-embedded threats and whether computer-use agents seek clarification when mobile or desktop instructions are ambiguous.
authors: Joy Chen; Alejandro Castillejo Munoz; Pierluca D'Oro; Yuxuan Sun; Chloe Evans; Joseph Tighe

name: ASIL: Replacing Screenshot-and-Click with Structured State and Semantic Actions
summary: ASIL exposes application state as structured JSON and provides code-executable semantic actions. Its application benchmark compares this interface with screenshot control and application-native APIs, and studies supervised and reinforcement learning on the structured interface.
authors: Rui Xie; Lu Chen

name: Benchmarking General Mobile Assistants in Challenging Real-World Scenarios
