summary: Introduces GMA, a benchmark of 300 mobile-assistant tasks across seven applications, and studies how agent context retention and state tracking affect complex workflows.
authors: Yiqi Zhu; Feiyu Gao; Jiaxing Fan; Jiahui Zeng; Minggang Wu; Chenliang Li; Haiyang Xu; Peng Li; Ming Yan; Yang Liu

name: WM-R1: Training GUI Agents to Reason and leverage World Models with Reinforcement Learning
summary: Uses learned world models for mobile-agent training rollouts and for reasoning about the consequences of candidate GUI actions.
authors: Yu Han; Tianwen Qian

name: CURA: Certified Runtime Alarms for Computer-Use Agents
summary: Introduces CURA, a telemetry-based runtime monitor that turns computer-use trajectories into sequential failure alarms and can trigger mid-task oversight. Its certificate controls false alarms, while the study separately reports detection performance and limits of retrospective monitoring.
authors: Divake Kumar; Sina Tayebati; Devashri Naik; Amanda Sofie Rios; Nilesh Ahuja; Omesh Tickoo; Ranganath Krishnan; Amit Ranjan Trivedi

name: Iron: Intent-Aligned and Retrospective Dual Learning Framework for Enhancing Generalist Virtual Agents
summary: Introduces Iron, a GUI-agent training framework that aligns low-level actions with high-level intent using cycle-consistency rewards. It also repurposes failed trajectories through hindsight reconstruction and evaluates transfer to other digital tasks.
authors: Jiahe Ying; Wendong Bu; Kaihang Pan; Bingchen Miao; Siyu Chen; Wen Wang; Xueming Jiang; Juncheng Li; Siliang Tang

name: Learning Simple Test-Time Environments for LLM Web Agents
summary: Introduces Test-Time Environment Decomposition, which uses trial interaction to break complex web observations into simpler modules. A label-free adaptation procedure learns from these sub-environments and studies whether their gains compose in full web tasks.
authors: Junxuan Li; Zijun Liu; Ziyi Huang; Peng Li; Yuzhou Liu; Ming Yan; Yang Liu

name: A Systematic Survey of Agentic Skills: Architecture, Lifecycle, and Security
summary: Surveys modular agentic skill architectures, skill lifecycles, and security risks in autonomous tool- and interface-using agents.
authors: Sanket Badhe; Deep Shah; Priyanka Tiwari; Nehal Kathrotia

name: ActReal: System-Level Mobile Agents Challenge Mobile Automation Detection
summary: Introduces ActReal, which translates semantic mobile-agent actions into coordinated touch and sensor signals to study automation-detection weaknesses. It evaluates detectors that observe touch events alone or together with inertial measurements under a privileged executor threat model.
authors: Mingshuo Wang; Hanqing Guo; Huining Li; Yuliang Fu; Jing Xu; Chenhan Xu

name: SIR: Self-improving Red-teaming for Compute Use Agents
summary: Introduces SIR, which iteratively refines a reusable library of prompt-injection strategies from failed computer-use attack trajectories. Its evaluation uses deterministic system-state checks and counts attacks only when the adversarial objective and legitimate task both complete.
authors: Chen Xiong; Zhiyuan He; Pin-Yu Chen; Stjepan Picek; Tsung-Yi Ho

name: WebWorld: The Browser as a World Model for Self-Improving Web Code
summary: Uses typed browser interaction contracts to accept web-code improvements only when target progress and previously verified capabilities are preserved. Accepted transitions supply self-improvement data.

name: UI-Venus-2 Technical Report
summary: Describes a GUI foundation agent trained through expanded environments, function-grounded tasks, and trajectory verification with safety-aware execution mechanisms.
authors: Venus Team; Zhuohan Cai; Haoxing Chen; Jiaxuan Chen; Weizhi Chen; Changlong Gao; Zhangxuan Gu; Yuan Guo; Yusong Hu; Jianrong Jiang; Jianguo Li; Runze Li; Jinzhen Lin; Zhenyu Ma; Changhua Meng; Han Peng; Xinyu Qiu; Shuheng Shen; Zhongyi Shui; Weiqiang Wang; Ming Wen; Zhuoer Xu; Hang Yan; Kaiwen Yang; Ruilin Yao; Nanjun Yu; Zhengwen Zeng; Lianrui Zhang; Yunzhu Zhang; Zhe Zhao; Beitong Zhou

name: GUI-CC: Benchmarking Contextual Consistency of GUI World Models as Agent Environments
summary: Introduces GUI-CC, a benchmark for assessing GUI world models as multi-step agent environments. Separate reference-action and agent-loop tracks test whether generated screens preserve context, plausible transitions, and task progress throughout interaction.
authors: Lin Fu; Zheyuan Yang; Tianhui Zhang; Jinbiao Wei; Guo Gan; Boxu Liu; Yilun Zhao; Yu Rong

name: Are We There Yet? Assessing Computer-Use Agents for Blind Users' Accessible Interaction with Desktop Applications
summary: A diary study deploys the screen-reader-accessible OLLA computer-use prototype with blind users across desktop applications. Recorded commands and interaction traces support model comparisons and analysis of grounding, planning, constraint tracking and termination failures.
authors: Satwik Ram Kodandaram; Monalika Padma Reddy; Xiaojun Bi; Jiawei Zhou; I. V. Ramakrishnan; Vikas Ashok

name: Monitoring Web Agents Without Internal Signals: Observable Trajectories and Key-Step Supervision
summary: Predicts web-agent failure risk from observable trajectory prefixes using cross-step behavior and black-box consistency queries. Key-step labels preserve valid early prefixes of failed runs, and evaluation tests early intervention and transfer across website categories.
authors: Sitong Pan; Yipeng Shen; Yilin Lu; Caiwen Ding; Lu Cheng; Qianwen Wang

name: OmegaUse-SOP: SOP Engineering for Professional Computer Use from Human Demonstrations
summary: OmegaUse-SOP converts expert GUI demonstrations into configurable procedures and refines them with domain rules and human input. It records, abstracts, grounds and verifies live execution, with a case study of photovoltaic simulation workflows in PVsyst 7.2.
authors: Yixiong Xiao; Lang An; Hucheng Yang; Pinxue Ma; Yongquan Chen; Jingjia Cao; Yusai Zhao; Ting Wang; Ting Liu; Siqi Bao; Jingbo Zhou; Hua Wu

name: WiP: Characterizing and Defending Against Mobile-Agent-Driven MFA Automation
summary: Studies how mobile automation can combine authentication factors within one agent environment and evaluates motion sensing as a user-presence signal.
authors: Yimeng Liu; Hua Huang

name: Efficient GUI Agents: A Systems Survey of Observation, Memory, Action, and Runtime Optimization
summary: Surveys GUI-agent efficiency beyond task success: observation, context and memory, action, and planner or runtime cost.
authors: Bizhe Bai; Jiakang Yuan; Hongming Wu; Xinyue Wang; Jie Ren; Siyao Chen; Yuchen Ya; Fan Bai; Pai Peng; Huafeng Qin; Tao Chen

name: CA-OPD: Confidence-Aware On-Policy Distillation for Structured Visual Prediction
summary: Introduces CA-OPD, a confidence-guided distillation method for visual prediction, evaluated on GUI grounding and optical character recognition benchmarks.
authors: Menghao Li; Linjie Mu; Haotian Hu; Yannian Gu; Lujiayi Xue; Liujian Tang; Yu Zhang; Fanyi Wang

name: Discriminative World Models for Web Agents
summary: Trains discriminative web world models to distinguish the true next state from outcomes of alternative actions. Branching web trajectories support training, followed by tests of predicted-state matching, process-reward action ranking and end-to-end WebArena-Lite selection.
authors: Kelvin Li; Dhruv Pendharkar; Anish Pahilajani; Chuyi Shang; Leon Oks; Leonid Karlinsky; Rogerio Feris; Trevor Darrell; Roei Herzig

name: Tail-Likelihood Reinforcement Learning
summary: Introduces Tail-Likelihood Reinforcement Learning (TailRL), an RL objective that favors rare high-reward rollouts; GUI grounding is one of several evaluation tasks.
authors: Shrinivas Ramasubramanian; Daman Arora; Fahim Tajwar; Guanning Zeng; Qingyang Wu; Zhongzhu Zhou; Chenfeng Xu; Haiwen Feng; Yuda Song; Aarti Singh; Ruslan Salakhutdinov; J. Andrew Bagnell; Jeff Schneider; Andrea Zanette

name: Do GUI Agents Know When Not to Act? Enabling Conflict-Aware Termination for Multimodal GUI Agents
summary: CONFLICTGUI evaluates termination under instruction conflicts and mismatches between instructions and interface context. CONFLICTGUARD couples feasibility checks with conditional action modulation to reduce unnecessary execution while tracking normal-task behavior.
authors: Zhaoyuan Huang; Tianjie Ju; Pengzhou Cheng; Zheng Wu; Yansi Li; Chuanbiao Song; Jun Lan; Huijia Zhu; Weiqiang Wang; Zhuosheng Zhang

name: ElderBench: Benchmarking Autonomous Mobile Agents for Older Adults
summary: ElderBench evaluates mobile GUI agents on smartphone requests elicited from older adults, including indirect and underspecified language. Online and offline tests, instruction normalization and linguistic analyses examine how these request patterns contribute to failures.
authors: Weide Zhan; Qumu Shaqu; Yuanqing Liu; Peng Zhang; Jiahao Liu; Kam Him Lam; Ning Gu; Zhan Hu; Tun Lu

name: From Interaction Traces to Persistent Skills: Online Evolution for Computer-Use Agents
summary: An online skill-evolution framework turns GUI interaction traces and evaluator feedback into a versioned library of reusable procedures without updating model parameters. Controlled OSWorld comparisons examine both the benefits of shared procedural memory and its domain-dependent instability under repeated revision.
authors: Longtao Hu; Xiao Liang; Linchao Zhu

name: CUA-Universe: A Scalable and Dynamic Environment for Hybrid GUI+CLI Agents
summary: Turns desktop applications into reproducible GUI-and-CLI environments and generates verified hybrid trajectories for agent post-training.
authors: Haoting Shi; Wenhao Wang; Weicheng Fang; Yaozhong Liang; Tian Jin; Pengxiang Zhao; Guangyi Liu; Siheng Chen; Yanfeng Wang

name: SCAFFOLD: Self-Improving Web Agents via Recursive Parametric Skill Abstraction
summary: Introduces SCAFFOLD, which extracts executable skills from web trajectories, composes them into a hierarchy, and compresses redundant skills through behavioral checks. It periodically distills skill-guided trajectories into the policy and studies repeated improvement across web benchmarks.
authors: Bowei He; Xiaokun Zhang; Meng Ding; Xue Liu

name: When and What to Teach: Budget-Aware Online Adaptation for Web Agents
summary: Proposes an online teaching framework that decides which web-agent episodes warrant a stronger teacher and which trajectory turns merit training. A solvability gate and score-guided trimming aim to preserve first-attempt performance while reducing teaching and training costs.
authors: Jianwei Zhang; Sihan Cao; Pengcheng Zheng; Ya Wen; Pei Ke; Kuien Liu; Shen Gao; Wei Dong; Yang Yang; Chaoning Zhang

name: Beyond the Verdict: Evidence-Aligned Evaluation of Visual Prompt-Injection Guardrails
summary: Introduces Mind2Web-Injection, a benchmark for evaluating web-agent guardrail decisions on instruction-screenshot pairs using evidence boxes and image-side counterfactuals.
authors: Suyoung Lee; Myungsub Choi

name: OmniStepBench: Deployment-Aware Agent Evaluation across Modalities and Task Complexity
summary: Introduces OmniStepBench, a shared-environment benchmark for evaluating multimodal agents on multi-step tasks, tool use, and delivered artifacts under one scoring protocol.
authors: Yu Liu; Zhilin Liu; Zhiwei Yang; Shaojie Zhang; Zheyuan Deng; Tingwei Huang; Zhenbo Luo; Lei Jiang; Yanbing Liu; Pei Fu

name: Selective Knowledge Control for Continual GUI Agent Learning over Application Streams
summary: Introduces activation-conditioned gradient control for GUI agents learning successive applications. It protects inactive application-specific neurons, constrains updates to shared neurons, and accumulates a compact historical state to balance adaptation with retention.
authors: Zirui Shang; Xin Shu; Yang Liu; Zhi Gao; Xinxiao Wu; Lifeng Fan

name: Improving Proficiency and Efficiency of Android GUI Agents via Self-Generating Tool Actions
summary: DroidTool generates application-state tools through proposal, implementation, testing and repair. Relational tests connect the tools’ preconditions and effects, and the resulting tools are evaluated as additions to Android GUI agents.
authors: Juyong Lee; Woogyeol Jin; Kimin Lee

name: FinCUABuild: Can Agents Build Reliable Benchmarks for Dynamic Financial Computer Use?
summary: Introduces FinCUABuildBench for assessing financial computer-use task construction and FinCUABuildAgent for generating tasks, environments, and validators.
authors: Jingpu Yang; Fengxian Ji; Jinri Guo; Tianhao Li; Qian Jiang; Fan Zhang; Min Peng; Qianqian Xie; Preslav Nakov; Zhuohan Xie

name: APPSim-Bench: Bridging Real-world Apps and Reproducible Evaluation for Mobile GUI Agents
summary: Introduces controlled simulated mobile apps with deterministic backend data and outcome checks for reproducible evaluation of realistic interactions.
authors: Jintian Feng; Long Chen; Xiao Yu; Jiayi Dai; Chenglong Liu; Haoru Wang; Zizhen Xue; Yuxuan Shi; Ziyang Wang; Yichen Gong

name: AgentHijack: Visual Patch Attacks on Multimodal Computer-Use Agents
summary: AgentHijack evaluates whether visual patch effects propagate from screenshots through model outputs and action parsing into real environment changes. Its controlled web-page experiments distinguish intermediate attack signals from verified end-to-end consequences.
authors: Zhihao Liu; Hongyu Sun; Zhiyuan Fu; Xiaonan Duan; Jice Wang; Shangru Zhao; Weizhi Meng; Wuxin Yang; Yangfan Zhou; Yuqing Zhang

name: GraphDroid: Asynchronous LLM-Based Mobile App GUI Testing via History-Aware Exploration and Hybrid Intent Fulfillment
summary: GraphDroid combines clustered memory of visited GUI states with asynchronous test-intent generation. A hybrid executor reserves LLM calls for complex intents and uses heuristics for simpler ones, evaluated through Android app coverage, bug discovery and crash detection.
authors: Xiaolei Li; Jialun Cao; Zhijian Hou; Yuzhi Zhao; Yepang Liu; Shing-Chi Cheung

name: TRACE: Trajectory-robust Admission with Evidence Ordering for Efficient GUI Agents
summary: TRACE orders screenshot evidence for monotonic visual-token reduction using layout priors, instruction relevance and feature novelty. Spatial token reserves and incremental KV contraction aim to preserve useful evidence for future GUI targets without repeatedly encoding retired frames.
authors: Yuhao Wang; Mu Qiao; Xindong Zhang; Yunzhi Zhuge; Lei Zhang; Huchuan Lu

name: JarvisGUI: Towards Cross-Device GUI Agents with Dynamic Task Composition
summary: JarvisGUI composes typed input-output task transformations into dynamic workflows spanning Android, Windows and Ubuntu devices. Its virtual-environment benchmark tests transfer of intermediate results, shared state and cross-device dependencies.
authors: Zixiang Chen; Yuheng Lu; Zihao Cheng; Zeming Liu; Jizeng Bai; Ziye Huang; Zhiyin Lin; Zihan Li; Yuhang Guo; Yunhong Wang; Haifeng Wang

name: BlueLM-GUI Technical Report: A Real-Device-Centric Flywheel for Self-Improving Mobile GUI Agents
summary: Describes a mobile-agent training pipeline centered on real-device rollouts, recovery of useful supervision from failures, and evolving evaluation tasks.

name: VRL-Bench: Benchmarking agents on computer control tasks under finite trial budgets
summary: Introduces VRL-Bench to compare trial-and-error learning for computer-control agents under limited attempts, and VEX² to schedule exploration and exploitation.
authors: Yu Bai; Yukai Miao; Dawei Wang; Li Chen; Yanyu Ren; Yuqian Shi; Dan Li; Ying Xiong; Chengqiu Tan; Run Zhou; Li Li

name: LLaDA-UI: Bringing Block-wise Diffusion to Vision-Language GUI Agents
summary: LLaDA-UI adapts block-wise diffusion generation to a vision-language GUI agent through multimodal pretraining and GUI supervised fine-tuning. It evaluates grounding and navigation across multiple platform settings.
authors: Zhangxuan Gu; Haoxing Chen; Qi Qin; Yi Xin; Kai Gan; Lin Liu; Long Cui; Xiaomei Wang; Beitong Zhou; Yunzhu Zhang; Zhengwen Zeng; Changlong Gao; Weizhi Chen; Rongchao Zhang; Haoyuan Wu; Shuheng Shen; Changhua Meng; Weiqiang Wang; Jianguo Li; Zhenzhong Lan

name: Token Efficient Task Execution via Application Behavior Modeling for Web Agents
summary: OdoBot builds a model of web-application behavior from successful task demonstrations and uses it to guide task execution. Its Canvas LMS evaluation compares token use and completion with existing web agents.
authors: Alexandru Ianta; Eleni Stroulia

name: AutoTailor: Automatic, User-Aligned Capability Selection and Adaptation for Web Agents
summary: AutoTailor compiles web trajectories into reusable browser-automation APIs, then filters and dynamically revises the capability inventory. WebArena experiments distinguish API-only operation from an agent that can fall back to ordinary reasoning and browser actions.
authors: Xinyun Cao; Adriana Szekeres; Fazle Elahi Faisal

name: PriMobiBench: Characterizing Visual Privacy Leakage in VLM-Driven Mobile GUI Agents
summary: PriMobiBench evaluates direct privacy leakage and user profiling from mobile GUI screenshot trajectories, supported by the MobiLeak trace dataset. It also tests masking sensitive, task-irrelevant interface elements before cloud processing and measures the resulting privacy and utility trade-off.
authors: Qihang Cen; Tianshuo Cong; Da Song; Xinlei He; Jiaxing Song; Ke Xu; Qi Li

name: CoArena: Evaluating Computer-Use and Multi-Agent Systems in Real Time
summary: Introduces CoArena, an evaluation method where user tasks run concurrently in sandboxed desktops and blind pairwise judgments update a public leaderboard.
authors: Nitish Kovuru; Prateek Jannu

name: Learning from Reliable Negatives: Confidence-Anchored Test-Time Adaptation for GUI Grounding
summary: Confidence-Anchored Learning uses coordinate-token confidence to filter pseudo-supervision for GUI grounding. Its negative-only variant performs label-free test-time updates to reduce reliance on potentially incorrect positive examples.
authors: Yizhou Liu; Fei Tang; Yuchen Yan; Zhengxi Lu; Songqin Nong; Tao Jiang; Wenhao Xu; Wenqi Zhang; Weiming Lu; Jun Xiao; Yongliang Shen

name: RSIAgent: Autonomous Exploration for Recursive Self-improvement in New Environments
summary: Introduces RSIAgent, a training-free framework that explores unfamiliar digital interfaces, stores environment-specific action knowledge, and reuses that memory for later tasks.
authors: Sibo Zhu; Shicheng Fan; Xinyue Wang; Wenyi Wu; Kun Zhou; Biwei Huang

name: AnchorGUI: Asymmetric Memory for Dual-Scale Learning in GUI Navigation
summary: AnchorGUI compares expected and observed UI transitions and selectively retains screenshots when they disagree. This asymmetric memory supports immediate correction and focuses cross-attempt experience distillation on likely failure steps.
authors: Shengjie Jin; Zelong Sun; Hengbo Xu; Yanbiao Ma; Zhiwu Lu

name: CADWorld: Computer-Use Benchmark for Long-Horizon Computer-Aided Design
summary: CADWorld evaluates screenshot-and-GUI agents on long FreeCAD workflows, from modeling and assembly to manufacturing and simulation. Executable checks inspect saved engineering artifacts for geometry, constraints, construction structure and downstream state.
authors: Zihan Dong; Yuanzhe Liu; Zhiyuan Ma; Qishi Zhan; Dehan Kong; Guohao Li; Kaixin Li

name: EchoPath: Execution-Level Replayable Memory for GUI Agents
summary: EchoPath turns validated GUI trajectories into parameterized replay procedures with explicit runtime preconditions. Image-based target matching adjusts stored coordinates, while ambiguous steps fall back to bounded repair or fresh planning.
authors: Yao Zhao; Aditya Shanmugham; Swastik Roy; Yanxun Xu
topics: memory; workflow; automation; grounding; efficiency; robustness

name: When Agents See Differently: Exposing UI Desynchronization Threats in Mobile Agents
summary: Investigates mismatches between what humans see on a mobile display and what agents receive through screenshots or accessibility metadata. An automated evaluation framework embeds instruction-agnostic perturbations into functional APK clones and compares static and dynamic agent deviations with human noticeability.
authors: Heng Li; Fulin Zhao; Zhe Geng; Zhiyuan Yao; Wei Yuan; Xiapu Luo

name: RiskChainBench: A Benchmark for Obfuscated Platform Message Restoration and Evidence-Grounded Web Investigation
summary: Introduces RiskChainBench, pairing obfuscated-message restoration with web-agent investigation of linked sites in labeled local web environments.
authors: ZhuoXin Liu; Zhiming Ma; Ying Zhang; Mengzheng Yang; Yifan Wang; Zhengqi Huang; Yanhan Zhou; Zekun Lin; Jun Zhang; Shun Zhang; Yue Chen; Qiao Zhao; Peng Chen

name: Reflect, Revise, Reuse: Training-Free Skill Evolution for GUI Agents
summary: EvoSkill-GUI revises reusable skill files from execution feedback through an executor–critic loop. It studies how training-free updates to localization, recovery and procedure information help subsequent mobile and desktop tasks.
authors: Bofan Chen; Boxuan Zhang; Fei Tang; Zhengxi Lu; Yong Du; Tongbo Chen; Weiming Lu; Jun Xiao; Yueting Zhuang; Yongliang Shen
topics: memory; training-free; self-reflection; robustness; long-horizon; workflow

name: ERPBench: A State-Grounded Evaluation Paradigm for Computer-Use Agents in Enterprise Software
summary: ERPBench evaluates screenshot-only agents in enterprise software using database values to check the business records produced by their actions. It pairs these state-based checks with a harness for human approval and analyzes cases where visible completion masks incorrect persisted data.
authors: Kratika Bhagtani; Kusha Sridhar; Maziyar Baran Pouyan; Yuying Zhao; Eugene Siow

name: The Verifiable Action Card: Trustworthy Human-in-the-Loop Control for Secure Autonomous Agents
summary: Presents the Verifiable Action Card (VAC), a browser approval mechanism that derives confirmations from pending actions and binds user approval to execution.
authors: Hasnain Irshad; Anam Mughees; Neelam Mughees; Abdullah Mughees; Imtiaz Ali Soomro

name: RankGround: Efficient High-Resolution GUI Grounding via Lightweight Reranker-Guided Crop Selection
summary: RankGround trains a lightweight reranker to select a promising screenshot crop before one VLM localization call. Ranking supervision uses containment and boundary-aware augmentation, with pointwise and listwise training stages.
authors: Liyang Fan; Xinping Bi; Yitai Li; Shuaimin Li; Hui Li; Min Yang

name: Affora: A Design System for Agent-Friendly Interfaces
summary: Presents Affora, a design system with reusable components and executable checks for interfaces used by computer-use agents, informed by studies of components and visual variation.
authors: Jin Gao

name: EconSkills: Studying Skill Transfer and Retrieval for Web Agents on Live Economic Data
summary: EconSkills converts verified economic-data browsing traces into parameterized procedures with navigation, verification and recovery guidance. Its evaluation separates known-skill transfer from library retrieval, exposing the limits of approximate matches to new tasks.
authors: Yinzhu Quan; Zefang Liu

name: A Dual-Process Perspective on Nudge Susceptibility in LLM-Based GUI Agents
summary: Studies how automatic defaults and reflective social-influence cues affect GUI-agent shopping decisions under different reasoning configurations. A randomized simulated-shopping experiment finds that reasoning changes the type of susceptibility.
authors: Haya Halimeh; Sascha Kaltenpoth; Kevin Bösch; Oliver Müller

name: RecreationWorld: Scalable and Verifiable Environments for Hybrid Computer-Use Agents
summary: RecreationWorld gives hybrid agents running reference applications to explore and recreate using native GUI controls and coding tools. Its multi-platform benchmark checks interaction-dependent behavior with programmatic and visual assertions, while trajectory-training transfer is evaluated separately.
authors: Shuai Bai; Jiayong Deng; Sicheng Fan; Yikun Fu; Chang Gao; Xuhao Hu; Mianqiu Huang; Yizhen Jiang; Yuheng Jing; Dehui Kong; Keliang Li; Ning Li; Wanli Li; Dayiheng Liu; Dunjie Lu; Changwei Luo; Que Shen; Zheyuan Wang; Zijian Wang; Jie Wu; Gao Wu; Zhihui Xie; Rui Xie; Haiyang Xu; An Yang; Jiakang Yuan; Yanming Zhang; Jiajun Zhang; Xi Zhang; Zhenru Zhang; Zhuo Zhen; Mingkang Zhu; Bowen Zhou
environments: desktop; linux; macos; windows; android; web

name: MintAct: A Unified Visual Agent for Digital Environments
summary: MintAct trains a visual-agent family for grounding, navigation and tool use across mobile, desktop and web environments. Its shared infrastructure supports trajectory collection and asynchronous online RL while controlling cross-domain sampling and off-policy drift.
authors: Mingfei Gao; Rui Tian; Haiming Gang; Bohan Zhai; Le Zhang; Yuanzheng Gong; Di Feng; Ege Özsoy; Kaixin Ma; Vishwesh Kirthivasan; Oğuzhan Fatih Kar; Roman Bachmann; Anders Boesen Lindbo Larsen; Afshin Dehghan

name: Beyond Task Completion: Training Capable and Safe Computer-Use Agents
summary: Introduces SCOPE, which trains computer-use agents on ordinary task demonstrations, safe continuations around hazards, and explicit refusals. Its SCOPE-Gen pipeline pairs verifiable tasks with environmental-risk variants to support joint capability and safety training.
authors: Zeyu Kang; Zhenyun Yin; Yang Zhang; Shan He; Shanzhe Lei; Yanjiu Zhong; Xinquan Chen; Xuhong Wang

name: Seeing Through Conflicts: Improving Instruction Hierarchy Alignment in Vision-Language Models
summary: Studies reinforcement learning for vision-language models facing conflicting instructions across text and images, including evaluation on web-agent safety tasks.
authors: Nicholas Sansoterra; Zishuo Zheng; Sachin Kumar

name: MATE: Policy-Aware Security Auditing for Mobile Agents via Synthesis-Driven Trajectory Learning
summary: Introduces MATE, a policy-conditioned auditor for mobile-agent trajectories, and MATEBench for evaluating whether those trajectories violate app security policies.
authors: Changyue Jiang; Jiayi Wang; Xin Wen; Jiarun Dai; Geng Hong; Xudong Pan

name: How Many Pixels Is a Digit Worth? Place-Aware Coordinate Entropy for GUI Agent Confidence Estimation
summary: PACE weights coordinate-digit entropy by place value to estimate confidence in GUI clicks from one forward pass. It evaluates correctness ranking and selective accuracy against repeated-sampling alternatives on ScreenSpot-Pro and ScreenSpot-v2.
authors: Yunxiang Li; Xixin Wu; Helen Meng

name: OSWorld-Pro: Process-based Evaluation for Computer Use Agents
summary: Adds annotated intermediate subgoals to computer-use tasks and uses process-oriented evaluation to identify action and progress failures.
authors: Zhilin Wang; Shaokun Zhang; Yifan Zhang; Hao Zhang; Jin Xu; Binfeng Xu; Jian Hu; Yunheng Zou; Karan Sapra; Andrew Tao; Jan Kautz; Yi Dong

name: Towards Omni-dimensional GUI Agent Navigation with Masked Trajectory Prediction
summary: MaP unifies GUI-navigation objectives by masking and predicting components of multi-turn trajectories. Role-aware adapters address heterogeneous training data, and evaluations compare the approach with direct task-mixture training across navigation benchmarks.
authors: Yan Zhang; Pei Fu; Daiqing Wu; Huawen Shen; Ruoceng Zhang; Shaojie Zhang; Jiahui Yang; Yu Zhou; Can Ma; Zhenbo Luo; Jian Luan

name: CAVEAT: Towards Robust Computer-Use Agents in Incentive-Misaligned Environments
summary: Introduces CAVEAT, a controlled marketplace benchmark for testing whether delegated agents preserve user objectives when interfaces favor other outcomes. It diagnoses decision failures and studies harness interventions and targeted training to improve resistance to marketplace steering.
authors: Yuxuan Li; Will Epperson; Wesley Deng; Zezhou Huang

name: Learn How to Act from Your Own Interactions: On-Policy Self-Distillation for GUI Agents
summary: GUI-SD-v2 extends on-policy self-distillation from grounding to multi-turn GUI interaction. It first strengthens responses to privileged guidance, then selectively distills step-specific reasoning and memory support for later actions.
authors: Yan Zhang; Daiqing Wu; Huawen Shen; Liang Li; Gang Cao; Zhi Gong; Wei Dai; Xiaode Zhang; Can Ma; Yu Zhou

name: Guides That Cause Actions: An Offline Study of Guide-Action Mutual Reinforcement in Multimodal Web Agents
summary: WebMRE pairs guidance sentences with grounded actions in an offline benchmark derived from successful WebArena traces. Controlled decoding-prefix interventions test how guide content affects action selection, while separating offline prediction metrics from live browser task success.
authors: Chengguang Gan; Yunhao Liang; QingHao Zhang; Shiwen Ni

name: Invisible in Space, Visible in Time: Motion Vision CAPTCHA against GUI Agents
summary: MVCAP-Bench tests live browser CAPTCHAs whose foreground meaning emerges through motion against dynamic backgrounds. A foreground-only control separates temporal camouflage difficulty from answer format and browser interaction.
authors: Zeyu Zhang; Dingyi Rong; Zijian Chen; Zicheng Zhang; Xiongkuo Min; Guangtao Zhai

name: Improving LLM-based Autonomous Web Agents with Filtering
summary: Trains HTML-element relevance filters on Mind2Web trajectories and transfers them to WebArena to reduce irrelevant browser context. It also evaluates a zero-shot ColBERT retriever and documents baseline web-agent failure modes.
authors: Zhitong Guo; Jing Yu Koh; Ruiyu Li

name: Qwen-Planner-Agent: A Closed-Loop AI-for-AI Framework for Real-World Mobile Planner Agents
summary: Trains a mobile planner with supervised trajectories and competence-adaptive RL, then couples typed tool execution with memory, skills and offline model-harness refinement.
authors: Tingyu Qu; Weigao Sun; Yuecheng Liu; Yucheng Zhao; Yi Zhu; Yifeng Ding; Qiyi Wang; Sihan Cao; Pengkun Jiao; Hanlei Xie; Xiongwei Wu; Qichao Wang; Haodong Zhang; Jiajun Liu; Yuhao Wang; Yuqing Xie; Junpeng Zhao; Long Chen; Ming Ma; Sihan Yang; Ziwang Zhao; Yanhao Jia; Liangquan Gong; Feida Zhu; Yiran Zhong; Steven Hoi
topics: planning; data-generation; reinforcement-learning; memory; mobile-navigation; efficiency

name: Jev-Mobile: Jev as an Executor for Mobile GUI Agents
summary: Separates occasional visual-language planning from frequent lightweight action selection over an accessibility-tree-based action space.
authors: Linghua Zhang

name: The Hard Part Comes After Search: Benchmarking Web Agents on Synthesizing, Organizing, and Displaying Knowledge
summary: KNOWS benchmarks browser workflows that retrieve and synthesize information into documents, presentations and spreadsheets. Task-specific evaluators combine deterministic checks with model judgments, distinguishing partial progress from usable end-to-end artifact completion.
authors: Alexander Gill; Md Farhan Ishmam; Xuyen Nguyen; Neha Bhat; Parker Henry DeYoung; Fateme Hashemi Chaleshtori; Nathan Stringham; Kenneth Marino; Ana Marasović

name: From Tapping to Hopping: Augmenting Mobile GUI Agents with App-Native Deeplinks
summary: GUI-Hopper combines verified Android deeplinks with GUI actions, using landing-screen descriptions, hybrid trajectory training and reinforcement learning to select navigation shortcuts and recover through GUI control.
authors: Yuchen Sun; Chenglin Cai; Gongjie Zhang; Tianyu Xia; Quyu Kong; Panrong Tong; Zhengwen Zeng; Long Chen; Steven Hoi; Chongyang Zhang; Yue Wang
topics: mobile-navigation; tool-integration; data-generation; imitation-learning; reinforcement-learning; efficiency

name: OpenVAM: Open-World Visual Attention Modeling with VLMs
summary: Combines dense saliency prediction with explanations of attended elements, including webpage layouts; evaluates human-attention agreement and textual rationales on static inputs.
authors: Kiana Hooshanfar; Amirhossein Kazerouni; Alireza Hosseini; Michael Brudno; Babak Taati

name: CaptchaArena: A Large-Scale, Fine-Grained Dataset for Training Computer-Use Agents on Interactive CAPTCHAs
summary: Introduces CaptchaArena, a dataset of execution-verified interactive CAPTCHA solutions with screenshot–action trajectories, reasoning annotations, and pixel masks for irregular targets. The work trains a single policy across CAPTCHA types using supervised learning followed by verifier-reward reinforcement learning.
authors: Zhenhao Zhang; Zhaoyu Fan; Haohan Ying; Jingwen Hu; Hancen Fan; Junhao Zhou; Zitian Chen; Linchao Zhu

name: ScreenHaystack: Finding Blind Zones in GUI Grounding
summary: Moves controlled target icons across high-resolution interfaces to diagnose spatial blind zones in grounding models and study targeted augmentation.
authors: Chenyue Li; Xiaoxiao Sun; Yubo Deng; Qinlin Zhao; Serena Yeung-Levy; Yuhui Zhang

name: REBASE: Device-Cloud Experience Coherence for GUI Agents Across App Updates
summary: Introduces REBASE, a device–cloud protocol for repairing cached GUI experience after app updates. It combines cloud replay, device-side step verification, and progressively richer failure reports to produce repairs tied to application versions.
authors: Beining Wu; Jun Huang; Yanxiao Zhao

name: PastForward: Faster On-Device GUI Agents via Computational Experience Reuse
summary: Introduces PastForward, which reuses earlier output sequences as verified decoding proposals and starts future action computation from predicted GUI transitions. Screen checks determine whether speculative computation and cached model states can be retained.
authors: Taehwan Park; Changmin Lee; Hayeon Lee; Taesik Gong

name: From Trajectories to Grounded Preferences: Process Preference Synthesis via Interaction Element Graphs for Web PRMs
summary: Introduces SURFPRM, which turns web demonstrations into an interaction-element graph for synthesizing grounded negative actions. Its contrastive preference data trains process reward models to distinguish plausible on-page alternatives and guide downstream trajectory search.
authors: Yangzhe Peng; Xiaoyang Wang; Yiyang Zhao; Lijun Wu; Kun He

name: DashAct: A Progressive Diagnostic Benchmark for GUI Agents in Interactive Dashboard Analysis
summary: Diagnoses dashboard-agent failures by progressively restoring interaction context, next-action support, and visual target information within the same task.
authors: Chuhan Zhang; Qi Xie; Ziyue Wang; Jianing Yin; Yunfan Zhou; Dazhen Deng; Yingcai Wu

name: Learning from Others, Acting for You: Cross-User Memory Sharing for LLM Agents
summary: ShareMem consolidates reusable experience across users while keeping preference retrieval user-bound; its web evaluation predicts target elements and actions on recorded Mind2Web states.
authors: Jinming Hu; Haodong Zhao; Qi Jia; Die Chen; Tianhang Zhao; Sufeng Duan; Gongshen Liu

name: CUA-SWE: When Computer-Use Agents Meet Visual Software Engineering
summary: Introduces CUA-SWE, a benchmark and execution environment that combines code changes with graphical interaction and visual inspection of running software. Task-specific tests verify repairs and changes whose required information may be available only through the application interface.
authors: Prince Zizhuang Wang; Chenhao Liang; Zelong Xu; Aojie Yuan; Xiaolin Zhou; Haiyue Zhang; Yue Zhao; Xiyang Hu; Shuli Jiang

name: The GUI Is Not the State: Diagnosing State Aliasing in GUI World Models
summary: Introduces StateAliasBench to isolate GUI world-model ambiguities in which matching visible screens and actions can lead to different futures. It augments frozen world models with structured state recovered from interaction history and evaluates the effect on prediction and agent execution.
authors: Dongsheng Liu; Chao Jin; Wenkui Yang; Hejin Wang; Junwei Yang; Zeren Zhang; Ziwei Chen; Huaibo Huang; Jie Cao; Ran He

name: CUA-Sandbox: Efficient Environments for Computer-Use Agent Reinforcement Learning
summary: Introduces CUA-Sandbox, which separates each rollout’s mutable state from shared initialized software runtimes. State-scoped execution and transactional resets or branches aim to reduce training-environment costs while retaining original interfaces and evaluators.
authors: Xin Yan; Zhengbo Jiao; Jiaqi Liu; Zhenglin Wan; SiYuan Ma; Xuliang Yu; Tianyi Jiang; Chubin Zhang; Pengfei Zhou; Wangbo Zhao; Xingrui Yu; Bo An; Yang You; Ivor Tsang

name: AgentTell: Behavioural Side-Channel Leakage in Browser-Use Agents
summary: Introduces AgentTell, a benchmark for privacy leakage through browser actions after an agent learns a private fact on another website. It examines whether agents choose revealing options despite nondisclosure instructions and whether their final reports accurately describe that behavior.
authors: Asif Shahriar; Md Nafiu Rahman; Sadif Ahmed; Farig Sadeque; Md Rizwan Parvez

name: ORBIT: A Framework for Multi-Agent Safety and Security Evaluations
summary: Inspect-based framework that varies multi-agent roles, communication, attacks and defenses, with BrowserGym and virtual-desktop GUI adapters alongside coding and other tool scenarios.
authors: Ben Hagag; William L. Anderson; Srija Chakraborty; Christian Schroeder de Witt

name: Relevance Does Not Imply Applicability: Experience Activation for Personal GUI Agents
summary: Introduces ExpActivator, which matches the current GUI state to relevant historical states before supplying past actions as guidance. A separate activation rule decides whether a recurring user intent is warranted by the current time and situation or should be withheld.
authors: Fuyao Zhang; Xuan Wang; Zherui Li; Jiaming Zhang; Longtao Huang; Wei Yang Bryan Lim

name: Probe to Act: Elevating Browser-Use Agent via Active Visual Probing
summary: Introduces Probe to Act, which lets browser agents request visual evidence linking DOM handles and screen regions before committing an operation. It retains selected interaction evidence as memory and studies both prompted use and distillation into open models.
authors: Keliang Li; Heng Wang; Chen Hu; Daxin Jiang; Hong Chang; Shiguang Shan

name: GUITAR: Structured Failure Diagnosis of GUI Agents via State Transitions
summary: Introduces GUITAR, which groups visually different screens into functional states and analyzes agent failures over a state-transition graph. It uses the resulting bottlenecks to diagnose recurring mobile and web errors and evaluate targeted guidance.
authors: Shaoqing Zhang; Kehai Chen; Xuefeng Bai; Zhuosheng Zhang; Pengfei Zhang; Yang Xiang; Min Zhang

name: Same Tasks, Different Apps: Why Mobile GUI Agents Fail to Generalize?
summary: Introduces AnyAppBench, a live Android benchmark that holds user goals fixed while changing the application used to achieve them. It combines category-controlled task pairs with failure annotations to distinguish task understanding from application-specific execution skill.
authors: Tien Tran; Namho Koh; Daiki E. Matsunaga; Ayush Jain; Kee Eung Kim

name: One Rollout Is All You Get: Fully Test-Time Adaptation for GUI Agents
summary: Defines a test-time adaptation setting with one counted attempt per arriving GUI task and no ground-truth feedback. Its SOLO method filters or relabels completed episodes, then updates a small adapter from a short window of the agent’s own experience.
authors: Ziqiang Wang; Li Gu; Zhixiang Chi; Linlian Jiang; Zihuan Jiang; Linqiang Guo; Siobhan Reid; Zhi Liu; Yang Wang

name: LongPuzzleBench: Evaluating GUI Agents on Long-Horizon Visual Puzzles
summary: LongPuzzleBench evaluates coherent long-horizon planning on persistent visual puzzle boards through native GUI actions. It compares GUI-only and code-assisted agents and uses controlled hints and memory diagnostics to examine decisions that preserve or eliminate future solutions.
authors: Bingo Zhang; Haochuan Lu; Zongjie Li; Genjian Li; Ari Yu Zhang; Chaozheng Wang

name: Before Acting, Change the State: Prospective State Intervention for Web Agents under Deceptive Interfaces
summary: Introduces Veer, a runtime defense that changes task-relevant web state when an otherwise valid proposed action would produce an unauthorized consequence. It plans a prospective intervention and grounds and verifies its execution before the base agent continues.
authors: Ruozhao Yang; Mingfei Cheng; Xiaofei Xie

name: WebPageBench: Event-Level Verification and Controlled UI-Variant Generation for Web Agents
summary: Verifies web tasks through typed interface events and generates controlled UI variations while preserving instructions and success conditions.
authors: Anton Emelyanov; Maria Tikhonova; Zaven Martirosian; Sergei Averkiev; Alena Fenogenova

name: PhoneCLI: From App Interfaces to Callable Commands for Mobile Agents
summary: Introduces PhoneCLI, which explores mobile app interfaces and compiles navigation paths into reusable commands without internal app APIs or instrumentation. At execution time it verifies compiled paths and falls back to a visual agent for open-ended interaction or failed navigation.
authors: Yangqin Jiang; Lingrui Xu; Chao Huang

name: SPECTRA: On-Device Cognitive Perturbation and Trajectory Analysis for Autonomous Edge-Cloud GUI Grounding
summary: Introduces SPECTRA, an edge-cloud GUI grounding framework that uses visual perturbations and trajectory analysis to decide when to request a cloud model.
authors: Zhan Qu; Hui Zang; Ran Chen; Tao Wang; Shengyu Zhang

name: Constructing Challenging Browser-Use Tasks by Controlled Environment Interventions
summary: BreakingWeb pairs solvable browser tasks with controlled environment interventions that preserve the goal, target and backend success criterion. The paired evaluations isolate robustness failures, including agents declaring completion without the required state change.
authors: Xunjian Yin; Tianchen Guan; Jinao Wang; Weili Cao; Daisy Xinlei Lin; Royce Cheng-Yue; Keagan Long; Kyle Wong; Bhuwan Dhingra; Xiangjun Wang; Shuyan Zhou

name: Structured Interaction, Visual Localization, and Robust Execution for Complex Web Tasks: A Technical Report on the WebRetriever Challenge
summary: Describes a WebRetriever agent that combines semantic webpage operations with visual localization when structured representations are insufficient. Hierarchical context management and fault-aware execution support processing tasks across concurrent browsers.
authors: Ziqi Zhang; Shaohui Li; Bing Li

name: SCOUT: Synergizing Reasoning and Tool-Use for Computer-Use Safety
summary: Introduces SCOUT, a safety verifier that first derives task-specific completion and safety rubrics from a computer-use trajectory, then actively probes the resulting environment for evidence. It evaluates whether these two stages detect harmful consequences that screenshots alone can miss.
authors: Jianxing Chen; Xiao Yu; Shipra Agrawal; Zhou Yu

name: AdaptArena: Evaluating Test-Time Personalization of Web Agents
summary: Introduces AdaptArena to test whether web agents can infer unstated user preferences from relevant past trajectories and carry those preferences into new tasks. Its AdaptiveAgent baseline separates preference-retrieval challenges from failures in downstream web execution.
authors: Dongchan Shin; Xing Han Lù; Jiaqi Deng; Jay Gala; Tomás Vergara Browne; Jaewon Moon; Fengyuan Liu; Alexandre Drouin; Siva Reddy; Alexandre Lacoste

name: PrecogUI: Proactive GUI Agents via Pre-cognitive Simulation and Experience Retrieval
summary: Presents PrecogUI, which retrieves prior anomaly and success patterns and predicts symbolic UI transitions before choosing actions. It also introduces InterfereBench, generated for evaluating long GUI workflows with disruptive events and recovery requirements.
authors: Bin Kang; Jiarui Ouyang; Li Jiang; Bin Chen; Zhuotao Tian

name: Neuro-Symbolic Computer Use: Learning Reusable Policies for Reliable and Efficient Execution
summary: Learns reusable computer-use policies that encode stable workflow logic in programs while delegating grounding and state checks to neural models. Policy iteration executes variants, diagnoses failures, revises the program, and adds verification before state-changing actions.
authors: Hyewon Suh; Thanh Minh Nguyen; Chih-Lun Lee; Darrow Hartman; Lizhao Liu; Xin Eric Wang; Ang Li; Jiachen Yang

name: SCA: Spatial Credit Assignment for Reinforcement Learning of GUI Agents
summary: Introduces Spatial Credit Assignment, which uses click coordinates to refine group-relative reinforcement-learning updates for GUI grounding. It distinguishes failed clicks by spatial evidence while leaving the deployed action policy unchanged.
authors: Shengtian Yang; Ziyu Xiong; Kaibing Yang; Guangfeng Cai; Yewen Li; Peng Jiang; Gai Kun; Qingpeng Cai; Lei Feng

name: MatToolBench: Benchmarking Multimodal Agents in Real-World Materials Science Workflows
summary: Introduces MatToolBench, a Windows-based materials-science benchmark combining GUI operation, scientific-software scripting, and database queries. Expert-defined subcriteria support partial-credit scoring, while the evaluation examines domain knowledge gaps and cross-tool handoff failures.
authors: Mei Wu; Rui Xie; Runyu Zhang; Yuqiang Li; Tianfan Fu; Bo Chen; Kai Yu; Xin Chen; Lu Chen

name: Absorbed in Inertia: Activation Analysis for Computer-Use Agents
summary: Studies repetitive, unproductive actions in desktop agents through their internal activation states. It proposes Reset, Reroute, Restore, a context intervention that temporarily resets an agent’s trajectory and later restores it to help escape repeated ineffective behavior.
authors: Giulio Segalini; Zhi Wen Soi; Jérémie Decouchant; Lydia Chen

name: EngiWorld: What Can Frontier Agents Deliver in Professional Engineering Environments?
summary: Introduces professional engineering tasks across software domains, with GUI and CLI access and artifact checks for geometric, physical, and design validity.
authors: Hongcheng Gao; Hailong Qu; Yu Lei; Henghui Sun; Haoyang Li; Yipeng Wei; Naihao Xue; Xiaohan Yu; Zhuo Tao; Yihe Zang; Yajiao Wang; Jingyi Tang; Yi Li; Jingjing Zhou; Jie Luo; Bohan Zeng; Chengyu Shen; Hao Jiang; Chong Chen; Bowen Qu; Olive Huang; Zeqiang Wang

name: HybridCUA: Learning to Orchestrate GUI and CLI for Computer-Use Agents
summary: Trains computer agents on verified GUI, command-line, and interleaved trajectories to learn when and how to combine interaction modes.
authors: Tongbo Chen; Junbo Niu; Zhengxi Lu; Niu Lian; Fei Tang; Yuchen Yan; Yike Hong; Yong Du; Yizhou Liu; Bofan Chen; Yongliang Shen

name: RealGUINoise: An Interactive Cross-Platform Benchmark for GUI Agent Robustness under Real-World Interface Noise
summary: Evaluates interactive GUI agents under varied realistic interface noise, comparing task completion, safety, and behavior with clean-environment runs.
authors: Yongjiang Wu; Junyuan Zhang; Ada Chen; Kuiyi Gao; Wenxuan Wang

name: SimTrace: Grounded Multimodal User Trajectories Generation for Online User Modeling
summary: Introduces SimTrace, a framework that generates synthetic multimodal web clickstreams by pairing a computer-use client agent's actions with web observations and user context.
authors: Yunan Lu; Shuang Xie; Meghna Allamudi; Mingyu Zhao; Han Li; Lingyun Wang; Zhou Yu

name: StateFork: Branchable Infrastructure for Agent Exploration
summary: Introduces StateFork and Waypoint for branching and restoring terminal-agent sessions so agents can explore multiple paths while preserving execution state.
authors: Jiakai Xu; Tianle Zhou; Georgios Liargkovas; Danielle Gillai; Ruizhe Fu; Patrick Shen; Eugene Wu; Kostis Kaffes

name: Action Conditioned Bisimulation For GUI Agent Memory
summary: Defines a GUI-memory merge rule that treats two states as equivalent only when shared actions lead to matching outcomes and successor states. The training-free method replaces observation-similarity merging and is tested in closed-loop MiniWoB++ interaction.
authors: Hongbo Zhang; Liuyang Song; Quanquan Li; Daqian Yang; Yan Wen; Zhengtao Yao

name: Talk2Agent: Benchmarking Voice Interfaces for Text Agents
summary: Introduces Talk2Agent, a benchmark of spoken instructions for computer-use tasks that measures whether voice interfaces preserve task-critical information. It pairs human speech with an execution-free intention-based metric and checks how that metric relates to downstream task completion.
authors: Terumi Chiba; Guangzhi Sun; Zheqi Yuan; Chao Zhang

name: ReSAIL: Mitigating Collapse in Iterative Agent Self-Distillation
summary: Introduces ReSAIL, an augmentation for iterative agent self-distillation that selects informative interaction steps; it also tests GUI-agent action prediction.
authors: Shengjie Jin; Hengbo Xu; Zelong Sun; YuJie Guo; Zhiwu Lu

name: Learning Reliable GUI Agents under Imperfect Priors
summary: Combines structured GUI exploration with training designed to tolerate imperfect retrieved experience. It builds state-transition graphs and synthetic task trajectories, then injects realistic forms of interface drift so agents learn when to rely on or reject prior guidance.
authors: Bo Han; Qianyi Wang; Shuai Liu; Xiong Zifan; Changqiao Wu; Yuanfa Li; Pengzhi Gao; Wei Liu; Jian Luan; Heng Qu; Yunpeng Song; Zhongmin Cai

name: OSWorld-Science: A Benchmark of Computer Use Agents for Learning and Using Scientific Software
summary: Benchmarks computer agents on scientific-software workflows with task-specific checks of application states and generated research artifacts.
authors: Dingyuan Dai; Heli Qi; Lei Liu; Yinxi Li; Baiding Chen; Zijun Dou; Qingcheng Zeng; Qi Kang; Oliver Sun; Eric Wang; Bo Zhou; Haixin Wang; Yufan Du; Shi Bo; Ruihan Lin; Mengqi Yuan; Dunjie Lu; Steven Dillmann; Yiming Shi; Tina Su; Amy Xin; Minghao Liu; Xi Wang; Xu Huang; Ge Zhang; Pengyu Nie; Zhen Yang; Jie Tang; Juanzi Li; Weihao Xuan; Tianyu Liu

name: ComputerSD: Online Self-Distillation from Real-Time Feedback for Computer-Use Agents
summary: Introduces ComputerSD, which turns feedback from executed GUI transitions into online self-distillation guidance and step-level scores. A GUI analyzer supplies these signals, which are combined with trajectory-level reinforcement learning in asynchronous training.
authors: Yong Du; Tongbo Chen; Zhengxi Lu; Yizhou Liu; Bofan Chen; Tao Jiang; Wenhao Xu; Yongliang Shen

name: cua-speedrun: Standardized Benchmarking of the Speed of Computer-Use Agents
summary: Standardizes virtual machines, interaction pipelines, and agent interfaces to compare computer-use speed, cost, and task performance.
authors: Pranjal Aggarwal; Lawrence Keunho Jang; Sean Welleck; Daniel Fried; Ruslan Salakhutdinov; Jing Yu Koh

name: GUI-HARVEST: Self-Improving GUI Agents through Evidence-Driven Harness Evolution
summary: Improves GUI-agent execution code by analyzing action effects and repeated-task failures, then validating bounded changes with frozen model weights.
authors: Geyi Yang; Zikun Qu; Xiang Li; Zhiyong Wang; Min Zhang; Shipei Zeng; Zhongxiang Dai

name: AutoGUIWorld: Image Generators as Visual World Models for GUI Agent
summary: Introduces AutoGUIWorld, which combines task planning and image editing to synthesize action-grounded GUI trajectories without running the depicted software. It filters generated transitions and tests whether training on them improves agents operating real desktop and scientific applications.
authors: Cheng Yang; Yifan Wu; Yutao Huang; Zhaohua Zhang; Beiduo Chen; Muxi Chen; Chenchen Zhao; Hexuan Deng; Haolin Yang; Geyuan Zhu; Sa Zhu; Jianhuan Zhuo; Qiuyong Xiao; Jianhao Ruan; Yiran Peng; Jiayi Zhang; Tian Ye; Xinlei Yu; Tianwen Jiang; Jihong Zhang; Yuyu Luo

name: Auditing Web Agent Evaluation on WebArena-Lite: Human Review of Outcomes and Trajectories
summary: Audits WebArena-Lite outcomes and trajectories with human review to identify automatic-evaluator false negatives and the first consequential execution errors. It also studies explicit execution-state memory and procedural guidance, showing why final task scores can miss substantial differences in agent behavior.
authors: Chengguang Gan; Zimeng He; Yoshihiro Tsujii; Ken-ichiro Kobayashi; Hiroki Itoh; Kotaro Funakoshi

name: Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents
summary: Studies how to route different parts of GUI experience into model weights or runtime context. It separates locators, procedures, state facts, and lessons, then predicts their destination from recurrence and dependence on the current state.
authors: Beining Wu; Zihao Ding; Jun Huang

name: DeskForge: Dense Supervision from Desktop Environments for Computer-Use Agents
summary: Generates dense desktop supervision by varying real application scenes and combining screenshots, accessibility trees, and window geometry.
authors: A. Said Gurbuz; Ahmed Nassar; Sunghwan Hong; Marc Pollefeys; Peter W. J. Staar

name: How To Train Your World Model: Fine-tuning vs RAG for LM-based World Modeling
summary: Compares fine-tuned, retrieval-based and hybrid language-model world models for next-observation prediction and action selection in text environments including WebShop.
authors: Dhananjay Ashok; Shantanu Agarwal; Vivek Datla; Jonathan May; Alfy Samuel

name: WebUIProof: Benchmarking WebUI Code Generators with UI-Agent Execution Harness
summary: Introduces an execution-based benchmark for generated web interfaces, with a headless-browser UI-agent harness that checks DOM interactions and functional assertions.
authors: Yun-Yun Tsai; Yuning Mao; Shiqi Wang; Junfeng Yang; Sinong Wang

name: When to Compile a Computer-Use Agent? Measuring Payback and Making Compilation Decisions for Token Efficiency
summary: Introduces PACE, a protocol and online decision rule for deciding when repeated GUI procedures are worth compiling into programs. It accounts for failed compilation attempts, measured per-use savings, uncertain reuse, and execution costs under an explicit cumulative budget.
authors: Yulong Ming; Jie Xu; Zihan Wu; Xiaohua Jia

name: WebFovea: When the Model Is Right but the Click Is Wrong -- Reliable Round Trips for Vision-Based Web Agents on Live Websites
summary: Describes WebFovea, a vision-based live-web agent whose execution loop checks action parsing, browser effects, feedback accuracy, and observation delivery. The report analyzes failures such as coordinate mismatches and silent control interactions and documents corresponding harness changes.
authors: Jiangang Han

name: Securing Computer-Use Agents Against Branch Steering Attacks
summary: Introduces STEER-Bench to study branch-steering attacks that manipulate untrusted web data toward hazardous paths already permitted by an agent’s plan. Its COBRA architecture combines trusted branching plans with advance constraints on the parameters and destinations each branch can use.
authors: Giulio Zingrillo; Hanna Foerster; Ilia Shumailov; Yiren Zhao; Robert Mullins

name: HyperBrowseComp: A Multilingual and Multimodal Stress Test for Web-Browsing Agents
summary: Introduces HyperBrowseComp, a multilingual benchmark for browsing agents that must connect evidence across open-web sources, including videos, scans, images, and maps.
authors: Alham Fikri Aji; Faiz Rizki Ramadhan; Zayd M. K. Zuhri; Seung Hun Eddie Han; Ryandito Diandaru; Qinrong Cui; Jan Christian Blaise Cruz; Badrinath Chandana; Peerawat Chomphooyod; Ahmed Attia; Jonibek Mansurov; Emilio Villa-Cueva; Canh Duong Nguyen; Imran Turganov; Minghao Wu; Peerat Limkonchotiwat; Irina Nikishina

name: Control OSWorld: An AI Control Environment for GUI Computer Use Agents
summary: Pairs OSWorld tasks with harmful side objectives to evaluate monitors that detect malicious behavior in computer-use agent trajectories.
authors: Maria Sanchez del Rio; Mikhail Terekhov

name: CUAWright: A Minimal Unified Interface for Digital Agents
summary: Studies a minimal terminal-based execution framework that lets digital agents construct tools and manage context across browser, desktop, and CAD tasks.
authors: Yadong Lu; Theodore Lee; Yifei Li; Lawrence Keunho Jang; Tianci Xue; Yu Su; Huan Sun; Ahmed Hassan Awadallah

name: MedImageOSWorld: Benchmarking GUI Agents for Medical Image Consoles
summary: Evaluates GUI agents in simulated medical-imaging consoles, separately checking workflow completion and acquisition outcomes against hidden anatomical targets.
authors: Ziyang Long; Xinqi Li; Lujing Xing; Hsin-Jung Yang

name: Recurrent Latent Visual Search for GUI Grounding
summary: Introduces ReLaViS, which performs recurrent visual search inside a grounding model by repeatedly querying screenshot tokens and feeding the resulting spatial evidence back into the model. Coarse-to-fine supervision is constructed from existing interface-element annotations.
authors: Kaiyu Wu; Beichen Zheng; Weiyao Huang; Keze Wang

name: TeleTune: Evolving Agent Skills From Offline Telemetry
summary: Introduces TeleTune, which edits a textual skill library using held-out action prediction on offline software-use logs with missing goals or interleaved tasks. The learned workflows also guide retrieval of demonstrations for subsequent web-agent execution.
authors: Justin Chih-Yao Chen; Elias Stengel-Eskin; Yan Chen; Pol Llado; Scott Counts; Mohit Bansal; Benjamin Van Durme; Harsh Jhamtani; Gaurav Verma

name: Imagine to Act: High-Fidelity Data Synthesis via Image Editing World Model for Scalable GUI Agent Training
summary: Introduces Infinite-Dreamer, which learns action-conditioned screenshot editing from structured descriptions of GUI changes and uses it to synthesize robustness examples and multi-step trajectories. The synthetic data trains a mobile GUI agent evaluated on AndroidWorld, MobileWorld, and AndroidControl-Curated.
authors: Yongxin Ning; Runliang Niu; Qianli Xing; Zhiyi Duan; Qingzu He; Pan Wang; Qi Wang

name: CLIFT: Conformal Self-Verification for Web Agent Training and Test-Time Scaling
summary: Introduces CLIFT, which certifies agent-generated verification signals against training-time judges and reuses them for per-step rewards and trajectory selection. At inference, a frozen question bank helps compare candidate web rollouts without querying an external judge.
authors: Yifan Zhang; Yutong Dai; Viraj Prabhu; Zhiyuan Hu; Ran Xu; Zeyuan Chen

name: DIBench: Benchmarking Decision Integrity of GUI-based Mobile Agents Under Deceptive Injections
summary: Evaluates whether deceptive UI content steers mobile agents away from instruction-consistent choices, using paired benign and injected decision states and decision-integrity metrics.
authors: Li Hu; Kanghua Mo; Yingbin Jin; Qingqing Ye; Haibo Hu

name: AMBER: Training Long-Horizon Web Agents through Append-Only Memory
summary: Introduces AMBER, an append-only memory framework in which a web agent learns to reason, act, and retain evidence using outcome-reward reinforcement learning. It studies whether preserving entries avoids the loss of facts and corrective feedback seen with rewritten memory.
authors: Chinmay Savadikar; Zhaoyu Zhang; Mingyu Zhao; Shuang Xie; Han Li; Tianfu Wu; Lingyun Wang

name: PlaySuite: A Large-Scale Benchmark for Interactive Visual Intelligence
summary: Introduces PlaySuite, a closed-loop video-game benchmark that evaluates interactive visual agents, including computer-use agents, over extended play.
authors: Dheeraj Varghese; Anna Vettoruzzo; Walter Simoncini; Michelle Lorena Acevedo Callejas; Mohammad Mahdi Derakhshani; Kristof Meding; Joaquin Vanschoren; Cees G. M. Snoek

name: Decoupling What from Where: How Should a Small GUI Grounding Model Receive the Action Type?
summary: Compares ways to condition a small GUI grounding model on action type under matched training conditions on Android in the Wild. The study traces apparent gains to a coordinate-serialization choice and reports limited evidence that the gains persist with predicted action types.
authors: Aadi Chauhan; Arthur Ilyasov

name: Can Agents Work for Everyone? Cross-User Reliability for Mobile GUI Agents in Personalized User Interfaces
summary: Introduces PAIR for controlled evaluation of mobile GUI agents across user-conditioned application states and RePAIR for training from cross-user subgoal outcomes. The study examines failures when personalized interfaces change which items an agent must identify.
authors: Yeji Park; Jaeyun Shim; Taesik Gong

name: nanoMuse: An Open-Source Personal Agent for Every Device You Own
summary: Presents nanoMuse, an open-source personal agent designed to act on phone and computer screens, with a shared conversation, action-checking Sentinel, and readable file memory.
authors: Guangyi Liu; Yong Liu; Jiangning Zhang

name: AdvSim2Real : Training Web Agents Against Adaptive Prompt Injection in a Web World Model
summary: Presents AdvSim2Real, which jointly adapts web-task curricula, prompt-injection adversaries, and agent policies inside a frozen web world model. It evaluates robustness against an unseen adversary and transfer from simulated interaction to a real browser.
authors: Sarim Hashmi; Mukul Ranjan; Kshitij Mishra; Mikhail Kuznetsov; Praneeth Vepakomma; Nils Lukas

name: Adversarial Images Hijack Web Agents from Visual Grounding to Browser Execution
summary: Introduces WebMirage, a visual red-teaming framework that models webpage element competition and action post-processing to test whether manipulated grounding decisions lead to executed browser actions.
authors: Wanjing Han; Levi Taiji Li; Mu Zhang; Yue Jiang; Guanhong Tao

name: Secure-CUA: Controlling Untrusted Influence in Computer-Use Agents
summary: Proposes Secure-CUA, which commits to per-action transactions before reading untrusted page content and separates content queries from GUI target selection. The paper formalizes its protection assumptions and evaluates benign task utility on WebArena.
authors: Sarthak Choudhary; Mihai Christodorescu; Ashish Hooda; Somesh Jha; Tongxin Li; Damien Octeau

name: AgentTime: Can Agents Estimate and Control Their Own Runtime?
summary: Evaluates duration following, runtime forecasts and elapsed-time estimates in native agent harnesses, including OSWorld desktop tasks, with external timers, native graders and work-versus-wait analysis.
authors: Michael Ofengenden; Maksym Andriushchenko

name: AgentHorizon: Evaluating Agentic Judges for Long-Horizon Computer-Use Tasks
summary: Introduces AgentHorizon, a benchmark for judging long computer-use trajectories using closely related instructions paired with recorded actions and screenshots. It tests whether judges can detect constraint violations and distinguish successful tasks from similar but incompatible requests.
authors: Xing Han Lù; Dheeraj Vattikonda; Sina Hajimiri; Fatemeh Pesaran Zadeh; Parishad BehnamGhader; Ghazwa Darwiche; Amirhossein Kazemnejad; Christopher Pal; Alexandre Drouin; Siva Reddy

name: Harness Evolution Hits a Ceiling: When Weight Training Should Begin
summary: Studies when to improve an LLM agent's runtime harness or train its weights by classifying failed trajectories; WebArena-Lite supplies a web-task transfer test.
authors: Yuan Tian; Bing Hu; Hao Wang; Binghang Lu; Fang Wu

name: DeltaReplay: Task-Relative Memory Reuse for Mobile GUI Agents
summary: Introduces DeltaReplay, which stores mobile GUI trajectories as transition graphs and decides at each step whether to reuse an action, substitute task-specific parameters, or defer to the base agent. This supports reuse of partially matching experiences without rewriting stored memory.
authors: Yudong Bai; Yihong Chen; Quanming Yao; Yaqing Wang

name: Right Screen, Wrong Transition: World Models as Verifiers for GUI Agents
summary: Presents LGWM, a decoder-free GUI world model that predicts the next screen representation from an action and compares it with the observed state to verify transitions. Its paired diagnostic separates legitimate and hijacked transitions that lead to the same credential screen.
authors: Jiaming Zhang; Xuan Wang; Fuyao Zhang; Yang Cao; Lingjuan Lyu; Wei Yang Bryan Lim

name: Can LLMs Fix It Without Code? Toward Automated Verification of No-Code Bug Fixes
summary: Tests natural-language no-code fixes through GUI execution in Linux Brave. Scripted fixed/buggy-state gates and issue-specific checkers distinguish fix outcomes from the executor's completion claims.
authors: Utku Boran Torun; Veli Karakaya; Eray Tüzün

name: SoftwareGym: Scaling Computer-Use Agent Training with Diverse Synthesized Software Environments
summary: Introduces SoftwareGym, a pipeline that synthesizes runnable GUI applications and iteratively repairs them using execution checks. It also provides a task benchmark and studies whether training on synthesized application trajectories transfers to other computer-use environments.
authors: Tian Jin; Wenhao Wang; Jing Kang; Haoting Shi; Rui Ye; Yijun Lu; Siheng Chen

name: When Charts Deceive Web Agents: A Paired Benchmark for Misleading Visualization-Grounded Tasks
summary: Introduces MisVisAgentBench, a paired executable benchmark that changes chart evidence while holding web tasks fixed, to trace how misleading visualizations affect agent decisions and downstream actions.
authors: Yisheng Li; Dongming Han; Hongkun Pan; Bingcheng Mao; Zijian Wang; Yunlong Mao; Wei Tong; Sheng Zhong

name: CaptchaAgent: Verifiable Visual Reasoning for CAPTCHA Solving
summary: Presents CaptchaAgent, which builds an explicit visual representation of objects and relations, refines ambiguous regions, and checks counterfactual consistency before acting on interactive CAPTCHAs.
authors: Shangquan Sun; Ruoyu Chen; Zhirui Liu; Xiang Liu; Chenghao Qian; Wenqi Ren; Xiaochun Cao

name: Work2Skill: Capturing Human GUI Experience for Reusable Agent Skill Induction
summary: Aligns human screen recordings, input events, and accessibility information to derive reusable workflow skills from desktop demonstrations.
authors: Yuqi Huang; Hui Li; Yifei Cao; Zikun Cai; Tianci Xie; Yangfan Gao; Pinxue Guo; Chaoyun Zhang; Bingxuan Li; Rui Zheng; Hang Yan; Ning Liao

name: When Faster Decisions Do Not Make Better Agents: An Empirical Study of Jev in Agent Workflows
summary: Evaluates Jev as a bounded action selector inside three AndroidWorld agents and two text-based ALFWorld agents, separating decision savings from task success, recovery and resources per delivered outcome.
authors: Yuchen Ling; Shengcheng Yu; Zhenyu Chen; Chunrong Fang

name: ConClick: Element-Wise Contrastive Learning Improves GUI Grounding
summary: Analyzes recurring distractor clicks in GUI grounding and introduces ConClick, a contrastive training method built from target–distractor pairs. Its ReClick inference procedure revisits candidate regions and compares competing predictions.
authors: Ruotian Zhang; Yuhui Zhang; Junzhe Huang; Yu Xin; Hehe Fan; Xiaoxiao Sun

name: Web$hell: A Unified Interface for Agentic Web Access
summary: Introduces Web$hell, an interface that compiles live pages into persistent information and action objects so agents can gather evidence, navigate websites, and reuse acquired content through shared operations.
authors: Sunghwan Kim; Deogyong Kim; Sangam Lee; Donguk Kwon; Dongha Lee

name: A Baseline Assessment for the Agentic Web Technology Stack
summary: Presents MASTIF, a framework for comparing combinations of agent models, protocols, and implementation frameworks on web tasks, with an initial assessment using 300 Mind2Web tasks.
authors: Vagner Figueredo de Santana; Diogo Cortiz

name: OpenMobile-2: Building Versatile Mobile Agents with Scalable Environments and App-Native Tools
summary: Introduces OpenMobile-2, combining simulated mobile apps, emulator tasks, released training data, and policies that can alternate GUI interaction with app-native tools.
authors: Chenyang Yan; Yingying Zhang; Kanzhi Cheng; Qiushi Sun; Zhengyuan Pan; Zheng Ma; Hang Yan; Yian Wang; Nuo Chen; Jialin Cao; Xingdong Gong; Wenpo Song; Han Chen; Zichen Ding; Fangzhi Xu; Shujian Huang; Xinyu Dai; Yichen Liu; Tiankuo Yao; Bo Wang; Ben Kao; Jianbing Zhang; Lewei Lu; Dahua Lin

name: Latent World Action Model for GUI Agents
summary: Replaces future-screenshot generation with a shared latent representation for GUI action selection and action-conditioned transition prediction. An action-aware contrastive objective encourages the transition representation to retain discriminative action-induced changes.
authors: Seungjun Yu; Hojun Choi; Seojeong Park; Jaeyo Shin; Hyunjung Shim

name: The Agent Clicks Approve: Injected Page Text Makes Browser Agents Authorize Access the Task Never Named
summary: Studies prompt-injected account-access approvals in browser agents and proposes a service-side authority envelope that checks authorization requests against the user task before allowing them to complete.
authors: Md Imran Hossen

name: From Observations to Authorized Actions: Measuring Source Information in Android Agents
summary: Measures source-attribution limits in Android accessibility and separately tests application-history and selected-WebView-object checks for authorizing AppFunctions actions.
authors: Hyobin Ahn; Dongjae Lee

name: Visible but Not Avoided: State-Dependent Re-Proposal of Rejected Candidates in Catalog-Based LLM Optimization Loops
summary: Studies repeated rejected edits while optimizing a screenshot-only GUI agent, contrasting static probes with reached loop states and testing how rejection wording changes subsequent edit proposals.
authors: Jianlin Chen; Wenhui Chen; Chi Man Vong

name: A Decade in a Day: Synthesizing Agent-Native Interfaces from Human-Oriented Software Evolution
summary: Introduces DeskIF-Bench to study how desktop application interfaces affect agents, and ANIS to synthesize interfaces from installed application capabilities.
authors: Alan Wu; Wei Tao; Yiwen Guo

name: Seg2Click: Learning Pixel-Level Action Masks for GUI Visual Grounding
summary: Recasts GUI grounding as predicting a mask of valid click locations from bounding-box supervision, then derives a click point with a deterministic selection rule.
authors: Jingchao Wang; Dingjiang Huang

name: HyWe: Unifying Search and Operation for Real-World Hybrid Web Tasks
summary: Introduces HyWe, which switches between information search and browser operation within one trajectory, alongside a demonstration pipeline and a benchmark of hybrid web tasks.
authors: Zijian Cai; Haowei Liu; Kailai Chen; Lin Peng; Cong Wan; Ziqi Zhang; Chunfeng Yuan; Bing Li; Weiming Hu; Haiyang Xu

name: EvoWeb: A Benchmark for Coding Agents on Evolving Web Applications
summary: Introduces EvoWeb, a benchmark for coding agents that extend web applications through dependent requests; a multimodal web agent checks each version in a live browser.
authors: David Nukrai; Bar Alon; Nativ Levy; Ido Andrew Atad; Ido Cohen; Itamar Zimerman; Lior Wolf; Eli David; Ilan Naiman

name: Learn from Move: the Next Step for GUI Agents
summary: Introduces LatentGUIWorld to test learning interface semantics and dynamics through interaction, and studies finer movement actions with intermediate visual feedback and exploration demonstrations.
authors: Jiahao Lu; Yize Shen; Chuanyuan Tan; Mianqiu Huang; Shicheng Fang; Xinchi Chen; Yining Zheng; Yuxin Wang; Xipeng Qiu

name: PrivacyGuard: Source-Linked Sanitization and Locally Resolvable PII References for Cloud GUI Agents
summary: Introduces PrivacyGuard, which sanitizes source-linked personal information and maintains locally resolvable references across mobile-agent turns to reduce exposure to remote planners.
authors: Zian Yuan; Wei Li

name: Glasseek: A Transparent Recipe for Training and Trustworthy Evaluation of DeepSearch Agents
summary: Introduces Glasseek, a framework for deep-search agents that explore the open web, with trajectory construction, training across context compression, and a test-set leakage audit.
authors: Cong Pang; Jiaqi Su; Chengrui Wu; Kuihao Yan; Tianrui Zhang; Zixuan Qiu; Chao Lin; Zixiu Lin; Zixuan Chen; Zelin Xiao; Tiankuo Yao; Jiawei Hong; Zixuan Chen; Dan Xu; Lewei Lu; Wenjie Wang; Xin Lou

name: BrowseSafe++: Benchmarking Prompt Injection Detection Across Web Contexts, Languages, and Browser Views
summary: Extends BrowseSafe with paired attacked and clean webpages in several representations, and studies text and screenshot detectors plus feedback-adapted prompt injections.
authors: Yuetian Chen; Kaiyuan Zhang; Yuntao Du; Thomas Li; Mark Tenenholtz; Kyle Polley; Jerry Ma; Denis Yarats; Ninghui Li

name: Adaptive-Group Process Rewards for GUI Agents
summary: Groups GUI trajectories by subgoal and combines action-level and group-level assessments into intermediate rewards for training agents with sparse task outcomes.
authors: Zirui Shang; Yang Liu; Xin Shu; Zhi Gao; Xinxiao Wu; Lifeng Fan

name: MHVF: Training-Free GUI Grounding via Verification-Guided Multi-Hypothesis Search
summary: Introduces MHVF, a training-free grounding method that explores several candidate screen regions, verifies them in local views, and uses those checks to guide further search.
authors: Minghua Chen; Xingming Liao; Weiqiang Zhong; Zhuowei Wang

name: Interaction-as-a-Judge
summary: Uses computer-use agents to interact with generated applications, studying whether interaction improves preference judging, requirement checks, and feedback for application generation.
authors: Wayne Chi; I-Hung Hsu; Li Chen; Wei-Lin Chiang; Ion Stoica; Anastasios Nikolas Angelopoulos; Ameet Talwalkar; Chris Donahue; Cho-Jui Hsieh

name: Learning How to Remember: Memory Modality Selection for GUI Agents
summary: Introduces SwitchMem, which chooses a textual or visual representation of retrieved experience at each GUI interaction step.
authors: Taeyun Roh; Suhyeong Park; Gijin Kim; Wonjune Jang; Jaewoo Kang

name: WorkRover: Scaling Long-Horizon Cowork Agent Training Via Recursive Environment Evolution
summary: Synthesizes resettable workspaces with files, application observations and skills; repairs environment incompatibilities and trains long-task agents using verifier-linked turn credit.
authors: Hang He; Linting Wang; Guanming Liu; Bo Mao; Jinxiu Liu; Yiran Suo; Maosen Zhou; Zhiheng Xi; Guanting Dong; Zhou Shao; Rui Zheng; Jie Zhou; Chengcheng Wan; Tao Gui; Qi Zhang; Xipeng Qiu; Xuanjing Huang
topics: data-generation; long-horizon; evaluation; reward-models; reinforcement-learning; workflow

name: Towards Safe Autonomy for Computer Use
summary: Presents SA-CUA, separating trusted and untrusted visual content using accessibility-derived masking rules and a controlled channel for verifying information before endorsement.
authors: Dominik Seip; Bartol Markovinović; Matthias Hein

name: Reading Right, Acting Wrong: Diagnosing Decision Failures of System One Models in Agent Loops
summary: Pairs factual probes with next-action choices on frozen agent traces, including Mind2Web, to diagnose reading-decision gaps without closed-loop execution.
authors: Yubo Li; Ramayya Krishnan; Rema Padman

name: Pack Light, CarryOn: Building Object-Oriented Context for Long-Horizon Agents
summary: Introduces CarryOn, which maintains evidence-linked task objects and remaining-work context across history compression, with evaluations on desktop tasks and web research.
authors: Yuchen Lu; Julian McAuley; Lei Zhang

name: GroundGUI: GUI Grounding by High-Quality Data and Distillation-to-Reinforcement Learning
summary: Introduces ScreenRef screenshot grounding data and a training sequence from supervised learning through teacher-guided distillation to reinforcement learning for GroundGUI-8B.
authors: Qingsong Xie; Jiahao Tian; Jiacheng Tang; Zhifeng Li; Madalina Ciobanu; Navan Preet Singh; Qingqing Mao; Ritankar Das

name: CLASHarness: Benchmarking Multi-Agent Conflict in Computer Use via a Controllable and Verifiable Generation Pipeline
summary: Introduces CLASHarness, generating verifiable computer-use tasks with conflicting agent reports, shared-state constraints, and coordination requirements to evaluate conflict detection and resolution.
authors: Yuxiang Lai; Jike Zhong; Chengzhi Liu; Ming Li; Haonan Wang; Xiaofeng Yang; Liang Zhao; Youbao Tang; Ruixi Fan

name: Seeing, Maintaining, and Learning: The Evolution of Multimodal Agent Memory
summary: Surveys multimodal memory using representation and management axes, distinguishing fixed-policy updates from policy evolution and comparing GUI memory evaluation with other modalities.
authors: Minghao Guo; Qingyue Jiao; Xiujin Liu; Jianhong Pang; Ruimeng Yang; Naihao Xu; Liwei Che; Haochen Xue; Ziqi Wang; Xinying Cai; Jiaxuan Luo; Jiaxin Deng; Xuesong Ye; Jintao Qu; Wenyao Gao; Jingwen Gu; Chenyang Zhao; Shichun Liu; Guibin Zhang; Zefang Liu; Siyin Wang; Wujiang Xu; Danrui Li; Zeru Shi; Woongyeong Yeo; Shuang Liu; Wei-Chieh Huang; Weizhi Zhang; Tianyu Yang; Kangsan Kim; Yebowen Hu; Bowen Wen; Bowen Jiang; Haohao Su; Ming Yin; Sheldon Yu; Mian Zhang; Yuyan Chen; Hanrong Zhang; Kai Mei; Zihao Zhang; Mingyu Jin; Xi Zhu; Hengyi Wang; Tianxin Wei; Linyong Nan; Zhenwen Liang; Zhendong Chu; Ziqi Huang; Yongye Su; Sixun Dong; Shujian Liu; Kaiqu Liang; Jiaojiao Han; Zhaoye Fei; Kun Wang; Shihan Dou; Zhichun Guo; Xingjian Diao; Zeqi Gu; Heng Wang; Tao Feng; Cheng Qian; Hamid Palangi; Silei Xu; Xi Yun; Yi Zhu; Shilong Liu; Qingsong Wen; Sung Ju Hwang; Zuxuan Wu; Yu-Gang Jiang; Yiyu Shi; Dimitris N. Metaxas; Jiaxuan You; Julian McAuley; Mengdi Wang; Jiawei Han; Philip S. Yu; Ziyi Ye

authors: Pranjal Aggarwal; Sean Welleck
